A process shutdown occurred minutes after this impact, and although the causal link has not yet been fully established, the timing suggests the crane event may have contributed to or triggered the shutdown.

Contractor carrying out repairs on the Scale Inhibitor Injection system, the system was understood to have been depressurised. As the contractor started to release an end cap, the cap was projected downwards under pressure. The cap went directly downwards into a section of plant close to a walkway. This could have had potential to impact personnel.

Flex Joint strikes handrail creating 2 Dropped Objects. During the removal of the Flex Joint from the Riser Feeding Machine (RFM) using the starboard crane, the aft sling of the Flex Joint became hung up on the RFM bucket. As the lift continued, the sling suddenly released, causing the Flex Joint to swing unexpectedly. The uncontrolled movement resulted in the Flex Joint striking and damaging the RFM track and the associated emergency-stop device. The Flex Joint then continued its swing path until coming to rest against the starboard-side handrail. The impact dislodged two sections of the handrail, weighing 2.4 kg and 4.6 kg, corresponding to 377 Joules and 722 Joules of potential energy respectively. Both handrail sections fell approximately 16 metres to the Riser Deck below.

Operator observed a concrete block on the tray of a flatbed truck and attempted to pick it up with the Front-end Loader tynes (pallet forks). The operator misjudged the fork tyne pockets of the pallet the concrete block was sitting on and inadvertently pushed the concrete block off the side of the flatbed truck. The concrete block weighed ~1.3 tonne and fell ~1.4m before rolling onto its side and coming to rest on the ground near a container on the opposite side of the flatbed truck.

During pallet racking activities in the warehouse, a forklift was in the process of lifting a pallet to the third shelf. The load backrest of the forklift inadvertently contacted another pallet directly above (load approximately 240kg) stored on the fourth shelf which dislodged and fell approximately 5.6m to grade. No personnel were injured. There was one nearby person 7 meters away.

IP1 observed visible bulging of a drain hose and proceeded to disconnect it. Although the associated compressor had been isolated, the hose remained connected to the main drainage manifold, which was linked to 24 compressors. The hose remained pressurized, and upon disconnection it struck the IP1 on the left hand and lower leg, and subsequently impacting IP2's hand as they attempted to assist. As a result, IP1 and IP2 were injured.

Whilst departing the north berth of the supply base wharf, the contractor inspection maintenance repair vessel began moving starboard and aft whilst the forward fender was being lifted and recovered using the vessel's crane.

A crew member stepped out of a cherry picker while connecting a hydraulic hose to the Annular BOP, lost balance, and fell onto the cellar-pit grating. Subsequent hospital evaluation confirmed a left zygomatic bone fracture.
2-7/8" tubing was released from the lifting cap and hit the back of the right shoulder.

During hot work activities to replace process lines, the flange of a service water line was broken. This resulted in a release of water followed by a hydrocarbon/water emulsion. There was no CO/LEL detected and the material was removed by flushing with service water. Despite a very minor, intermittent liquid release (droplets) from the open line, work activities continued to cut an upstream service water line. About 10-15 minutes later, a fire ignited from the open process nozzle.
Fly jib on mobile crane fell to the floor.

Whilst lifting a pennant on deck as part of a lifting activity (~56.2m length, static weight 16.2 mT), a tagline was in a basket arrangement around the rigging to provide stability. The tagline had a single wrap on the generator lifting frame, used as an anchor point. During the lift, the involved person who had been on deck dogging the load in a safe location, moved to a location positioned between the generator and stored deck boards. As the generator tilted, it trapped the involved person against a stack of wooden deck boards. The involved person received an injury that required Medevac to an onshore medical facility for further treatment.
Employee fell into well cellar. Loose grating led to a fall into the cellar.
Cut through live supply line. Employee cut into a cable with 400V ac current.

When filling a mud tank with brine to prepare for cleaning of the tank, the transfer hose became dislodged, fell towards the ground (2.6m) and began to whip. The hose struck the pump operator's leg, who suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon. The operator required surgery, classifying this as a Lost Work Day Case under IOGP guidelines. The incident is considered high potential, as the heavy hose coupling could have caused a fatality if it struck the head of the injured person when it fell.

On 8 October 2025 on an offshore rig, a lifting operation was underway to land an 11.8 m, 2.67 ton bottom hole assembly (BHA) into a storage basket on the riser deck. During the final positioning, the BHA made a sudden uncontrolled movement. The forward end either contacted the basket edge, rotating the load toward the injured person, or the crane made an unintended movement. The injured person was positioned in a narrow space between riser guide posts with no escape route available. He had earlier climbed onto adjacent baskets and manually guided the load several times to open covers in the inner basket. The BHA struck him in the chest and compressed him against another basket. Emergency response was immediate, and medical evacuation was carried out via search and rescue (SAR) helicopter. The investigation identified multiple human, organisational, technical, and task-related contributors including lack of hands-free lifting, trainee crane operator without supervision, congested deck layout, communication challenges, inadequate planning, and procedural non-compliance.

An operator was removing a grating panel with manual handling hooks on the weather deck. During the operation, the grating unhooked from the manual handling tools and fell through the opening, hit a cable gate before landing on the underlying deck, approximately 10 meters below. The grating measures 1x1 meter and weighs 52,4 kg which gives a kinetic energy of 5149, 44 Joules. No one was injured, but under slightly changed circumstances people could have been in the line of fire as the deck was not cordoned off and there was a work team close to the area where it dropped.
A worker was seriously injured when he fell from a height of 4.4 metres.
Sucker rod broke consequently elevator dropped. Overpull due to wax caused the sucker rod to break, impact ejected the elevator out of the hook.

During platform crane lifting operations to land a container on the main deck North landing, the IP sustained a crush/impact injury to shoulder/ribs. The crane and container were made safe and the individual treated by platform advanced first aider followed by coastguard medevac for further assessment.
Loss of Primary Containment - Methanol Release.
Jack failed, with load moving towards personnel. No injuries however fatality as worst case potential outcome.
Scaffold pole dropped to deck during handling operations. No injuries however dropped object calculator indicates fatality as worst case potential outcome.
Scaffold pole dropped to deck during handling operations. No injuries however dropped object calculator indicates fatality as worst case potential outcome.

A forklift driver's ankle was struck by a spreader bar during offloading from a truck at the logistics base. There were no lifting pockets welded onto the bar. In past lifting operations, the spreader bar had been placed on wooden blocks on the truck bed and lifted directly on the forks of a forklift. This time the wooden blocks were not in place. The truck driver and the forklift driver decided to lift the spreader bar off the truck by hooking hoisting slings attached to the spreader bar and to the forklift forks, crossing them to reduce the length of the slings. During hoisting, the spreader bar rotated and swung into the forklift cabin, hitting the driver's ankle. The forklift cabin door had been left open to improve communication between the drivers.

On an offshore drilling rig, on 1 September 2025, personnel and marine crew were installing handrails on top of a unit on the main deck. Handrail sections (60-90 kg) were lifted by deck crane to the top of the unit, where an operator worked at height to receive and install them, using fall-arrest equipment. The operator initially attached his lanyard to the stairs, then to handrail, and later to another section to reach the final corner section. To fit the last section, he had to lift and adjust some of the handrail. The locking pins were weakly retained and the chain/carabiner secondary securing arrangement did not prevent them from sliding out. The section of the handrail tilted and fell, pulling the operator with it. He fell approximately 4.3 m to deck, landing partly on the fallen handrail. The incident resulted in an LTI and a dropped object with calculated energy of 2733 J, with assessed potential for a single fatality.

In connection with a pigging operation on an offshore installation, several pigs weighing 35 - 40 kg were lowered from a scaffold using rope, as the pig receiver was placed 5m above the turret deck. When the last pig was being lowered, the knot loosened, and the pig fell onto the turret deck and then bounced outside the barrier and down onto the tank deck. No one was injured and there was no significant material damage.

Collision between northern crane and derrick resulting in falling objects. Three objects fell after the north crane collided with the derrick. The crane operator had been planning to perform lubrication of the slewing ring with the logistics discipline responsible for some time, but this was changed to the crane operator bringing along a deck operator who was being trained as a crane-operator. A helicopter was on its way to the platform, and they had about 25 minutes to finish before the helicopter arrived. It was decided that the crane operator was to perform the lubrication in the crane pedestal while the deck operator operated the crane. The crane was lifted and swung out over the sea. The crane operator reminded to "elevate the crane-boom" to avoid the derrick and then went down into the pedestal. The deck operator elevated the boom and swung the crane towards the platform. After a brief stop to change the lubrication cartridge, the crane was topped up a little more before it swung further towards the derrick. The deck operator believed the boom was topped up enough. The walkway and the spotlight mounted on the right side of the boom were driven into the upper corner of the wind wall high up in the derrick. At the same time, the crane was lifted somewhat and detached from the tower. The crane shook, and the deck operator observed an object fall into an area where personnel were normally present. After receiving information about what had happened over the radio, the crane operator came to the cabin, took over, and lowered the crane into the cradle. The logistics discipline responsible heard what was being said on the radio, responded, and found the spotlight in a pallet with wooden lids in the moonpool area. A section of weather protection from the derrick was found a few minutes later, and a bracket for securing electrical cables was found three days later on a walkway one level above the moonpool area.

Two personnel experienced symptoms of severe oxygen deficiency during inspection work, but managed to self-evacuate safely. Subsequent measurements confirmed low oxygen levels inside the enclosure, linked to nitrogen ingress from the turbine seal system combined with a lack of ventilation.

During preparations for installing a 20'' sealing ring on the platform on 2 July 2025, a technician tested the ring for fit before the lift operation. The 7.1 kg ring slipped from the technician's hands and fell 6.35 meters to the deck below, landing approximately two meters from a mechanic who was grinding at deck level. The ring then bounced and struck the mechanic on the arm. The mechanic received a first-aid level impact with no observable injury. The event had a severe potential for fatality due to the weight and fall height. The ring had been brought into the elevated work area earlier than planned, the area was insufficiently barricaded, and the test occurred without notification to the crew below. Multiple procedural, communication and barrier-management weaknesses contributed.

Gangway disconnect during personnel transfer. • Equipment.
• Inadequate control over maintenance.

During the night shift, the crew attempted to release an anchor latch tool from a permanent packer using a straight pull of 60 klbs (including 55 klbs string weight) without success. Following contractors' procedures, the string was tensioned with 5 klbs over string weight and rotated manually, but no movement was observed. Based on contractors' instructions, power tongs were partially used due to the absence of a power swivel on site. During the sixth right-hand turn with a 5 klbs overpull, the 2-7/8" tubing coupling connected to the safety valve backed off and fell approximately 21 ft onto the rig floor, then a further 14 ft to the ground. At the same time, the tubing string settled approximately 6 ft into the packer. The combined weight of the coupling and safety valve was 36.5 kg.

While dismantling a scaffold, a contractor accidentally dropped a scaffold board. The board struck a 0.5-inch, 32-bar pressurized tube, causing physical damage to the tube and resulting in a gas leak.

During maintenance activities, an electrical arc occurred in Switch Rack 6 LV, resulting in electrical burns to two electrical technicians. The injured personnel received immediate evacuation to the clinic for initial medical attention before being transferred to the Hospital for further treatment.

A contractor working in the Telecoms room at Central Control Building was found removing a light fixture from the ceiling without ensuring the power was fully isolated. The light was part of an energized circuit, switched off only at the local lighting switch. With the light removed, the exposed flex had bare copper ends, live and hanging from the ceiling. The worker, on metal steps, was at risk of electrocution if someone had entered and switched on the lights

Observed that a Contractor Scaffolder working at 12m height on a Piperack without using his fall protection, standing on the hanging scaffold platform without using his double lanyards attached to a suitable anchor point and there was no handrail in place for fall prevention.
A Contractor scaffolder was dismantling a scaffold by removing a 3m high scaffold standard at a height of 11.5m, without using lanyards and passing the scaffold standard to a colleague below.

A forklift operator was pulling a service hose from the backyard to the rig location, the operator raised the boom to a higher position. During this operation, the boom came into contact with a deadline data cable positioned approximately 5 meters high on overhead line stands. As a result, the cable fell and sustained minor damage. There were no injuries or harm to personnel

During space-out of the traveling block to function-test the power tong, the Driller hoisted the traveling block with the working string. When the string was about 2 meters above the rig floor, the Driller applied the brake. At that moment, the traveling block and working string suddenly moved down to the rig floor. Work string landed on the slip and travelling block stopped moving where the brake was activated.

A contractor mechanical field service representative and mechanical team had disconnected the export gas compressor gas turbine's primary and secondary flexible fuel gas hoses. After disconnecting the hoses, the contractor field service representative was on the back side of the gas turbine while the mechanical technicians were on the front side. While lying beneath the gas turbine to check the water wash drain tube under the gas turbine, pressure was released, causing the loose hoses to swing.
Company pickup truck collided with a concrete barrier at a diversion point.

A steel structure crew was modifying a permanent grating platform handrail when a crowbar (weight approximately 0.72kg) fell from the platform (height 20 metres) and landed on the ground below in an unbarricaded area. No person injury occurred or was reported.

A gate door (two sections) of the Blasting Shop toppled over due to strong winds (approximately 16m/s). Each door section measures 7.5m x 4m and weighs approx. 425kg. They landed on the ground and came to rest on a pipe stand, resulting in damage to the cladding and frame. The incident occurred next to a pedestrian walkway, but no personnel were in the vicinity at the time. No personal Injury was reported

A trailer driver was transporting six concrete barriers (3.5t each) on a flatbed trailer. The barriers were stacked in two rows (three in each row), with one cargo lashing belt securing two concrete barriers each. While the trailer was travelling on the bumpy road, the driver noticed that one of the lashing belts securing the rear concrete barriers had broken, causing the load to shift slightly towards the edge of the trailer. He pulled over to address the situation. Fortunately, no injuries or damage occurred.
During welding activities, the fire watch for the naked flame activity received an electrical shock when attempting to shift an electrical welding rod oven.

A telehandler operator was moving a 714kg pipe spool when he observed a trailer blocking his access. The operator pulled the telehandler over to the side waiting for the trailer to move away. When the trailer moved, the operator started to reverse the telehandler. After reversing approximately 2 metres, the front right tyre of the telehandler failed and exploded. The release of pressure ejected the tyre 7 metres away from the telehandler. The primary locking rim (weight 19.3kg) and the secondary locking rim (weight 2.3kg) were ejected from the split rim, causing the primary locking rim to land 50 metres away and the secondary locking rim to land 70 metres away. No injuries were reported. The Flagman and Rigger were positioned behind the telehandler approximately 5 metres away.

An 800-ton crawler crane and a 280-ton crawler crane had concluded lifting operations and were idle. A civil crew requested the 800-ton crane operator to reposition the hook so they could avoid working under it. While slewing, the boom tip section of the 800-ton crawler crane contacted the wire rope of the stationary 280-ton crawler crane. The crane was operating within a barricaded area. No visible damage was found on both crawler cranes, and there were no injuries

While a Wellhead Engineer was installing a side outlet valve at the wellhead deck, a Floor Man was preparing downhole guides on the upper deck level, but one down hole guide clamp, weighing 7 kg, slipped and dropped through open hatch and hit the right middle side of the hard hat above the brim and landed in the grating, causing the IP to fall on to the grating resulting in bruises to his right forehead and injury to his right knee.

Power cable damage during excavation. The incident resulted from inadequate excavation planning, including missing cable markers, an overly shallow trial pit that failed to expose the deeper 11 kV cable, the absence of cable detection tools, and the use of mechanical excavation where manual digging was required. These issues were compounded by missing underground service drawings and a Permit to Work issued without proper site inspection.

Workers were unloading sandbags from the bucket of a wheel loader. While unloading the sandbags, a worker's left foot was under the loader's bucket. The bucket was inadvertently lowered, resulting in a crush injury to the worker (hereinafter referred to as the injured person or IP).

On 30/04/2025, a High Potential (HIPO) occurred when a crane's counterweight of 15 tonnes fell off the trailer due to failure in the securing belt. The trailer was moving from the laydown area to the well-pad. No personnel injuries were reported.

After completing the second gyro survey, the crew began rigging down. On the platform deck, a tugger line was attached to the gyro tool as secondary retention. The tool was lifted to the rig floor using the wireline. Once above the rotary table, the wireline gooseneck was installed on top of the tool. As the tugger was spooled in to take the tool's weight, its swivel caught the gooseneck, pulling it off. The gooseneck, weighing 2.3 kg, fell approximately 50 ft from the rotary table to the platform deck.

During racking-back a 7" landing joint using the Monkey board forward pullback tugger, the line parted, causing the parted hook and line to fall from the Monkey board to the rig floor. No one was injured or struck by the dropped object. 3 crew members were in the Red Zone at the time of the Dropped Object. Hook weighed 0.75kg and dropped 83ft approx.

The rig crew were in the process of nipple down the bell nipple mandrel. While positioning the multi purpose crane for installing the bell nipple lifting slings the man basket (354kg), which was holding 2 persons, dislodged from the main structure of the crane and fell approx.16.5m to the top deck of the platform. Neither of the 2 persons fell as they were suspended by their harness and inertia reels. Both personnel were recovered in 2 minutes. One of the 2 personnel received first aid treatment for slight swelling.

During the workboat transfer operation, workboat was transferred from the laydown area to the transport vessel main deck and positioned in its transport cradle. During final positioning, the vessel could not remain steady. As a result, the workboat swung into a nearby Cargo Carrying Unit (CCU), causing damage to the hull. A crew member handling a tag line was exposed to risk and was nearly caught between the CCU and the swinging workboat.

Two project contractors were observed working outside the handrail on structural beams approximately 30 meters above sea level. They were without the required fall-prevention barriers or authorized permits. Both individuals faced an uncontrolled fall-from-height hazard, posing a significant risk where survivability is minimal and multiple fatalities could occur.

IP was working alone and attempted to disconnect a 2" airline which was pressurized. An assumption was made that line was de-pressurized without being verified - line was still connected to an air compressor. Upon release, hose kicked back striking IPs hand and helmet.

On May 20, 2025, a worker was engaged in repositioning a spec blind from the closed to the open position on the flare line, in preparation to de-isolate the unit for commissioning activities. During this activity, the worker was exposed to a gas/energy release from the down steam side of the isolated gate valve at the open flange pair. Worker required rescue from heights and was provided onsite first aid; worker was transported to a local hospital for further medical assessment where it was determined worker sustained bruised ribs and a concussion. Worker was released from hospital the same day.

During a fluid-hauling task, water transfer to a tank truck was completed and the hose was disconnected. A valve was found not fully closed, and hot fluid sprayed during subsequent valve manipulation. The job was stopped, emergency medical response was initiated, and the well/site was shut down to support response and control the release.

During offloading of a delivery of structural steel, a stacked load became unstable while the final securement strap was being removed. A beam fell from the trailer and struck a worker. Emergency response was initiated, the beam was removed from contact, and the worker was transported for medical assessment and treatment.

Crew was killing the well with Axis Reverse Unit when the Axis Pump Hand appears to have engaged valves in the incorrect order allowing pressure to exit well bore through a disconnected 2" hose at the rig floor. Pressure estimated to be 600 psi. Loose end of hose whipped and struck one individual on the top of their hard hat.

A Mechanic and an E-Tech were repairing a section of the natural gas manifold on frac pump. The employees were replacing a section on the manifold referred to as a pistol. After the repairs were made the employees opened the natural gas supply valve to supply the gas manifold on the pump. The mechanic stepped up onto a platform to open the main ball valve of the natural gas manifold to allow the pump to start burning the natural gas as fuel. As the mechanic (IP) opened the main ball valve, both employees heard a loud pop noise. The top of the low-pressure regulator (VDR) broke away from its base and struck the mechanic in the head above his right eye causing a laceration. The top of the VDR is made of aluminum and weighs approximately 1lb/~454g. The IP was evaluated at a local emergency room, and the IP received 8 sutures to close the laceration.

IP contacted by 2 3/8" joint of pipe. The team finished wireline work of setting a cast iron bridge plug, pressure tested well, ND frac valve and NU BOP. The crew then installed 2.875" elevators (2.375" and 2.875" elevators were both on the ground) and began process of picking up a single joint of 2.375" tubing. The tubing was almost vertical when it fell through the elevators, causing the pin end to land back in the pick-up/lay-down machine trough and the collar end to fall toward the off-operator side of the rig floor. The collar end of the tubing initially contacted the tong lifting cylinder, then ricocheted, hitting the floor hand in the lower-right shoulder before coming to rest across the handrails. Notifications were made, and the well was secured.
A flash fire occurred during the demolition of internal components in the first-stage knockout drum (module C2) at the facility.
While releasing the tubing hanger, after a BOP test, unknown pressure had built up below the tubing hanger assembly causing it to lift up out of the BOP stack and fall to the ground.
While changing out tong heads during an ESP install, the IP's right arm came into contact with the actuating lever, activating the tongs. IP's left forearm was struck by the rotation of the tongs.

A worker fell approximately 16 feet from an aerial work platform onto a Christmas tree cart. The incident occurred while the worker was using a rope tied to the basket to pull an umbilical and create slack for a storm loop. The rope failed under tension, releasing stored energy that transferred to the basket. This sudden release caused the basket to jolt, ejecting the worker.

While adjusting the ultra-high-pressure water blasting equipment in close proximity to normally energized cable trays, in three separate instances, two workers reported experiencing electrical shock sensations upon contacting the cable trays.

Following heavy rainfall, landslide occurred in the area behind the ten wagon-type cabins (accommodation, canteen, washing, changing, and rest facilities) located at the oil well site. A ground instability and multiple surface cracks were identified in the surrounding area. Personnel were immediately informed of the hazardous ground conditions and instructed to remain vigilant and exercise caution. As a preventive control measure, the wagon-type units were relocated to a safer area to eliminate the risk of impact from further ground movement.

Contractor personnel were performing a scheduled calibration of a flow meter in accordance with the preventive maintenance plan. During the calibration process, the technician initiated pressure stabilization by draining fluid through the designated drainage line. To enhance the drainage process, the technician also opted to use an additional line and proceeded to remove the plug at the end of that line. Upon removal of the plug, an uncontrolled release of oil containing H2S occurred. Work was stopped immediately. Workers H2S detectors activated, donned respirators and evacuated the area.

A dropped object incident occurred while lowering an overdrive with the casing joint held stationary in the elevator. The mud saver (component of overdrive) contacted top of the liner joint in the rotary, causing failure at the connection to the mandrel. The mud saver (~40 kg) fell ~14 meters to the rig floor. Two personnel were in the red zone at the time (required for the task).

During the installation of a subsea telescopic clamp on the well shaft beneath the offshore platform, the Diving Service team encountered a safety-critical situation when a support vessel unexpectedly approached the platform, despite all established safety measures being in place. The vessel's captain was promptly contacted and informed that underwater diving operations were in progress.

During the inspection of the 8-inch subsea oil and gas pipeline located between offshore platforms, diving operations were in progress and a scheduled descent from the diving vessel had commenced. Approximately 15 minutes after the diver entered the water, the vessel's mechanic reported hull damage resulting in water ingress into the engine room. The diver was immediately recovered from the water, and the vessel proceeded toward the platform, where it was safely moored at the docking bridge. Following the safe disembarkation of personnel, the damaged vessel was towed to the onshore port by an assisting tugboat.
While performing orifice change on a choke valve, the choke bean was ejected toward the operator ́s position.

Contractor personnel were working on the installation of a 12-inch spool at ground level, while it was being held in a lifting operation. For causes yet to be determined, an actuated valve (SDV) located near the installation area -resting vertically on the ground and not involved in the lifting operation - lost its vertical stability and fell, resulting in a person being crushed between the valve and the skid structure.

Crew shuttle collision during a braking manoeuvre, the shuttle initially collided with the vehicle in front, then crossed into the oncoming lane and was struck on the right side by a semi-trailer truck traveling in the opposite direction.

During the movement of the workover rig truck from one well to another, the rear tyre on one of the truck's axles completely detached, resulting in an impact with the injection line of a well, with no visible damage.

During the dismantling of scaffolding in a 45° angular configuration, assembler 01 had to apply excessive force to loosen a remaining clamp (exposed to the weather) using a ratchet wrench, causing the bolt to shear and subsequently break. With the sudden opening of the clamp, the tube (3.65 kg) slipped from his left hand, fell, and slid along the structure, traveling a lateral distance of approximately 4.5 meters, striking the back of assembler 04s helmet on the lower level, resulting in a superficial cut to the scalp.
During maintenance work at a Generation Unit, the mechanical technician suffered a fall from height, falling to a lower level from the engine access platform.

During the heating of an 18-inch pipe to remove the coating, the worker placed the torch at the entrance of the 18-inch pipe. When attempting to light the torch with a manual spark igniter, a flammable atmosphere was created, causing a flash fire that resulted in first and second-degree burns to the worker's face after being hit sideways by a flash fire in the manufacturing workshop area.

During production tubing running operations on the drilling rig, four metallic components fell from height while using the catline system.
• Objects dropped from approximately 40 m height
• 2 × 1.8 kg (≈ 706 J each)
• 2 × 10.4 kg (≈ 4,076 J each) The falling energy was sufficient to cause a fatality. No injuries occurred, but this qualifies as a High Potential Event (HIPO) due to the severe dropped-object energy.

During load handling with the crane (Knuckle Boom Crane #1), after positioning a container on the deck and removing the sling from the crane hook, while moving the boom to connect the sling to another nearby load, the tip of Knuckle Boom Crane #1 collided with the joint of the other crane (Pipe Handling Crane) located in the center of the pipe deck, causing a load cell from KBC #1 to fall onto the top of a container on the pipe deck.

On 22 March at approximately 08:45, a tool bag was lifted from the rig floor to the derrick using catline #02 during equipment mobilisation. When the bag reached the derrickman's platform level, it suddenly accelerated upward, struck the sheave, the bag handles failed, and the bag and tools fell, impacting a container on the deck below. No injuries occurred, but the dropped object had fatality potential.

On 17 November at approximately 09:40, the smoke detector in the laundry room activated after several cleaning cloths spontaneously combusted shortly after being removed from a dryer and placed on the floor. The fire brigade responded immediately and extinguished the fire using CO2 and dry powder extinguishers. No injuries or asset damage occurred, but the event had potential for a serious fire and smoke exposure.

On 27 December at approximately 07:30, cleaning cloths contaminated with cooking oil were washed and dried in the laundry. After drying, the cloths were placed on the floor inside an open bag next to other cloths. Later, all laundry ventilation, exhaust, and air-conditioning systems were switched off while the room was unattended. At approximately 13:15, the cloths began releasing smoke and an incipient fire developed. The steward used a dry chemical extinguisher and the fire brigade extinguished the fire. No injuries or damage occurred, but the event had serious fire potential.
A forklift traveling in reverse moved toward the spotter during the warehouse exit manoeuvre.
During a pull-out operation on the platform, an uncommanded movement of the vessel's aft reel occurred, exposing a worker to a potentially fatal risk.
Employee sustained burns during line tie-in operations at an oil and gas site.
One employee was hospitalized after being struck by a tire when he was airing the tire up during his pre-drive inspection.
Employee was descending a work over rig derrick via a ladder when he fell a distance. Employee suffered a lacerated spleen and fractured hip and shoulder.
Employee was burned from his knees up to his lower abdomen after removing the strainer for maintenance on the Scott Unit.
Employee was working on a fluid end expendable pump using a torque wrench when his left ring finger got caught in between and was amputated - halfway through the nailbed.
An employee was exposed to a pinch point hazard when his left thumb was caught between the ST-80 and another metal object.

Two employees of 4 Swift Service passed out in a tank that was being cleaned. Employees proceeded into a tank which had been closed, but was opened by an employee. Employees went inside to clean, but were supposed to clean the outside of the tank only. Both employees were transported to the hospital, but only one employee was admitted.

Employee was on the side of the derrick untying tubular when his fast line became caught up in his SRL. The employee was pulled away from the ladder. The SRL stopped and so did the anchor. Therefore, no fall resulted. The employee received contusions to the head, ribs, and chest area. He also suffered bruising to the brain and lungs and received six stitches to the forehead. He did not lose consciousness.
On 01/08/15, employee suffered an amputation of the left index finger while operating a mulch machine at a well site.

At the facility shop area, an employee tripped over his feet and fell on an industrial sized valve stem used in hydrofracking (a piece of sharp equipment) and lacerated his abdomen. This injury required hospitalization for two days.

Employee was working from the derrick monkey board latching and unlatching tubing. As he was unlatching the elevator that has horns and a locking mechanism, the employee's harness got caught on the horns. The horns pulled the harness and pulled him down causing small fractures in his knees that required surgery.

On January 8, 2015 at 10:15pm, an employee was cleaning/unclogging an automatic in-line cement powder sampler. He used his finger to verify there was no longer a clog and the sampler actuated amputating the tip of the third finger on the employee's left hand.

On or about January 9, 2015, an employee slipped on ice on the rig floor. He put his right hand out to break his fall. His right index finger was caught between the stump and the Kelly ripping skin off the fingertip. The employee was treated an his hand was wrapped in gauze and he returned to work. On or about January 19, 2015, he had surgery and the finger was amputated at the first joint.

On or about January 9, 2014 at about 0535 hrs an employee of Propetrol Services Inc. was repairing a pump at the Mabee 139-202 HA well site 10 miles north of Midland Texas. When he reached into the pump to repair a faulty plunger, the unit "kicked" and amputated the tip of his right middle finger. He was driven to Medical Center Hospital in Odessa Texas where the prognosis was that the flesh portion not the bone will be amputated.
Employee slipped on ice and broke femur while working on well site in the vicinity of the Anderson 1-4-H location near Williston, North Dakota.
Employee was injured when he fell 20-40 feet from an elevated man-lift.

The employee was attempting to rig a steel beam with a chain sling and overhead crane. While attempting to rig this elevated beam, it fell towards the employee. The employee tried to brace/stop the beam with his hand and the fore of the beam pushed him back, striking his face and chest as well, knocking him into another steel beam. The employee was admitted to the hospital with a broken wrist. Surgery was performed to correct the injury to the employee's wrist. The injury occurred in the Welding/Fabrication shop.
Employee was breaking a bolt with a crescent wrench and it slipped. The employee fell back and rolled onto the leg fracturing the ankle.
Employee was removing a flow line from preventer to mud tank. The flow line pinched the employee's finger between the flange and the BOP causing the amputation.
An employee slipped on a step and fell forward injuring both knees.
On January 13, 2015, the employees were in the process of changing a heater treater tube. The leaking fluid ignited causing severe burn injuries. One employee was sent to the Minnesota burn unit.

An employee was injured and admitted to the hospital due to being struck by equipment during the movement of pipe while working on a work-over rig in Northeast Colorado. The accident occurred on November 13, 2015 at approximately 1:20 pm.
An employee was making a connection with a drill fork when the speeding wrench struck the left hand smashing the middle finger on that hand.

On 1/14/2015 at approximately 11:23a.m. an employee was using a blow down system on a National 340 pump to blow out water in the hard line. Once the 4 inch suction hose was drained, the suction hose was disconnected and a cam lock was placed on the suction hose coming from the pump. The four inch butterfly valve for the suction was left open allowing air to pressure up against the cam lock cap. The employee used this system to build air and blow down the fluid in the tubing line to the tank. The employee was standing in front of the manifold and slightly to the right approximately one foot away. When the employee opened up the manifold, the cam lock cap popped free hitting him in the shin.

An employee was unjamming a stuck granulated salt spreader used on the back of a truck to salt roads. The employee reached into the impeller and chain components while the machine was running and something grabbed his right hand and amputated his right index finger past the nail bed, but before the first joint.

Frac technicians conducting monitoring operations on water levels of gauging tanks during oil and gas drilling operations are potentially overexposed to air contaminants and respiratory irritants such as chlorine, hydrogen sulfide, and benzene. Recently, an employee was admitted to the hospital for observation and treatment after suffering from an extreme coughing episode after working a monitoring shift at the worksite. A second employee was treated and released.
Employee burned by flash fire at pumping station while adjusting compressor.
Employee received an electric shock when he placed his wrench near an energized bolt on a conductor he was removing.
Employee was tightening a strap used to tie down equipment on his truck when the pry bar came out of the hole and hit him in the mouth, fracturing the maxilla bone.
Two employees were burned when a bubble tower exploded creating a flash fire during maintenance work on a well site.

Employee was taking out a 10-inch hose to get water ready for the frac operation when he was struck by the hose on his ankle. The employee flipped and fell on his head. He bled from the left ear and suffered a closed fracture behind his left ear and internal bleeding on the brain.

Employee was injured while performing a "cold cut" on a 6" metal pipe of a gathering system. Employee was burned on the face, both arms, and knees. Employee was using a striker from the welding equipment and possibly ignited natural gas.

At the Hat Creek Production Pad, an employee slipped when climbing down a fixed ladder of a heater treater. The employee fell from an approximate height of 6' onto the ground. The employee was hospitalized for a period of 2 days at Southwest General Hospital.
An employee suffered a back injury when a hopper that was being lifted by a forklift fell on the employee.

At 9:00AM an employee was working on an oil field energy services tanker removing a camlock cap. Pressure was on the cap when it was removed. It blew off and struck the employee in the face injuring his jaw and damaging his teeth. The employee was transferred to different hospitals before receiving treatment. The employee was hospitalized one night in Bismarck.

On 1/21/15 at about 16:20 pm a worker was hit by the tongs on his right arm, chest, and leg. He was transported to OU Medical Center where his right hand was amputated. Immediately before the accident the drilling line was stuck. The snub line connected to the tongs snapped causing the tongs to swing around and hit the worker.

On January 22, 2015, at about 8:30 pm, a casing trough was being loaded by a forklift to a truck. The trough slid off the forks and struck the employee at the midsection of his stomach. He was pinned between the trough and a pipe rack. The employee was admitted to OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City around midnight on 1/22/15.
An employee suffered a severe struck-by injury from a bull plug and gauge while repairing the bull plug.
Employee was using a 10 lb. sledge hammer to tighten a hammer union. The employee missed and caught his right index finger between the handle of the hammer and a valve handle.
The employee was in a snubbing basket. Upon exiting, the employee slid down the emergency fire pole, lost his grip, and fell.
On January 22, 2015, an employee was hospitalized after falling 12 feet to the ground through a 2' x 3' opening in a centrifuge stand.

An employee was on the stabbing board to hang the tong line. He unhooked the derrick climber from his harness and when he let go of it he was hit in the mouth, lost his footing, and fell even though his lanyard was attached. His face hit the standpipe of the derrick and the 3 foot fall injured his back.

A crew of employees was performing workover services. The crew was attempting to break out a crossover sub, on top of the casing scraper, using tongs. The employee was using a 36-inch wrench on top of the tongs. The tong operator engaged the tong before the employee removed his hand. The tong pinched the employee's finger between the tong and the wrench. The employee lost the fingertip of his right middle finger.

While the employees were picking up tubing, a worker grabbed the bell and pulled it back. The elevator slipped and caught his finger between the horn's elevator and the bottom of the bell. His middle finger was amputated from the finger nail to the first knuckle of the finger. He was taken to the hospital, treated and released.
Employee was working on a can wrench without the lock out/tag out system in place. The jaws of the machine opened and retracted smashing and amputating the tip of the middle finger on his left hand.
An employee fell approximately 16 feet from the stairway of a drilling rig onto the ground below. The employee suffered multiple fractures and a collapsed lung.
The employee, walking across a muddy location, slipped and twisted his left ankle and broke his fibula near the ankle.

Two employees were pressure washing mud tanks. The injured employee slipped and grabbed the end of the wand barrel. He then came into contact with the pressurized water, resulting in a laceration on his leg. The water was considered dirty which led to a hospitalization as a precautionary measure.

The rig crew was rigging down the work floor on the rig to change out a valve on the well head. The injured employee was standing on the rig platform reaching for the pin and lost his balance. He fell and hit the cellar ring of the well head. He injured his right ribs, right shoulder blade and punctured a lung.

On January 28, 2015, an employee was using an 8-foot A-frame ladder to change out pipe fitting at the Hydro Cracker Unit. The employee fell from the ladder while descending, breaking his lower right leg in the ankle area. Employee was transported by ambulance to Pauls Valley, then transferred to the Norman Regional Hospital where he had surgery to set the bone.
Pipeline was being cleaned using a pig. The pig shot out of the pipeline and struck the employee, causing injuries to the lower part of his body.

The injured employee had his left hand on a forklift, signaling to the operator to lower the forks due to an unbalanced situation with a parts catcher screen assembly. In the process of lowering the forks the screen assembly shifted smashing the tip of the employees index finger on his left hand between the bonnet of the manual valve of the screen assembly and the forks.
An employee's finger was caught between the top and bottom of the top drive track causing an acute traumatic amputation of the left distal index finger.
Employees were making a connection when tubing fell striking the employee in the lower face.

An employee at a remote Marathon Oil jobsite was pressure testing pipe when he was struck-by 9500psi of water when bolts broke on the flange connecting two pipes causing the high pressure water to strike the employee and one other sub-contractor's employee who were standing approximately 15 feet away.

An employee was working on an offshore barge and fell while trying to connect a hook to a lowered boom of a crane. The employee braced his fall with his hands, fracturing his right wrist. The employee was taken to the hospital by helicopter to receive treatment. A cast was placed on the employee's right wrist and he was kept overnight for observation.
On or about February 6, 2015 at 12:00pm, an employee's finger was caught in between two collars on a pipe while assisting in the lay down of 3 1/2" tubing coming out of the oil head.
On or about Monday, February 9, 2015, at 2:45 pm an employee was changing a transformer in a Merit Energy oil rig when he touched a hot wire injuring his head and left hand.

Employee was installing a TIW valve assembly for Blow Out Preventive (BOP) testing to get a pressure reading from the pipe. During the BOP process, the TIW assembly was sitting on top of the pipe when the pipe fell and struck the employee in the left foot causing lacerations. Employee was Medevac'd to hospital to receive sutures in left foot and was kept overnight for observation.

On 2/11/15, a Pioneer Oil Field Services Rig Hand working at Petco/Louden Field amputated the first digit (approximately the length of his fingernail) of his right ring finger. The amputation occurred when a landing joint connector being pulled by a chain became tight and wrapped around said employee's finger who was holding/guiding the chain at the time of incident.
A worker slipped on ice and fractured his ankle. The injury required surgery and admission to the hospital.

An employee tripped and fell to the ground. The employee landed on his knees in a pile of hot petroleum coke. The employee sustained burns on both legs from the coke, and possibly the hot steam. The employee was taken by ambulance to Christiana Hospital, and later transferred to Crozer-Chester Medical Center in Chester, Pennsylvania. The employee sustained 2nd degree burns on his legs, and 3rd degree burns on his ankles.

Employee was changing out a hydraulic ram on a rig when a swivel on the come-along broke and pinched the employee's thumb. First aid was performed at the local hospital and then the employee was transported to Denver. An artery in the thumb was damaged and the right hand thumb was later amputated at the first joint.

On or about February 12, 2015, a worker was trying to light the heater treater In The Barriers Well, but the gas valve was not fully shut causing the gas to flash in his face. The Well was shut in and the worker was trying to get it back online. The worker sustained injuries to his face and right hand.
On or about February 12, 2015, an employee slipped on ice/gravel while walking in the company's job yard resulting in a broken leg.

An employee put a valve into the hole of an oil well as part of the process to plug the well. Pressure built up behind the valve causing it to explode out of the hole. One of the employee's legs was severely injured and is being medically amputated.
An employee was injured during a fire at a gas well.

Employee had a finger surgically amputated after sustaining an injury while filling a tanker truck with water. The employee's pinky ring caught on a grease fitting while he was climbing off the truck stripping the skin from the center knuckle to the tip of his finger.

An employee was standing on a pipe rack using his feet to roll pipe to the edge when his foot was caught by a pipe causing him to fall off the rack. The employee's foot was broken by the pipe that also fell off the rack.
On or before February 19, 2015, an employee slipped and fell on ice while carrying a 2-inch x 30-foot-long piece of pipe, resulting in a tibia/fibula fracture to the right leg.
On February 20, 2015, an employee was injured when a Genie man lift rolled over. The employee was hospitalized.

On 20 February 2015, at approximately 1100hrs, employee was holding a pin that was being hammered by a third-party employee. His right, middle distal phalanx was struck by the hammer and crushed. The employee was taken to Midland Memorial Hospital. The distal phalanx was surgically removed on 23 February 2015 during an outpatient procedure.

An employee working on an oil-and-gas service rig suffered partial amputations of the right middle and right ring fingers after his hand was caught between the tong plate and the pin that secures the tongs.

Employee amputated the tip of the left-hand pinky finger while pulling 20' long pipe from a pipe rack. While pulling one section of pipe from the rack, another pipe shifted; the employee's finger became caught between the pipe and pipe rack, which caused the amputation.

Two employees were hospitalized due to injuries sustained during maintenance operations on a workover rig in the maintenance shop. One employee suffered a crushing injury when a derrick floor fell on his chest, breaking ribs and causing a collapsed lung. A second employee suffered a broken elbow due to a fall sustained while attempting to hold the falling rig floor.

Employees were opening a hatch at one of the salt water disposal tanks when a spark created a flash fire. The employee was burned in the flash fire and hospitalized. The other employees received minor skin burns and were examined and released the same day.
An employee was attaching a compressor to a skid with a pneumatic impact driver. The employee's finger got caught in the driver, which tore off his fingertip; the injury did not involve the bone.
An employee was draining condensate out of the treater line when a flash fire occurred, causing second degree burns.
An employee was struck by falling blocks from a crane.
Employee was struck in his back with a chain while walking behind a vehicle-mounted drilling rig.
Employee was lifting pipes when the pipes slipped and fell onto the employee's fingers resulting in medical amputation.
An employee fell approximately 6 feet off of a rig structure while nippling up the BOP and broke a tibia.

On 03/09/15, at approximately 10:30 a.m., an employee was working from an aluminum ladder that was leaning against a tank. The employee fell approximately 4 feet off of the ladder and landed on a cement barrier. The employee suffered three broken ribs and a bruised kidney and was admitted to UPMC-Presbyterian.

On or about March 10, 2015, at 2:30 p.m., two employees got struck by a drilling motor and a cart. While pushing the cart from the outside of the building to the inside, the cart tipped and the drilling motor fell off. The cart struck the first employee in the torso area and pinned him underneath. The cart struck the second employee when it tipped and propelled to the side. The second employee sustained a forehead contusion, fractured left ankle, right ear laceration, and fractured facial bone. Both employees were taken to the hospital.

On 3/11/2015, at approximately 8:30 AM, an employee was injured when the tank load he was unloading shifted on his forklift. His finger got caught between the forks and the load when he reached in to secure it. He was taken to the hospital and received surgery.

At approximately 3:00 AM on 3/11/2015, an employee was injured while trying to avoid an animal in the road. His truck swerved, and the tires got caught on the soft shoulder, causing the semi-trailer to roll over. He suffered three broken ribs and a punctured lung.

An employee was unloading fuel into a tank at a customer location. He was walking while offloading and talking with another employee when he lost consciousness. A local bystander attempted CPR. Employee was taken to the hospital.

An employee's right ring finger was smashed between hydraulic tongs and a truck bed while running rods. The employee lost the finger from the nail to the end. The employee was transported to the hospital and treated.
An employee's finger was amputated while operating a service rig.

An employee was spotting a tractor that was picking up equipment. The employee slipped, and the employee's hand was caught between the tractor and equipment. The hand was crushed and required surgery.
An employee's hand got pinched between a cylinder and an air cylinder casing; the right index finger and middle finger were amputated.
An employee on an oil rig had his left hand amputated by a rock crusher while dislodging rocks from the machine. Lockout procedures were not followed at the time.

An employee was attempting to place the pipe spinner leaver in neutral position when he tripped. His right hand engaged the spinner, and his left hand got caught in the spinner chain, cutting his left pinky and ring fingers.
An employee suffered a broken arm while removing a stack from a combustor. The crew was loosening bolts from the ground level to remove a stack when it pivoted and struck the employee's arm.

An employee was retrieving mud flaps to reinstall on a truck. A cotter pin on the winch line, which was secured to the rear of the truck, came loose. The wire on the driver's side became unsecure and struck the employee on the left side, below the shoulder and back.
An employee was opening a gate when the last finger of the employee's left hand was pinched in a roller; the fingertip was amputated.
An employee was straightening "subs" (pipe-shaped oilfield tools) on a pallet when he caught his finger between two subs. He pulled his hand away, tearing the skin and nail from his fingertip.
An employee stepped off of the boat in mud and water up to his knees. He was hospitalized with cellulitis.
An employee was struck by a 2,000-pound pipe while working on a service rig. He sustained damage to his left ankle.

An employee fractured his right middle finger while loading a 250-pound test plug onto the back of his truck. The forklift used to raise the load released it, and the employee's finger got caught between the test plug and a supporting bracket. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
Employees were relieving pressure from a pressure relief valve assembly. The valve bar or assembly struck the injured employee in the neck and chest.

Employees were lifting a BOP using a forklift to work on the bottom of the BOP. While the BOP was suspended by the forklift, the injured employee placed his hand on the forks. The BOP rolled backwards, catching and amputating his left pinky fingertip between the heavy equipment and the fork.
An employee was operating the elevators and tongs to run pipe out of the hole when the drilling line broke. The block fell and struck his foot.
An employee sustained injuries to his left index finger while rigging down.

Employees were hanging a horse head on a well. The injured employee was on a pumping unit, waiting for the horse head to be lifted with rig blocks, with a safety retractable line attached. The line got caught in the blocks and pulled the employee off of the pumping unit, causing the employee to fall 10 to 15 feet before the safety line engaged. At the point of engagement, the safety line snapped, and the employee fell to the ground.
An employee was injured on 3/26/15 while working on an inactive, disengaged brake. The employee tripped and was struck by a counterbalance in the chest and abdomen.

An employee was stabbing up in the derrick while a pipe was being brought up on an elevator. As the employee reached to unlatch the elevator, the tongs engaged, striking the employee's left hand resulting in a broken wrist.

Two employees were removing sludge with a vacuum hose and pressure washer inside a frac tank. One of the employees was hit in the foot with the pressurized water (approximately 3500 psi) from the pressure washer, blowing out the employee's boot. The employee sustained a pin-hole injury to the foot and was admitted to the hospital.
Employees were connecting a drill pipe. The injured employee suffered a partial amputation to his pinky finger when it got caught between the pipe and tong.
An employee's hand got caught between elevators and a derrick. The employee sustained a laceration between the ring and small fingers on the right hand, as well as a fractured small finger.
An employee slipped and caught his finger between two pieces of equipment. As the crossover sub fell, he was unable to remove his finger in time. He also broke his wrist.
An employee was walking up the stairs of a work-over rig when he lost his footing and slipped. He landed on the ground at the bottom of the stairs and fractured his hip.

An employee was on a drilling rig floor during normal drilling operations when pressure built up and blew through a hole. The employee was blown backwards and hit his head and arm. His head and arm sustained lacerations. He was admitted to the hospital for surgery on a fractured skull.
An employee injured his fingertip while rebuilding a down-hole tube. He was taken to the hospital where part of his finger was amputated.

An employee was grinding at a pedestal grinder on a small piece of work. The work had been set in place using vice grips. The work slipped from its placement, moving and lodging into the space between the work rest and the disc. The employee's left hand was also moved by the force into this area, lacerating/crushing his index, middle, and ring fingers.
An employee with a sledgehammer struck the injured employee's left middle finger while he was holding a board. The injured employee's fingertip was amputated.
Employees were replacing equipment to install a cannon ball. As they were replacing the equipment, an employee bumped one of the valves. Pressure was released, spraying onto the employee's neck.
The employee was sprayed by caustic when a 1/2" tubing broke while preparing a 3/4" line for maintenance.

On April 6, 2015, an employee working on a rig sustained a head injury that required stitches after falling approximately 5.5 feet from the top of the scavenger tank/platform to the matting board. Guardrails on top of the platform were removed at the time. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
An employee received an abrasion on the second right toe, which escalated to and infection and required amputation.

An employee was adjusting a belt on a power washer. While checking the tension, the pump turned back on. This kicked the wrench away from the employee's hand and pulled his hand into the machine. His right little fingertip was amputated, and his right thumb was lacerated.
An employee's foot got crushed between the floor and boom of a drill rig. He broke his big toe.

An employee was performing cementing operations on a drilling rig. While using an air hoist to hoist a cement plug over a pipe, his thumb got caught between the "wing" of the plug and the plug itself. He sustained an amputation to the left-hand thumb up to the knuckle.
An employee heard a hissing sound from pressure while breaking pipe joints. He then jumped from the rig floor six feet above ground and broke his leg when he landed.

On April 13, 2015, at approximately 1:30 p.m., an employee was shot in the left hand. Prior to the incident, a well tender found an issue at a well site. The well tender contacted a roustabout crew to repair and clean the area. The injured employee responded to the job to oversee the work, take pictures, and complete an incident report. After completing his work, he was driving away from the site and was stopped by a suspect dressed in camouflage, standing in the road. The suspect stood on the passenger side of the truck, played a recording that said "stop drilling," and pointed a gun at the employee's head. The employee grabbed the gun and shoved it away from his head; the gun fired into his left hand. The employee drove off and was hospitalized.
An employee suffered systemic poisoning when he ingested anti-freeze while drinking from an improperly labeled, temporary-use container.
An employee received a head injury when a pressurized line came apart.
An employee was hospitalized when his truck rolled over while hauling produce water to a disposal site due to soft road conditions on 60th Street NW, Williston, ND.

An employee was in the process of rolling a 22 inch diameter pipe with an instrument called a C-Bar (tool used to roll the pipe). His finger got caught between the C-Bar and the next joint of pipe to be rolled which resulted in an amputation.

On or about 20 April 2015 at approximately 1000 hrs an employee of Holman Well Service was hospitalized with an injured hand. The employee was assisting in the replacement of a BOP for Apache Bevins East 99-1H well head. The BOP was placed on the ground next to the well head. As the employees were working around the BOP, it fell over pinning the employee's right hand between the BOP body and the structure of the well head. The employee sustained multiple hand fractures.

An employee working on the drilling floor was picking up the jerk chain for the tongs when the driller applied tension to the chain. The employee got the fingers of his left hand pinched between the headache post and the chain.
An employee fell from a tractor and struck her head on the ground, resulting in a concussion. She was hospitalized overnight.
An employee fell while standing on a crescent wrench, cutting his leg on a valve.
An employee was sliding mail from a cart to the floor when she felt pain in the middle of her abdomen below the belly button. She was hospitalized for treatment of a hernia and required surgery.

An employee was attaching drill pipe to elevators using his hands. His fingers got stuck between the elevator and the drill pipe, which broke two fingers (pointer and middle finger of the right hand).
An employee was directing a forklift with a load trying to get it on a trailer. The employee got caught between the forklift and the rail while holding the tote support.

An employee's finger was crushed while performing rigging-down operations at a well site. The employee was hospitalized, and surgery was performed to remove the left index finger to the first knuckle.
An employee suffered burns from a flashover fire.

An employee was running a panel that opens/shuts hydraulic valves, pumping nitrogen. The employee was told to open the valve slowly; a flashover occurred when this action was taken. The employee was hospitalized for burns.

A third party contractor was nippling up a production tree. The employee was tightening the bull plug and the wrench slipped off causing the employee to lose balance and to fall approximately 5 feet to the ground.
An employee was injured by a brush wire and was hospitalized after infection spread to his arm.
An employee reached into a 12-inch pipe opening and a hydraulic valve closed on his left hand, partially amputating three fingers and causing skin loss to the back of his hand. He was hospitalized.
Employee performing flow-back operations at an oil and gas well site received burns from a flash fire.
An employee suffered a partial amputation injury when his fingers were caught in a pinch point between the hoist line and sheave.

Drilling pipe was being rolled off of a truck onto the rack. The pipe kicked back as it reached the bottom, catching an employee's right thumb between the pipe and the stack of pipes. The employee sustained an amputation to half of his thumb tip.
An employee received flash fire burns while working on a non-functioning vaporizer at the 13-mile, full-service terminal vicinity in Williston, North Dakota.
An employee suffered an amputation injury when a valve slipped and pinched the employee's finger between the valve and the frame of the truck at or near Micahlucas 2-5H in Dunn County, North Dakota.
An employee was exposed to hydrocarbons while tank gauging at or near well site Charging Eagle 14-14-10 in Dunn County, North Dakota.
An employee fell from an elevated work platform on a drill rig while installing piping for the well. The employee broke both ankles.
An employee was struck on the head by a piece of a split rim when he was inflating a tire on a motor grader.
An employee was changing the fuel filter on an all-terrain skid loader. The skid loader was turned on while the gear was engaged, causing the unit to roll over and crush the employee's legs.

While being lifted by a derrick air hoist during oil well drilling operations, an employee's steel-toe boot got caught under the steel cross member "girt" of the derrick. The toe was amputated inside the boot.

On May 13, 2015, at approximately 12:00 midnight, an employee suffered a concussion and was hospitalized after being struck by a 1.5- to 2-inch flex steel hose. The employee was working in the cellar while a rig hand worked on the rig floor 30 feet above. The rig hand disconnected the hydraulic hose, which fell 30 feet and struck the employee in the head.
Employees were trying to maneuver a metal pipe into place using a hoist when the swivel released and caused the pipe to suddenly lift up about 6 inches and strike the injured employee in the jaw.

An employee was disassembling a wire-line tool when a section of the tooling fell onto the employee's hand. The employee sustained deep lacerations to four fingers and small fractures to two fingers, requiring hospitalization.
An employee's arm got caught in conveyor belt guide rollers while troubleshooting the equipment, resulting in hospitalization.

Two employees were installing plastic on a strainer basket inside of a reactor 30' high when the basket slipped and pulled in one employee's glove and middle finger. Approximately 1/4" of the employee's left middle fingertip was amputated. The basket is made of steel and is shaped like a small garbage can measuring 2' x 1.5' and weighing 200 pounds.
An employee suffered an amputation injury while rigging up a top drive at or near Parshall, North Dakota.

An employee was loading oil into the gun barrel while on a ladder. The gun barrel caught fire possibly from the electric heating element and ignited the employee's FR clothes. The employee received second degree burns on his forearm, his hand, and behind his ear.
An employee fell from a height, fracturing his left and right ankles and left arm. He was hospitalized.
An employee suffered a hand injury while performing routine maintenance on a pump jack at or near Pierre Creek Nelson 44-23 HR in McKenzie County, North Dakota.
A Noble Energy employee was injured by a compressor fire at a company location in rural Northeast Weld County, Colorado. The employee was hospitalized.

On May 22, 2015, a contractor had removed the stairs from a job trailer in order to install skirting around the trailer. An employee, who had not heard the warning of the contractor, exited the trailer and fell 40 inches to the gravel below. The employee fractured his right leg and was transported to a local hospital.

An operator was instructing a new employee how to operate the hydro blasting machine when it suddenly actuated. The operator suffered injuries to the hand and was admitted to the local hospital for surgery.
An employee was moving a cement head that weighs approximately 400 lbs when it fell onto the employee's left foot.
On May 24, 2015, an employee working near a mud pump suffered an injury to his right leg/knee when he was struck by fluid under pressure when a hose ruptured.

Employees were unloading the BOP from the trailer to start nippling up. The injured employee was assisting in the lift and had his hand on one of the cables. His gloved hand was pulled into a pulley when the BOP shifted, resulting in the amputation of the middle fingertip on his right hand.

On May 29, 2015, an employee was working inside a sulpha treat reactor vessel using a high pressure (5000 PSI) water sprayer gun to cut off the congealed catalyst material inside. The employee slipped and fell; the high-pressure water sprayer hit the employee's right foot and punctured a hole through the rubber boot. The employee sustained a puncture open wound on the right foot, second toe. The employee was hospitalized and received treatment.
An employee suffered a fractured leg after getting pinned between a semi truck and a tank at or near 58th Street NW in Williston, North Dakota.

An employee was loading equipment and tools onto a truck to prepare to leave a well site. The employee was standing on a lubricator rack/catwalk where he was releasing the straps on the crane when the catwalk collapsed. The employee fell approximately 5 feet to the truck below and hit his head. He was hospitalized.

On or about 1300 hrs on 31 May 2015, a One Source Industrial Services employee was hospitalized when the employee's vehicle overturned on CR 5000 in Andrews County, Texas. The incident occurred as the employee attempted to turn onto CR 5000. The employee lost control of the vehicle, causing it to overturn and resulting in a broken arm, bruised ribs, and a possible concussion.

While removing and replacing worn wire rope on a hydraulic tugger winch, the injured employee's left foot was caught in the wire rope while the drum was rotating. The employee was hospitalized and had toes on his left foot amputated.

On or about 0530 hrs on the 2nd day of June 2015, an employee was injured when the vehicle he was driving overturned on a lease road approximately five miles east of Mentone Texas. The employee was hospitalized with three broken ribs on the right side of the thorax and a broken rib on the left side of the thorax.

On or about 3 June 2015 at 0715 hrs an employee suffered an amputation of the distal portion of his middle phalanges left hand. The employee was attempting to replace a flange when the flange slipped and pinched his phalanges between it and the structure he was placing the flange on.

An employee was pulled off of the drill floor by a tugger line. The employee was standing behind a safety gate holding the hoist line to put tension on it so it would not get tangled in the hoist drum. Something made the line jerk; the employee did not let go and was pulled over the safety gate, sliding down what the employer called a beaver slide. He was hospitalized to repair his badly damaged hand. He also had 23 stitches put in his head and three fractured vertebrae.

On June 06, 2015, at approximately 8:45 p.m., an employee was struck on the right leg by a rubber discharge hose that had been disconnected on one end after the pump was engaged by the equipment operator.

On June 9, 2015, an employee wearing flame resistant clothing was retrieving samples of hot, 400 degrees F asphalt from a controlled sample point when he was splashed/sprayed by pressurized hot asphalt. He received second degree burns to his head, neck, chest, and both arms. He also received first and second degree burns on the right side of his face.

An employee was loading a well with hot oil. The employee had turned valves off and started to fill the well. The pressure in the tank filled due to the hot oil. The pressure release valve released flammable vapors and/or gases. The flammable vapors and/or gases ignited, burning the employee's face (cheeks and ears). The employee was wearing flame resistant clothing, a hard hat, and safety glasses at the time.

An employee was assisting offloading truck. A supervisor noticed the employee was sweating excessively and looked pale. The supervisor informed the employee to sit inside the air-conditioned truck and cool off. After a period of time the employee came out of the truck and attempted to continue to work. The employee complained that his hands were cramping. The employee was taken to the hospital. At the hospital, it was noted that the employee had high CK levels possibly due to prior heat illness.

An employee was spotting moving equipment when he noticed a piece of iron that was sticking out from the equipment. He reached up to swivel the iron when his finger got caught between the iron and the parked equipment.

An employee was working at an oil and gas lease site when he made contact with a 480 V transmission line while working between the distribution box and the well he was inspecting. The employee received third degree burns on his hands and back and was admitted to the hospital.
An employee was found unresponsive after being missing for approximately one hour. The employee was potentially exposed to struck by hazards while performing lay down hand duties.

One employee from Chevron and two employees from Exterran were putting compressors back on line when a rupture on the discharge line occurred. The Chevron employee was taken to the hospital to removed debris from his left leg and released. One Exterran employee was not injured and the other employee received a scratch above eye requiring first aid only.
Hydraulic fluid injected into the finger of an employee working on a forklift.

An employee was operating a hydraulic-activated torque wrench to bolt up a flange. The hydraulic hose to the wrench developed a leak. The employee was injured when high pressure hydraulic fluid penetrated his right hand. The hydraulic wrench was a rental unit. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee slipped and fell while going down stairs and broke his leg.

A contract truck driver from another company delivered material at the well site and left without unhooking a hose. As the driver drove away, the hose broke and struck an employee, breaking the employee's femur. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was cleaning a clogged strainer on a pump. Upon removal of the strainer, stored up steam was released and burned the employee's face, chest and right arm.
While a boom was being unlatched at a well site, the boom snapped and threw the pipe off, hitting an employee on the ground.
An employee was hospitalized due to a flash fire at a compressor station while servicing a stage 2 compressor in Alexander, North Dakota.
An employee was installing a pulley on a machine in the pipe yard. The pulley pulled the employee's left index finger into the machine, amputating the fingertip.

An employee was changing a belt on an abrasive blasting machine. The employee placed the belt on the pulley while the machine was still turning. The pulley pulled his finger into the machine. His left index fingertip was amputated.
An employee was handling pipe on the drilling rig. His right ring finger got caught between the thread protector and pipe collar.
On or about June 26, 2015, at approximately 1240 hrs. an employee for J&M Energy Services suffered the amputation of the distal phalanx of his right thumb when it was caught in a pumping unit.

A crew member was attempting to remove a blockage in a 2" discharge line on mud pump #2 when it released, striking him in the right calf and knocking him to the ground. The crew member was taken to the hospital for medical evaluation and treatment and then transferred to another hospital for surgery and further treatment.

On or about June 30, 2015, an employee for Archer Pressure Pumping was hospitalized when he fell off a truck and onto a metal ramp while attempting to cover an equipment truck with a tarp. The injured employee was standing on the truck and reaching for the tarp when he lost his balance and fell onto the ramp striking his face on the ramp. As a result of the fall, the employee fractured an eye socket and check bone, the right hip and right forearm. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery to repair his injuries.

Employees were running rods downhole on a servicing rig when the pump hit a tight spot causing slack on the rods. The slack resulted in the rod elevator breaking and allowing the rods to come loose. The rod struck the employee in the middle, right side of the back and knocked him to the ground.

Employees were making up float shoes on the first joint of a casing job. The pipe came loose, swung, and caught one of the employees between the manual back-up tong and the back-up snub line. The employee was hospitalized and treated for injuries to the chest and colon area.
An employee became dehydrated during work and was hospitalized overnight.
While lowering a swivel arm/gate, an employee's fingertip got caught between the heavy equipment. The fingertip was later amputated.
An employee was troubleshooting an oil rig top drive while the main drive was running. The employee sustained an amputation.

An employee was working with a perforating gun on a work bench. He turned the gun and it skipped off the roller wheels and fell on the edge of the table, amputating the index and middle fingertips on his right hand.
