Employees were rigging down the workover rig at about 11:30 a.m., on July 5, when an employee's right thumb and first finger were caught between the derrick tip section and stop plate. The employee's thumb had to be surgically amputated.
An employee fell approximately 12 feet from the top of the tanker truck he was washing injuring the left shoulder and upper ribs and suffering a facial fracture.

An employee was cutting bands off of tubing to separate the electric cable from the tubing when the band cutter came up and hit him in his left eye. Eye protection was not worn at the time. He was hospitalized.
An employee slipped and fell while climbing an A-Frame ladder, landing on his right side. He was hospitalized for fractured ribs.
An employee got caught between a trailer and truck while directing the truck driver to back up. The employee's leg was crushed, and the employee was hospitalized.
An employee loading high-pressure iron into pipe racking suffered a fingertip amputation after his left pinky finger got caught between the pinch point of the iron and pipe racking.
On July 8, 2015, at approximately 6:00 p.m., an employee was struck in the face by a high-pressure hose. The employee suffered multiple facial fractures and was hospitalized.

An employee was repairing a seal on a valve operator. He placed the drum cover over the actuator piston using an overhead crane and was manipulating the drum while operating the crane controls. While attempting to lower the drum the final 2 inches, he inadvertently pushed the wrong button on the hoist control, causing the drum to move upward. As a result, his left thumb was pinched between the base plate and drum cover. There was no amputation.

A vertical 42' section of 4" drilling pipe was being supported by a forklift tine and sash rope for an electric cable installation. The sash broke and the pipe fell to the ground striking a drilling rig worker and causing a skull fracture.
An employee suffered burns from a flash fire that was created by a trash pump unit powered by a gas generator. It is used to pump oil and water from an open top tank at the well site.

On July 17, 2015, at approximately 1:45pm, an employee was hospitalized after suffering two broken bones to his lower left leg. Before the incident, the employee was standing on the third rung of a 12-foot stepladder, tightening bolts on a flange with a torque wrench. While applying pressure to the wrench, a reducer on the wrench broke, causing the employee to lose his balance. As he stepped down 34" to the gravel surface, he landed awkwardly on his left foot, causing fractures.

An employee was working on a valve that was suspended in the air with a threaded eye bolt. The eye bolt became unthreaded and the valve fell on the employee's right ring finger. The employee was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was hospitalized for hydrogen sulfide exposure while pulling tank bottoms at an oil and gas waste disposal site.

An employee was walking near a forklift holding a non-secure joint casing. The employee sustained a compound fracture to the leg when the joint casing rolled off the forklift tines and landed on the employee's leg.

On or about 19 July 2015, at approximately 1600 hours, an employee of Precision Drilling was lowering a roof over the mud tanks area during rigging down procedures. The roof fell on top of him, fracturing his ribs. He was hospitalized.
An employee suffered an amputation while connecting an air puller to the D ring of a hydraulic tong on a servicing rig.
An employee experienced heat-related muscle cramps while loading materials onto a vehicle.
An explosion occurred while an employee was performing work on a well head. He sustained burns to 60% to 80% of his body.
An employee was hospitalized for dehydration/heat exhaustion.
An employee was hospitalized with an ankle injury after falling 4 feet from a pipe lifting machine.

On July 27, 2015, a work crew was rigging up. At approximately 11:45 PM, a guardrail was installed. Before the workers secured it with bolts, the injured employee leaned against it and fell 26 feet to the ground below. He sustained five small fractures to his back and was hospitalized.

An employee was ascending a steel fixed ladder. The employee fell approximately 7 to 9 feet to the ground below. The total elevation change was 9 1/2 feet high. The employee suffered a head laceration and broken bones and was hospitalized.
Employee was performing maintenance by changing out lubricator. While manually putting the sheave back on, the employee caught a finger between the sheave and belt.
An employee's third and fourth digits were amputated.

An employee was coming out of a hole with tubing when the tubing broke. A pipe fell and hit the employee on the head, causing the employee to lose consciousness. The employee was wearing a hard hat at the time. The employee was hospitalized overnight with a mild concussion.
An employee was burned by hot water while disconnecting a pump hose that was under pressure. He was hospitalized.
An employee was using a pneumatic torque wrench while working on a well head. The employee lost control of the wrench, which struck his right thumb and fractured the bone.
An employee was stabbing a mud tool into casing when the employee's left-hand thumb was amputated just behind the thumb nail. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was overcome by heat stress while conducting oil-well servicing operations.

An employee was performing normal work duties doing a "meter run" when he started to feel badly and went to the Arnett office. Employees/management at that location thought the employee was suffering from heat related issues and called an ambulance. The employee was treated at the hospital for heat stress.

An employee was pinning tubing together to skid the rig. The employee's hands were placed between the two pieces, and the left pinky and ring fingers got pinched. Both fingers were surgically amputated.
The employee was cutting a sample valve using an unguarded grinder. There was a 6" blade installed on a 4" grinder. The employee cut his left index finger and shattered the bone.
Employee was struck by a high pressure rigid line on a oil and gas production site and sustained non-life-threatening injuries.

An employee was performing a fluid end replacement on a pump using an impact gun to remove pump suction manifold bolts. While loosening the bolts, the suction manifold fell ~6 inches catching employee's arms between the suction manifold and trail fender resulting in a contusion injury. The header weighs approximately 250-300 pounds.

During pipeline construction and while stringing pipe, a track hoe operator was unloading pipe from a delivery truck when an employee walked behind the track hoe on the operator's blind side. The track hoe backed up onto the employee's left foot amputating it.
An industrial power washer exploded sending an employee to the hospital for a fractured skull.
An employee lost control of the brake handle during rig down operations and it struck him in the jaw.

An employee had connected a flux car for unloading. The previous car that unloaded into this line had oil with some residual water. When the flux (a tar-like substance) made contact with the water, it expanded and contacted the employee as he exited the railcar, causing first and second degree thermal burns.

An employee was installing a pump during the fracking process when he felt lightheaded and began vomiting. He started having heat cramps and was hospitalized after suffering severe dehydration while operating equipment outside with temperatures of 105F.
An employee was being lifted by an aerial lift to repair a wellhead. The employee's left thumb got crushed and fractured between the aerial lift and the wellhead.

An employee was helping a flow hand from another company change rubber between two pieces of high-pressure pipe. As the employee was checking to make sure the rubber was seated properly, the clamp slipped, amputating his right-hand middle fingertip.

An employee was cleaning out a mud pond when his right leg, up to his shin, became stuck in the mud. He was unable to free himself. A coworker used a high-pressure washing wand to try to loosen the area around the employee's leg. The pressure wand got too close and cut through the employee's boot, lacerating the side of his right foot from the small toe to the middle. He was hospitalized and received stitches.
An employee was holding a pin while another employee was driving the pin in with a hammer. The employee's finger was struck by the hammer resulting in the amputation of the fingertip.
An employee was positioning dunnage under a load when the load fell on the left hand resulting in the amputation of the left hand.
An employee fell approximately 10 feet while setting straps on a storage tank and landed on his feet. He suffered injuries to both feet and a broken right ankle.

An employee was working on an oil rig attempting to place a pulser into the drilling hole. A metal cable on the hula band being used to guide the pulser into the hole caught his thumb and amputated it at the first joint.

An employee was performing maintenance on a compressor unit. The compressor unit inside the building was shut off. The employee went to restart the compressor and a flash fire occurred. The employee suffered first and second degree burns to the hands, face, and arms, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was working on an oil drilling rig. While attaching a check valve to a vertical pup joint, the employee's right index finger was pinched between the two parts, amputating the fingertip.

An employee was doing iron fabrication work. While working on a circular saw, the blade "kicked" back the piece of flat strap iron, injuring the employee's left-hand middle finger. The injury resulted in an amputation (bone loss) along the fingertip.
An employee was climbing into a bulldozer when wind caused the door to shut on and amputate his thumb.
An employee was assembling testing equipment. The employee's left index finger got caught between a nut and an impact wrench and was amputated to the knuckle.
An employee was working to set a tool up to start torqueing when his pinky finger got caught between the hydraulic torque wrench and a part. He dislocated his pinky finger.

An employee was conducting work on the 60-feet-high platform of an oil derrick, operating rigging to move piping into position. The employee became sick, vomited, experienced cramps, and was eventually hospitalized for heat-related health issues.
An employee's H2S monitor went off while he was delivering salt water on location. He eventually became ill and was hospitalized with respiratory problems.

An employee was moving an oil field casing/pipe-related materials in and out of a pipe rack with a forklift. The pipes rolled down the rack and pinched/lacerated the employee's fingertip, which had to be amputated.

An employee was driving through a construction zone after unloading production water at a disposal well when his vehicle veered off the road and crashed south of Killdeer, North Dakota, on Highway 22. He suffered back injuries.
An employee was greasing a 2-inch valve with a high-pressure grease gun when the hose erupted in the employee's right palm, lacerating the palm of the right hand.

On September 7, 2015, an employee's left ankle was swollen after working in the acetic acid unit to clear/de-inventory the purification section. He was eventually hospitalized for ankle blisters and chemical burns.

An employee was changing a swab on a mud pump using a wrench to stroke the pump. The pipe wrench slipped and he fell backwards off the skid to the ground. His back and head struck the ground and he injured his chest. He sustained a head laceration, upper right bicep cut, chest contusion, and concussion.
An employee fractured his hand while connecting a trailer when his hand got caught in the trailer's hydraulic cylinder.

Employees were working at a remote well site in Kingfisher, Oklahoma making a connection with two pipes when the pumping host attachment at one end came loose and struck the employee's left arm, breaking both bones of the forearm.

At approximately 11:30 on 15 September 2015, an employee was hospitalized when he was struck in the chest by a cap on a pressure vessel that he and another employee were removing. Remaining pressure in the pipe leading to the pressure vessel caused the cap to violently dislodge during the procedure and strike the employee in the chest, breaking one rib and causing the employee to suffer a broken left elbow, a laceration that required sutures on his right elbow and a hemorrhage on the artery leading to his adrenal gland.
An employee was bitten by a rattle snake on the right index finger.

The employee was circulating mud and water and sucking fluid from a steel container with a running vacuum truck. H2S vapor accumulated under the truck. When it reached his hot pump, it caused a flash fire. The employee suffered burns to his face and hands.

An employee was cleaning out the air actuator. The employee called out to a second employee who did not hear him correctly and the second employee closed a valve amputating the employee's right middle finger above the finger nail.

An employee at an oil field site was snubbing pipe while standing on a catwalk. As a second pipe was being loaded into the V-door, it caught the end of the first pipe, sending the second pipe into the air. The employee saw the pipe and jumped from the catwalk to avoid being struck. The pipe fell on and broke his left leg.
An employee was working on a heater when the fuel gas system detonated and caused a flash fire. The employee was burned on the right side of the face and ear.

An employee was using elevators to latch pipe. While pulling the elevators back to latch another joint of pipe from the trailer, his fingertip got caught between the horn and bale. He sustained a right index fingertip avulsion.
An employee was performing maintenance on a dehydration unit when the employee received a fluid burn to the left hand.

Two shop employees were in the process of tearing down a 1250 Ton Slip Type Elevator (STE) and were pulling the carriers and slips out of the STE. While removing one of the carriers from the slip, utilizing the overhead crane, the entire slip assembly (carrier, slip, and slip hanger) began to rise out of the tool. As the slip hanger rose the IP reached in to remove it when the slip suddenly released from the carrier pushing the slip hanger back into position. The IP's finger was caught between the slip hanger and the timing ring of the STE amputating the tip of his left index finger midway up the fingernail.

On October 8, 2015, at approximately 12:45pm, an employee was operating an ATV when it began to slide on gravel. The ATV went over an embankment and rolled approximately 100 feet. The employee fell out of the ATV and suffered a fracture to his right ankle.
An employee fell from an drilling derrick while in the process of disassembling the unit. The employee suffered injuries to the head, face and right leg as a result of the fall.
An employee was hospitalized for inhalation hazards.

The employee was pulling a safety pin out of an outrigger on the telebelt and had his finger pinched in the outrigger. The employee sustained a flesh amputation to the fingertip of the right hand middle finger.
On 10/14/2015, about 8:30pm, an employee was injured on his abdomen by pressurized fluids from an oil well when the coil tubing burst. The injured employee was hospitalized.

An employee was putting air into a tire and having trouble getting the tire bead to seal. The employee put a rag in between the rim and tire to assist the seal. When the employee went to remove the rag, the tire sealed and caught his right index finger, amputating the fingertip.

The elevator lifting a 30 foot long pipe at an oil well shifted causing the bottom of the pipe to strike an employee in the back. This employee then fell against a second employee pushing the tongs into his face and causing employee 2 to fall and strike his head against the guardrail. Employee 2 was knocked unconscious for several seconds and was hospitalized with a fracture of the bottom orbital bone below the left eye.
An employee was helping to put valves in place on a flatbed truck. A valve shifted and his hand got pinched between two valves, amputating (de-gloving) his right index finger.
An employee was pulling and laying down pipe and amputated the third digit on the right hand from the tip to the knuckle.

An employee was purging the ambient air on the compressor displacing it with natural gas. The night before, an electrical storm had shorted the motor. While purging the line, a spark ignited the natural gas causing a flash fire. The employee received burns on his face and hands and was hospitalized.
The employee was walking, tripped over a wooden pallet, and fell breaking his hip.

A company truck was overheating and an employee removed the radiator cap in an attempt to fix the problem. As he removed the cap, hot fluids exited the radiator and splashed into the employee's face, burning him. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was operating a cat head on the drilling rig and amputated fingertips.
An employee was disposing of lab quantities of chemicals and came in contact with 50% phosphoric acid. The employee suffered chemical burns to the right hand.

An employee working in the maintenance garage was conducting an oil change on a vehicle and was looking for a drum to collect the oil. The employee and another employee found a partially full drum that was labeled as methanol. The employees thought the drum potentially contained water. They took the drum outside and poured some of the contents on the ground. The employee that was conducting the oil change applied a lighter to the material on the ground. The material caught on fire. As the other employee was attempting to move the drum out of the area, some of the liquid exited the drum, and was ignited by the fire on the ground. The employee that was conducting the oil change suffered second degree burns to his right leg from the knee to the ankle.

An employee was attempting to break loose a pipe connection with a pipe wrench when his thumb was caught between the pipe and the wrench when the pipe string was lifted. He suffered a soft tissue amputation to the tip of the thumb.

The injured employee was working inside a sleeper detached from the truck. He was repairing the interior of the sleeper when a forklift driver lifted the sleeper approximately three feet off the ground. The injured employee stepped out of the sleeper and fell on his arm and shoulder breaking his upper left arm.

Employees were moving a lubricator onto a flatbed truck. An employee's finger was caught between the collar on the lubricator and the bed of the truck resulting in a right middle fingertip amputation.
An employee was rigging up a swab lubricator when he tripped on an uneven surface and broke his tibia and dislocated the fibula.
The employee was conducting a pressure test of a Blow Out Preventer (BOP) when a high pressure water spray contacted the employee's right armpit causing a 1/4 to 1/2" laceration.

An employee removed a blow out preventer (BOP) from a well head. The BOP was suspended by the rig. While suspended, the BOP started rotating catching the employee's left ring fingertip between the BOP and the stationary well head resulting in amputation.

On November 4, 2015, at approximately 8:45 an employee smashed three fingers on his right hand which resulted in hospitalization to surgically repair a broken right pinkie finger. The employee smashed the fingers when his right hand became caught between the rod elevator and tubing in the wellbore.
An employee broke two bones in his left leg when he slipped in the pea gravel and his leg slid under a cradle that was being used to support and hold in place a steel pipe.

An employee operating a forklift tried to steady something on the opposite side of the forklift with his arm. While doing so, he made contact with the controls, actuating the forklift mast in the downward direction. He broke multiple bones in his forearm and was hospitalized.
An employee was changing a valve on a trailer when the valve popped, causing the hose to disconnect and swing. The employee was exposed to propylene, requiring hospitalization for chemical burns.

An employee was working on the monkey board on an oil rig. There was a high-pressure gas kick (air pocket of gas) during drilling, and the force of the sudden explosion sent the employee flying upward. The employee's back struck the guard rail on the derrick board and was fractured, requiring surgery.
An employee was hydro-blasting the inside of a tank when the hose ruptured, sending high-velocity water over his foot. The water lacerated his ankle, requiring surgery.
Half an inch of an employee's left little finger was crushed and amputated between pipes.
An employee's right-hand middle finger was partially amputated when it got caught in an elevator door he was latching.

While a rig was being dismantled, the flow line was being moved with the boom line. The flow line pipe got caught on the stairs and pulled them loose from the rig. The stairs fell and struck an employee, who suffered a broken leg, knee fracture, and spine fracture.

A crew was removing worn slats from a burn table, which was hoisted approximately 3 feet. When an employee cut one of the slats, the table came down to its home position and cut the employee's right thigh, requiring hospitalization and stitches.
An employee was unloading pipe racks when a rack fell on and broke the employee's leg.
An employee was performing maintenance on an engine when some of the fluid got on his hands and burned them.
An employee was pulling wire on the slip line of a truck when the wire loop caught and amputated his thumb tip.
An employee ran into a guardrail and fractured vertebrae while trying to avoid being struck by a pipe that had fallen from the elevator.
The wind caught a containment pan the employee was handling and the employee suffered a hernia when he tried to hold onto it.
An employee stepped into an uncovered hole and sprained their back.
While removing a discharge hose from a water pump, an employee was exposed to hot water and suffered burns to the arms, neck and abdomen.

On or about November 22, 2015, an employee was seriously injured and hospitalized with a crushed pelvis and a lower left arm amputation, after being ejected from a front end loader that went over an embankment at the facility.

On 11/22/2015 at 11:50 a.m. an employee was isolating the gas line to identify the point of a suspected ice plug. He walked over to the meter when the hammer union on a two inch gas line disconnected and the pipe struck his leg injuring the tibia and fibula.

An employee was tripping production pipe in a well using a rig and traveling block. A pipe slipped in the well, causing a pressure change and blowout. The employee went down an escape line and fell at about 10 feet above the ground, fracturing and lacerating his face.

An employee was installing casing joints in a well using tongs when the bite of the tongs malfunctioned and the tongs bucked unexpectedly. The employee's hand got crushed between the tongs and the derrick, causing hand fractures.
An employee suffered a fracture to his left hand while moving a hydraulic catwalk.

An employee was transferring wire cable from a spool to a cradle. His right-hand middle finger got caught between a washer and a bolt, amputating the distal third of his fingertip. He required reattachment surgery.

An employee working on a oil and gas drilling rig fell from a height of 85 feet due to icy conditions on the derrick board. The ladder safety device did not engage properly resulting in the employee's fall. The employee was hospitalized with multiple broken bones, internal injuries, and lacerations.

An employee sustained second degree burns on the left side of their face, neck, arm, hand and both legs from hot oil. The employee was cleaning a slurry screen for a pump and opened the flange to check for product flow. A coke plug was present and let loose during the pulling of the screen which allowed hot oil to release and spray the employee.

An operator was injured while preparing equipment for maintenance by flushing the equipment with condensate (warm water) and flushing it into an oily water sewer system. While performing the flush, it went to the hydrocarbon sewer where it flashed and ignited. The employee suffered second degree burns to the lower face and neck region and lesser burns to his right hand.

An employee was struck in the face while blowing down a reinjection line at an oilfield production location, resulting in facial bone fractures, a hole in the roof of his mouth, tooth loss, and a big gash on his right cheek near/under the lower edge of his safety glasses. He required surgery.
An employee was using a wrench to remove pipe while standing on a stairway platform. The wrench slipped, and the employee fell off the stairway, suffering a lower back injury.
An employee was checking a collection box and lost his balance as he stood up. As he attempted to jump the front of the collection box ditch, the impact of the landing fractured his lower left leg.

An employee was tightening the nipple onto a choke manifold with a 36 inch pipe wrench. As the employee was tightening the nipple, the wrench slipped causing the employee to shift his weight to his right leg and fracture it above the ankle.

An employee was disconnecting a piece of flow iron from a pump. He was supporting the piece of pipe with his left hand and hitting it with his right hand when it suddenly disconnected. Due to the weight of the pipe, it dropped about 1 foot, catching his left ring finger between the iron and rear bumper of the pump and amputating the fingertip. He required surgery.
An employee was removing a coupling from a rotating pipe when his glove was caught in the rotating pipe. The employee's wrist was wrenched and later surgically repaired.
A rattlesnake bit an employee's left index finger while the employee was loading pallets.
An employee was moving a fluid pump into the maintenance bay when a work platform fell and struck the employee's right arm, fracturing it.
An employee was rigging down a conductor pipe. A pipe swung and struck the employee in the back as it was being hoisted. The employee was hospitalized with a back injury.
An employee was welding a trailer fender. The tire burst and debris struck the welding mask causing a facial laceration and temporary vision impairment. The injured employee was hospitalized.
An employee was seriously burned while working at a fracking fluid recycling facility, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was working independently underneath a trailer in the yard to repair a lift axle that was jammed. While the axle was rising slowly, he held onto the safety chain. When the arm had enough pressure to release itself from under the axle where it was jammed, the axle shot up, tightening the chain to the axle and amputating three of his right-hand fingers.
An employee slipped on a sloped hill at the worksite and fell onto a protruding sapling suffering a puncture wound to his right backside. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was in the process of tightening belts on an electric motor on a pump jack and was caught between the arm and the base of the motor experiencing a fractured pelvis, abrasions to left side of the abdomen, and abrasions to the buttocks.

At an oil and gas well drilling site the injured employee was standing on the well bore cover while a forklift was attempting to pick up the well bore cover. The employee fell and fractured the right fibula and lacerated the right side of the head.

An employee was unscrewing a 90 foot vertical pipe weighing 1000 lbs. from the rigging. The pipe came loose and fell onto the employee's right foot. The employee was hospitalized for treatment and the right little toe was amputated.

An employee was working on a derrick about 10 feet off the ground and was being lifted to disconnect the elevator. A wire rope under tension snapped back striking the employee and throwing him in the air and then back down. The employee was wearing a safety harness and he only fell the length of his lanyard or about 4 feet. The employee injured his back and was hospitalized.
An employee suffered a chemical exposure to his face and was hospitalized.
An employee was checking the shaker on the slurry unit when the unit caught on fire, causing 12% burns to his head, face, and neck.

An employee was trying to determine why an automatic gate was stopping and functioning incorrectly. While attempting to open the gate, the employee's left ring finger got caught inside the gate opening and was partially amputated.

An employee was performing gouging operations on the internal surfaces of a vessel when a flash fire occurred. The employee received burns to the upper chest, arms, and legs (approximately 44% of body) and was hospitalized for treatment of burns and smoke inhalation.

Employees were lifting an I-beam (approximately 1800 pounds) with a material handler to place it on a tractor trailer. The strap used in the lift broke, and the I-beam struck an employee, breaking two legs.
An employee was offloading iron from a trailer when the employee's right index finger got caught between a 4-inch iron, which fell from above, and the edge of the trailer.

A maintenance employee was unplugging a process condensate drain line. When the plug came loose, 200-degree water shot out and caused 2nd degree burns on the employee's chest, neck, and arm. He was hospitalized.
An employee was exposed to an arc flash while conducting an electrical switching procedure on an electrical panel in the tank farm. His left shoulder and hand were injured.
An employee was hospitalized for burns to the face and hands when a flash fire occurred while he was draining a gas supply vessel.

An employee was hanging a horsehead on a pump jack. As the employee swung the horsehead into place and reached up to grab the weight, the weight was released. The employee's finger got caught between metal, and the fingertip was surgically amputated.
An employee was operating a concrete coring machine. The machine got hung-up in the concrete causing the machine to jerk and the employee to fall fracturing a hip.

An employee was operating a paddle valve in an elevated lock position on the global SCM running tool. The valve self-assisted to the open position crushing his left pinkie finger between the paddle valve and the SCM running tool frame. The employee had an open laceration as well as an open fracture that was repaired at the hospital.
An employee was hospitalized after being shot in the forearm with abrasive material from a pneumatic sand blaster.
An employee was uncoupling rail cars when the wheel of a railcar ran over their left foot.

A Delaware City Refining Company employee was walking to his work location on 1/23/16, at approximately 1:00 AM during an intense snow event. As he was walking, he stopped on the side of the road to allow a snow-plowing pickup truck to pass and then crossed the street. The pickup truck reversed and its back bumper contacted the employee from behind, fracturing his femur. He was hospitalized.
An employee fell approximately 47 inches while changing an upper ram on a BOP, fracturing ribs.
An employee was removing a positive displacement diaphragm pump in the wastewater treating unit when potassium hydroxide splashed the employee's eyes and face.
An employee mistakenly grabbed a bottle of methanol, believing it to be a water bottle, and took a drink. The employee suffered from methanol poisoning.

On January 25, 2016, at approximately 4:30 p.m., an employee was completing rig service on the top drive. The service door was open and lowered with a winch. The employee was positioned on the service door, approximately 8 to 10 feet above the ground, and wore fall protection. The remote for the winch developed an electrical short, causing the winch to re-spoil. This caused the door to raise back up. The employee was pinned between the service door and the top drive, resulting in two hairline hip fractures.
While an employee was operating a drill collar clamp on a workover rig, his right pinky finger was caught between the clamp and the tubing tongs, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was adjusting the chute on the T-Belt going to the FB4K hopper resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee slipped on ice and broke his right tibia and fibula.
An employee slipped on ice and fell, hitting his head.

An employee was attempting to pump water into a natural gas line. After he was given the "all clear" sign by the pipeline supervisor, he opened a water valve and was instantly struck and injured by pressurized water. The gas line was not de-energized at the time.

An employee was getting ready to reposition portable source lights using a material lift cart. He picked up the front of the lift. As he twisted around, he turned/rolled his ankle and it gave out. He suffered torn ankle ligaments.
An employee sustained burns to the side of the face and neck after coming in contact with heavy oil while unplugging a bleeder valve.

An employee was helping an aerial access driver load multiple mobile light plants that were off-rent onto an aerial access trailer. The employee was bent down in a squat position, attempting to adjust the tongue of a mobile light tower, when the aerial access driver put his back against the rear light plant and shoved it forward. The employee's index finger was caught between the transport trailer deck and tongue of the mobile light tower, amputating the left index fingertip.

The injured employee was part of a crew that was off loading a barge of 10' scrap pipe encased in concrete. One of the joints was not lying straight, so the injured employee stood on top of the pile of pipe kicking it in order to roll it into place. It rolled into place, and when it moved, he fell and another piece of pipe rolled up onto the back of his leg fracturing it.

An employee received an injury to the right middle finger that required surgery and hospitalization. The employee's finger was caught between a pump plunger and the catwalk when the pump plunger fell to the catwalk.

An employee was helping the driver of a winch truck back up and hook up to a tank. When the driver was close enough to the tank to hook up, the employee told him to stop and set the brakes. The driver did stop and set the brakes, but the truck was still in gear and jerked backwards when his foot came off of the clutch. The employee had moved between the truck and the tank to connect the winch line and was struck causing a fracture of the right femur.

An employee was acting as a spotter for a trencher who was removing frozen soil to expose an empty conduit near a chain link fence. The stinger hit something hard underground and bounced up in the air, catching the chain link fence. This caused the teeth of the stinger to ride up the chain link fence, catching the employee's hand, which was resting on the fence. He suffered a large laceration to the palm of his right hand below the middle and ring finger, as well as a broken finger.
An employee mistakenly grabbed a bottle of methanol, believing it to be a water bottle, and took a drink. The employee suffered from methanol poisoning.
An employee was hospitalized due to an explosion at the tank battery.
An employee was stepping down from the crane operator's cab and fell to the ground, fracturing the right hip.
An employee was engaged in rigging down activities. The top drive cradle fell from the rig and struck an employee on the leg resulting in amputation of the leg.
An employee was moving a 2' base plate with a fork truck and 1/2 inch chain. He caught his finger between the fork and the chain amputating the right index fingertip.

On 2/20/2016, at around 4:00 p.m., an employee was using a machine called a planner to prep the poly pipe for welding repairs when a short burst of flame occurred. The employee received second degree burns to the side of the face and neck and was hospitalized overnight.
An employee was loading a filter into a casing while a coworker pushed the other end. The employee's fingers were pinched and his right-hand index and middle fingertips were amputated.
An employee was tightening a safety stand to a pole when the pole shifted, causing the safety stand to move and catch the employee's fingertip between the stand and pole. The fingertip was amputated.

On February 26, 2016, an employee had unloaded a load of salt water from the trailer before bringing it to the shop to help a mechanic remove bolts from the lid on the first hatch to replace the scrubber ball. They tried using vice grips and wrenches, but were unsuccessful. The employee proceeded to use a metal die grinder to attempt to remove the bolts while the mechanic walked to the tool room. Both the employee and the mechanic reported that they heard a whistling sound. At some point the vapors left behind after unloading the salt water ignited causing a flash fire. The employee's left forearm was burned.

An employee experienced an amputation of the left pinky finger while guiding a rod out of a well. The rod was sticky and grabbed the employee's gloved left hand and spun it counterclockwise resulting in the amputation of the pinky finger and dislocation of the ring and middle fingers.
An employee was using a drilling machine when a 6-inch collar fell and struck the machine, causing it to rotate and strike the employee's left leg. The employee's left femur fractured.

An employee was troubleshooting a furnace when hot condensate that had built up in the vertical muffler of a steam vent line splashed onto the employee and caused first and second degree burns to the employee's back, shoulders, arms, posterior and legs.

An employee was performing maintenance on a truck. The truck brakes were on fire and employees used a fire extinguisher to suppress the flames. The employee then began adjusting the brakes and sustained a hand injury.
An employee was trying to line up two pin holes when the pipes came together and amputated the first two left-hand fingertips.

An employee was helping unravel hose when his hand was placed in the buffer zone between the trailer and hose. His right middle finger was caught between the hose and the trailer, resulting in the traumatic amputation of his fingertip.
An employee was running pipe in a hole when his right pinky finger was caught and fractured between the wrench line and the rod.
An employee was performing maintenance on a blowout preventer when his finger was crushed by a hydraulic valve. He was hospitalized and had surgery for fractured bones in the left ring phalanges.
An employee was cleaning wet sand from the sand bin gate when the gate closed on his left hand, causing multiple fractures and lacerations. He required sutures.
An employee had replaced a clutch in a drive belt when he tripped on the concrete base and struck his left hand on the unit frame. His fingertip and a small amount of bone were amputated.

On March 28, 2016, at approximately 11:20 p.m., an employee exited his excavator and peered into the bin where he was placing additives. Wearing metatarsal gloves, the employee placed his left hand on the side of the bin. A piece of metal, used as a trough, was not secure and slid against his hand, amputating his left pinky finger down to the knuckle.

An employee was removing a pump from a truck using a forklift. Another employee was removing the last bolt from the pump on the back of the truck, when the forks of the forklift struck that employee in the back of the right leg resulting in a laceration.
An employee was hand grinding a flat piece of metal that was held in place by a vice. The piece of metal slipped out of the vice striking the employee and cutting the right side of his neck.

A rig crew was attempting to pull a drill rig through the mud using a company-owned winch truck. While doing so, the winch line separated, striking the injured employee. The employee was hospitalized with a lacerated arm and injured spleen.
An employee was performing maintenance on a D/C line when the line ruptured, creating a flash fire. The employee suffered first degree burns to the hands and face.
An employee was breaking a horse when the horse ran into the metal railing of the pen, fracturing the employee's knee.
An employee was driving a dump truck on an oil lease when the truck rolled over. The employee suffered head lacerations, a brain hemorrhage, and a bruised shoulder and thigh.
An employee was putting a filter system back into service after changing product filters when he was sprayed with sulfolane product, suffering second and third degree burns.
An employee was repairing a flow pipe when he tripped and fell backward with the flow pipe on his body. He fractured his left ankle.

An employee was transferring wax from a storage tank into a tanker truck. The employee opened a valve that was under pressure and a fire occurred. The employee sustained second and third degree burns to the face and neck.

An employee putting thread protectors on drill pipe was resting his hand on a TM-80 iron rough neck. The rough neck operator did not see his hand and started retracting the equipment, which caught the employee's right hand in a pinch point and broke a bone.

An employee was attempting to disconnect a hose from a 4-inch centrifugal pump on a rig that was under pressure. When the employee released the fittings, the hoses blew apart, spraying hot mud that burned the right side of the employee's face, neck, shoulder, and head, as well as his right arm and back.
An employee was using a ratchet wrench to tighten a bolt when the wrench slipped, catching his finger between it and a piece of steel. His left-hand third fingertip was amputated.

An employee was replacing the spring and U-bolt behind a tire. He was replacing the tire when the jack collapsed, catching and amputating the distal phalanges on his right-hand middle and ring fingers.

An employee was working on a workover rig. While the crew was running pipe in the bore hole, the employee's hand was caught between two strands of pipe. The distal phalanges of the employee's right-hand middle finger was crushed and partially amputated.

An employee was standing on the floor plate of a drilling rig when the method of attaching the floor plate to the structure failed. The employee fell 17 feet to the ground, suffering a head laceration that required surgery.

On April 22, 2016, at approximately 7:05am, an employee was hospitalized after being injured while moving a plastic water line on I-beams. The employee and a coworker were rolling a 14 inch diameter PVC pipe weighing approximately 300 lbs. and 15 feet in length across I-beam stands. During the roll, the pipe slipped off the I-beam and the employee's thumb was pinched between the I-beam and the pipe resulting in cuts and crushing injuries to the left thumb.

Employees were setting up pipe slips and the well-head ring needed to be centered. The injured employee was attempting to center the ring on the bottom of the flange. When the well flange came down, it caught his right pinky finger and smashed it at the joint. The finger was surgically amputated.
An employee was using a power wash to clean a rebuilt gas compression unit when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained 2nd degree burns on the hands, face, neck, and ears.

An employee was using a pressure washer at an oil and gas site. The water pressure was approximately 1400 psi. He lost control of the hose and the wand struck the employee's left hand causing a laceration between the thumb and wrist. The employee was hospitalized overnight.

An employee was washing up equipment located on a flatbed trailer in the wash bay. As the employee was moving around the equipment, the employee started to lose his footing and reached out and put his hand on the equipment. The equipment shifted pinching the employee's left ring finger between the two pieces of equipment. The finger was later amputated below the nail.
An employee was on the forks of a forklift installing anti-pigeon spikes on the ceiling when his finger was crushed between the forklift and a beam.

Employees laid a pump down and prepared to put a blowout preventer on the well head when one of the rods fell from the derrick and struck the ground. The top of it struck the employee on the right shoulder and neck area.

An employee thought that something was loose on the flat bed trailer, so he pulled off to the shoulder of the road. When he was getting off the trailer, he slipped and fell and broke his wrists. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was standing next to the tubing waiting for the hydrotester to go down the hole and plug in the water hose when the hydrotester broke sticking the employee on the right forearm.
An employee was moving heavy equipment on the rig floor when his left hand was caught between two pieces of the equipment, amputating his ring fingertip and the first knuckle of his middle finger.

An employee was unbolting pipe and installing a plug on valves. A crane was lifting a B-Tex condensing unit. The unit tipped over, striking the employee in the back. The employee suffered a broken right shoulder blade, three broken ribs, and a collapsed lung, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was descending a ladder and lost his footing falling 12-15 feet. The employee sustained a broken left wrist, dislocated the right shoulder and fractured the right side of his face and jaw.
While running tubing into a well, an employee was struck on the head and face by the tubing, requiring hospitalization.
While stabilizing and leveling a rig, an employee's hand was caught between the stabilizing jack and the jack stand, amputating his right ring fingertip.
While pulling a drilling pipe, the pipe broke and the jack fell onto the employee's foot crushing the steel toe portion into his foot.

An employee was delivering parts when the employee's vehicle became stuck. As the employee attempted to dislodge the vehicle, the grass caught on fire and the employee fell approximately 6 to 8 feet into a ravine. The employee suffered a second degree burn to the left forearm, a broken rib, a punctured lung, and a broken collarbone.

An employee was plumbing in a separator on a natural gas line that had pressure in it. The line blew up and knocked the employee to the ground, spraying him with dirt and rocks. He fractured his skull and suffered cuts to his arms.
An employee was removing tong dies from hydraulic tongs when the tongs engaged and broke the employee's left forearm.

An employee climbed a ladder to assess the next level of a metal roof. He stepped on a shingle and fell 8 feet through the roof to the ground, breaking his right index finger, left middle finger, right hip, and back.
An employee was injured when condensate spontaneously released while the employee was starting up a coker.

An employee hoisted the lubricator up off a well head using a winch and was inspecting the tool stream. The winch malfunctioned and continued to raise the lubricator up which was 8 feet long. It was raised approximately 15 feet off the ground. The cable snapped and the lubricator fell striking the employee and causing a laceration to his chest approximately 6-8 inches long and 1 1/2 inches deep.

A hydraulic hose/fitting separated from the hydraulic cylinder to which it was attached. In doing so, the fitting that parted from the hose struck one employee just below the left knee causing a laceration. The protective sleeve that slides over the fitting connection, struck another employee in the abdomen causing a contusion.
An employee was changing a pin on a pneumatic cylinder when the cylinder's pressure released and amputated the employee's fingertip.
An employee was steaming a pipe when steam burned the employee on both legs below the knees.

An employee was changing a flat tire on a pickup truck. While the employee was jacking up the truck, the jack slipped off, causing the truck to fall. The employee's left forearm was caught and crushed between the fender and the tire, requiring surgery.
An employee was using internal line clamps to drive the internals of piping joints when his fingers were caught between two pipes. His right-hand ring and middle fingertips were amputated.

On June 11, 2016, an employee was assisting the crew as it rigged out a crane. The crane operator was retracting the outrigger when the injured employee used his left hand to brace himself as he bent down to pick up the outrigger pad. He placed his left hand on the outrigger, and his finger entered the eyelets on the outrigger. As the outer section of the outrigger retracted into the inner section, the eyelet on the outer section amputated the employee's left middle fingertip.

A crew was pulling tubing out of a hole. As elevators were coming down, an employee grabbed the tubing elevators by the handles and was unable to push them back far enough to latch them onto tubing. The elevators hit the top of the tubing collar, causing it to shift and pinch his right index finger between the elevators and tubing bail. His finger was lacerated and fractured.

An employee was running a string of pipe from a derrick basket when his shirt was caught by the rotating torque rod. It pulled his shirt tight, compressing his chest against the derrick basket. He suffered chest bruising and lost consciousness, requiring hospitalization.
On June 15, 2016, an employee was inspecting a refrigeration compressor outside and began to feel unwell. He was hospitalized with heat stress.

An employee and a coworker were pulling packing from a pump using a plunger. The coworker used the plunger while the employee had his hand in to pull the packing. The employee's hand was caught between the tool and the packing, amputating the right middle finger.

An employee was changing the belts on a pumping unit. The employee left one bolt in place and held the 40-pound guard up with his shoulder. The guard slipped from his shoulder and lacerated his bicep, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was operating a service rig with a snubbing crew when a flash fire or explosion occurred and severely burned the employee.

An employee was working from a 10-foot platform, tripping tubing, when the elevators made contact with a stub on the next joint of tubing. The employee dismounted the platform and landed on the ground 10 feet below, breaking both legs.
An employee was lifting power tongs from a tong cradle when his finger was caught between the tongs and tong cradle. His right middle fingertip was amputated.
An employee was on a workover rig, transferring rods from the transfer and screwing them in, when his glove/sleeve became snagged on the equipment and was twisted around, amputating his left thumb.

An employee arrived at a worksite, opened the lease gate, drove the vehicle through the gate, and exited the vehicle to close the gate when the wind caught it. The employee tried to block the gate from hitting the company vehicle. The gate caught his thumb between it and the vehicle door, amputating flesh on his left thumb tip.

On June 27, 2016, at approximately 8:00 a.m., an employee was unpinning traveling blocks from a top drive when the blocks shifted and his right hand was caught in a pinch point, amputating his ring fingertip.
An employee was bitten on the leg by a rattlesnake and hospitalized.

An employee was starting up a compressor with a fitting on the hard pipe airline. The airline was loose and allowed air pressure to release and hit the employee in the face. His face became swollen and his lungs got air in them.

An employee was helping to remove sand from holding tanks during hydraulic fracturing treatment rigging breakdown. A pipe containing an auger was being used to remove sand from a tank. There was an opening at the end to allow the sand to drop from the pipe, and the employee thought the pipe was stopped up. While inspecting the opening, the employee's left-hand index finger was amputated to the distal joint and the middle finger was severely lacerated by the rotating auger inside the pipe.

An employee was pulling a rope connected to tubing when the tubing bent and the attached clamp struck him in the face and collarbone. He suffered a facial laceration and fractured collarbone, requiring hospitalization.

On 7/1/16, at approximately 6:30 PM, an employee was helping to pull tubing from a derrick rig. The employee climbed the derrick structure to attach the necessary rigging. As he descended to the working level, his climb assist became caught/wrapped in the gooseneck assembly. He was then pulled into the derrick board, breaking his tibia and dislocating his ankle.
An employee was trying to rig up a well. The employee enabled the clutch and accidently struck the emergency stop button resulting in a kick back and a broken left arm.

On or about 7/6/16, at 17:45 hours, an employee had been working outside at several oilfield locations in high heat conditions when he began feeling ill and collapsed. He was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

An employee was attempting to move a pump from an empty drum to a full drum. Once the metal cap was loosened, the pressure blew the cap into his face, breaking his nose and orbital socket and lacerating his eyelids.

Two employees were loading a port-a-potty onto the pickup truck. One employee pushed a port-a-potty causing the second employee to fall and strike their head on the ground. The injured employee was hospitalized for a head injury requiring four stitches and a possible concussion.

An employee was attempting to remove a hose reel basket from a mat that was sitting on a trailer. When the employee went around to put a pin on the trailer to prevent the mat from falling off, the operator pushed on the load, catching the employee's fingers between the mat and pin. The employee's middle finger was amputated to the middle knuckle, and his ring finger was totally amputated.

An employee was setting a bushing when the assembly began to fall. He attempted to catch the assembly to prevent it from falling and in the process caught his right middle finger between the assembly and the rig floor, amputating the finger.

An employee was moving a setting tool from the tool stand to a vise located on the back bumper of the logging unit to make some adjustments on the tool. As he was attempting to place the setting tool onto the vise, the setting tool struck the vise, causing the tool to slide down from the employee's hand. His finger slipped into a hole on the tool and a sleeve on the tool came down, pinching his left middle finger.

An employee was lighting a vessel's pilot when the vessel exploded and struck the employee, causing multiple lacerations to the employee's head and face and multiple fractures to the wrist, shoulder, ribs, and clavicle.
An employee was laying down rods that were being removed from an oil well when he began to feel fatigued and lightheaded before collapsing to his knees.

On July 12, 2016, at approximately 1:45 p.m., an employee was attempting to remove a stairway from a 100-barrel tank that was also being prepped for removal. The stairway was held to a platform by two bolts. Standing on the ground, the employee removed one bolt, which allowed the stairway to swing towards the tank. The employee was pinned between the tank and the stairway, suffering a collapsed left lung, contusion to the back and right shoulder, and friction burn to the trunk and right ear. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee slipped off the bottom rung of a truck mounted ladder and fell to the ground, resulting in a fractured right hip.

An employee was installing a security camera when the ladder he was standing on slipped out from underneath him and he fell approximately 7 to 8 feet. He fractured his fibula, scapula, and L1 vertebra.

Two employees were performing compression checks on cylinders. One employee opened the gas valve and another employee was bending over to light the starter. The gas flashed, engulfing an employee and causing second degree burns to his face, neck, wrist, and back.

While conducting well servicing operations, a rig crew was changing out swab cups and preparing to go back into the hole (oil well), when an employee had his hand pinched between a bar and the tubing resulting in the amputation of the employee's pinky finger.

Employees were picking up a mud pump using a winch and two trucks. The winch line slipped and broke causing the truck holding the pump to be raised approximately five feet off the ground and then slammed back down. The employee in the truck suffered a compression fracture in their back.
An employee was clearing brush and experienced heat stress.
An employee was rigging steel and started to experience symptoms of heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was on an oil rig handling the tubing and suffered a heat-related illness resulting in hospitalization.
While starting a pumping unit at a well site, an employee felt ill and asked for assistance. The employee was hospitalized for heat stroke.
An employee exited the rear of a flatbed semi-trailer onto an unpaved county road, and fractured his left tibia and was hospitalized.
An employee was working in an oilfield cleaning a sand hopper. He got caught in a hydraulic gate fracturing both femurs.
An employee fell 15 feet from a forklift mast while trying to put an overhead door back on its tracks. The employee sustained three broken ribs and an injury to the T9/T10 vertebrae.
While performing well servicing operations, an employee became lightheaded and began vomiting. He was hospitalized for dehydration.

An employee was on a gangway of a transloader. While preparing to load acid into a company chemical hauler cargo tanker, the employee fell from the gangway, approximately 11 feet to 13 feet. The employee was hospitalized with injuries that required surgery.
An employee was cutting an 8-inch pipe used to carry natural gas when a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's face and hands.

An employee was cutting on a damaged tank when the tank buckled and caused the employee to fall 16 inches face-first onto the concrete surface. The employee suffered a fractured orbital socket, broken jaw, and lacerations.

While conducting well-servicing operations, an employee was setting up the work floor of a workover rig. The employee slipped on loose dirt, causing him to lose his grip on the wing portion of the rig floor. The wing portion fell, landing on his left ring finger and amputating the fingertip.

An employee was working on the rig floor and tripped over an object that he just placed on the rig floor falling to the ground. The employee landed on his shoulder fracturing an arm and dislocating his elbow.
On or about August 1, 2016, an employee was helping to remove a piece of equipment from the wellhead using a crane. The piece of equipment fell and struck the employee's left leg, fracturing it.
An employee was securing a stand of drilling pipe with a chain wrench when the wrench broke and hit his hand, breaking his wrist and finger.

An employee was helping a coworker change out a plug catcher. After re-inserting the screen, the employees attempted to attach the connection. As the connection cap was pushed forward to prepare it for threading, the loose bolts on the cap allowed for significant play and crushed the employee's left thumb between the cap and flange bolts. The employee's left thumb was partially amputated below the fingernail.

An employee was completing a rig down and had finished cementing. He was attempting to remove the cement plug of the plug container by lowering the plug to the ground using a wench. The plug shifted and the employee's left wrist was caught between the drill pipe and the manifold on the plug container. The employee was hospitalized with a dislocated left wrist.
An employee was hospitalized for heat stress symptoms while conducting rig down operations.
An employee was performing tank gauging on a produced water tank. After opening the tank's thief hatch, the employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, suffering headaches and nausea.
On August 07, 2016, at approximately 10:00 PM, an employee was hospitalized due to dehydration and heat exhaustion.
An employee was bitten on the hand by a rattlesnake while turning a valve to change the flow direction. The snake was coiled underneath the tank hatch. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was laying down a power swivel when the swivel fell and fractured the employee's tibia and fibula.

An employee had attached braces to a tank using a ladder. He started to climb down and fell approximately 7 to 8 feet to the ground striking his head. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured skull and ribs.
An employee was connecting pipes on the drilling rig from the derrick position. The employee fell from the derrick to the rig floor, suffering torso injuries.

An employee was moving a 55-gallon drum off a tommy-lift to a pickup truck. The employee tilted the drum back to roll it off the lift and released the drum. The drum pinched the employee's left pinky finger between the other drum, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was connecting a pipe to a wellhead. The pipe separated under pressure and struck the employee, fracturing the employee's ribs and leg.
An employee was performing well test operations and experienced heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee climbed up onto the workover rig to secure the mast and lost his balance. He slipped and fell to the ground, fracturing his left orbital bone.

On 8/17/16, an employee was helping to remove swabbing tools from an oil well when the swab lubricator pipe fell onto his hands, amputating his right thumb and injuring his left thumb and pinky finger.
An employee's glove was caught in the tubing while making connections with tubing tongs. The employee's arms were twisted around the tubing resulting in injuries to his arms and hand.
An employee was using a pressure washer and lacerated a finger.
An employee who was troubleshooting a level transmitter was found unconscious within the vicinity of a suspected hydrocarbon (H2S) release.
An employee was servicing a deck engine to look for a coolant leak when a fan blade in the back of the radiator lacerated his left hand.

An employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion. For approximately one hour, the employee was securing a load of pipe on a flatbed trailer. Standing on the ground, the employee was throwing straps over the load and ratcheting tight.
An employee was repairing a meter run and began to experience cramping. The employee was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.
An employee fell and broke an ankle.

An employee was gauging a crude oil tank through a thief hatch and may have been exposed to vapors from the tank or oxygen depletion. The employee became ill and fell down the stairs breaking the right wrist.

The employee was reaching into a tool box and slipped and fell to the ground. During the fall, the employee grabbed the tool chain which caused the tool box lid to slam against his fingers resulting in a partial amputation of a finger.
An employee raised the bed of a truck and contacted a power line. The employee received second and third degree burns on his hands and back.
On or about August 31, 2016, an employee was disconnecting drill pipe joints in the rig and slipped and fell. The drill pipe joint came down and struck his right hand middle and index fingers.
An employee was performing maintenance on pot one of a pump. The plunger from the pot moved and injured the employee's fingers on his left hand.
An employee was struck by a pressurized 4-inch hose when it was disconnected from his truck. The employee suffered broken ribs, a collapsed lung and a right arm laceration.

The employee was tramming a sonic grip (drilling). He was operating the drill from an enclosed cab. A radiator from an engine next to the cab failed and blew out hot radiator fluid. The fluid came through the open cab open window causing second degree burns to the employee's face and head.

An employee was attempting to release tension from a 2-inch ratchet strap by lifting the lever that activates the lock/unlock mechanism. The pressurized strap released and the locking mechanism amputated his right thumb tip.
An employee was performing servicing operations at a well site when he experienced lower back pain due to water intoxication and dehydration, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was ascending a fixed ladder to maintain equipment when he fell and suffered leg and ankle injuries. He was hospitalized.

On September 07, 2016, at approximately 2:00 AM, an employee was unloading a fluid trailer during fluid service operations. While he was disconnecting a hose, pressure released and he fell to the ground, sustaining a head injury.
While disconnecting a pressurized flexible hose an employee was struck in the abdomen/chest area by the hose. The employee suffered internal bruising and fluid build up.
While climbing into construction equipment, an employee slipped and fell onto an operating handle, suffering a broken left rib and punctured lung.

An employee's arm was between two flanges, one stationary and the other being pulled by a come-along. The non-stationary flange came free and caught the employee's arm between the flanges, fracturing his right ulna. He was hospitalized.

An employee was working on a rig floor. A casing basket fell into the tongs of a nearby rig, and the tongs would not release. Both retaining chains to the tongs released and the tong movement lever activated. The tongs swung and hit an employee, pinning him between the tongs and a derrick mast. He suffered one broken rib and one bruised lung.
While climbing off a work platform, an employee lost his grip on the side rail and his leg was caught between the rail and platform. His leg was severed and required hospitalization.
An employee was walking to the rear of a truck when a piece of equipment slid and struck the employee, breaking the right leg.
An employee was moving items from one vehicle to another and stepped into a hole and fractured their lower leg.
While operating a hydraulic torque wrench, an employee dropped the remote, which activated the torque wrench. The wrench then struck the employee's right hand, fracturing the index finger.

An employee was removing clevises from under a blowout preventer (BOP). The employee retrieved the first clevis, but the second clevis was trapped underneath one of the BOPs. He lifted the BOP up and stuck the first clevis underneath to support the BOP's weight (this allowed him to retrieve the second clevis). When he attempted to lift the BOP back up to remove the first clevis, the BOP slipped and fell. His right index fingertip was caught/pinched between the two BOPs, resulting in a finger amputation.
An employee was changing a light bulb on a rig unit when he fell approximately 10 feet to the ground below, breaking four ribs on his right side and suffering a lung contusion.

An employee was driving back to the rig from the water well and ran over a rattlesnake. He got out of his vehicle and walked to the rattlesnake, which bit his right middle finger. He was hospitalized.
While tripping pipe on a derrick, an employee's left index finger was pinched between a metal beam and a driller collar, amputating the fingertip.
An employee was stung by bees while servicing a controller panel, requiring hospitalization.
An employee went to disconnect a hose for a Q10 pump when a coworker opened a discharge valve, causing the pressurized hose to strike and fracture the employee's ankle.
An employee's finger was smashed between a winch line and the tailboard of the winch truck.
An employee was working on the floor of a rig when a hinge pin became unlatched on the tubing that held the rig elevator. The tubing struck the employee, breaking the collarbone on the right side.
An employee lost his grip and fell 6 feet off a fixed ladder, breaking his right ankle.
An employee was helping to unload a 200-pound flare stack from a gooseneck trailer when the stack shifted and fell, striking the employee in the right shoulder and lower back area.
An employee was dressing a wash pipe when the chain came loose and broke the employee's leg.
An employee was walking through the lobby of the building when she fell on the left side of her hip and broke it. She was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee slipped on water droplets on the floor and fell, breaking her left hip and right ankle.

An employee was venting a container with water and condensation at an oil site when a vacuum truck at the site caught fire in the engine compartment or cab. While retrieving a fire extinguisher from the truck, the employee received first and second degree burns and required overnight hospitalization.
During rig down procedures, an employee was moving a mud tank with a tandem truck when an overhead walkway slid, hit the ground, and then struck the employee on the left knee.
An employee was pressure testing oil and gas equipment. As the employee was removing the tube/pipe, high-pressure air and water released and amputated the employee's left-hand digits.
The employee was opening a valve. The free end of a connected hose struck the employee when he opened the valve injuring his lower left leg.

An employee was helping to move a stick pipe. He was standing on the ground by the pipe wrangler and had his left hand on the pipe. The pipe skate was too close to the pipe so he motioned to the pipe wrangler operator to move the skate back. However, the skate moverd forward, pinching the employee's left index finger between the skate and the pipe. His left index finger was partially amputated.

At approximately 2:30 a.m., an employee was power washing the inside of a tanker. The employee got out of the tanker and said it smelled foul. Monitoring was done and no hazardous atmospheres were detected. The employee re-entered the tanker and approximately 10 minutes upon return he passed out. The employee was hospitalized and treated.
An employee was operating a pulling unit on a rig when he tripped on a pipe, fell, and broke his leg.
An employee received an electric shock with the wrench cable the employee was holding made contact with the power line.

An employee was attaching a connection to the wellhead for treatment when a stream of high pressured natural gas caused the following injuries to the employee: facial Injuries, right punctured lung, and a torn esophagus. The employee was hospitalized.
The worker was rotating the "setting tool" and placed their left middle finger inside the tool. The finger was amputated and the employee was hospitalized.
An employee was conducting regular maintenance of a motor on the pumping equipment. The motor was running and the employee's hand was crushed.

An employee was working on the ground aligning the bottom of a 13 3/8" casing joint into the drilling rig v-door by hand. A winch on the rig floor was lifting the joint top through the v-door. The winch line was lowered causing the bottom of the pipe to slide into the injured employee's left foot resulting in a compound ankle fracture.

An employee was stacking rods to space out a pump. His finger was caught between the polishing rod and load cell resulting in the traumatic amputation of the distal and middle phalanx at the proximal interphalangeal joint of the right index finger.
An employee was hospitalized after sustaining an electrical shock while unscrewing a light bulb on a training rig.

An employee was on the tubing platform of a production rig placing tubes in the elevators when his safety line became snagged by the tubing being elevated. The employee was lifted off of the platform until his line separated, then he fell onto the platform. The employee sustained back and neck injuries and five broken ribs. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was conducting maintenance on a gas processing unit when a flash fire occurred. The employee was burned and was hospitalized. See also 1151988.
Two employees were conducting maintenance on a gas processing unit when a flash fire occurred. Both employees received burns and were hospitalized. See also 1151826.

On October 28, 2016, at approximately 6:00 AM, a PVC pipe got clogged causing mud to overflow from the shakers. An employee went down to unclog it and when he did, the PVC pipe struck another employee, who was standing at the end of the pipe, on the neck. He was admitted to the hospital and was diagnosed with a fracture to the C6 vertebrae.
On October 31, 2016, an employee's fingertip was amputated when he was attempting to use tongs on the screw casings.

An employee was preparing to rig up a laydown truck using a rake. He was standing on top of the rake when it was activated. The rake then came back up and smashed his left foot between it and the laydown truck.
While working on a derrick, an employee's right thumb was caught between a rotator and a stuffing box during a drilling process. The first digit of the employee's right thumb was amputated.
An employee was struck by a counterweight while adjusting lines during workover rigging activities. The employee suffered facial injuries and a fractured eye socket.

On November 11, 2016, at approximately 1:30 p.m., two employees were hospitalized after receiving second degree burns to the face and third degree burns to both arms from a flash fire that occurred during a natural gas leak at a wellhead.

Two employees were attempting to clear a clog from a cellar with a water hose. As they moved the hose into the cellar, an obstruction came out and pushed the hose out. The hose whipped around, striking both employees in the face, causing lacerations and facial bone fractures.

An employee instructed a coworker to reverse a forklift so he could use the back portion as a work platform. He then cut a piece of 1/4" manila rope to use as a tagline around the protruding end of a pipe. He attempted to tighten the rope, but when he cinched down, the 1/4" manila rope broke, causing him to fall face first into gravel. He suffered two fractured left eye bones and three fractured ribs.
An employee was using a wire rope cutter and hammer to cut wire rope when a sliver of metal became lodged in the employee's eye. PPE was not worn at the time.
An employee was positioning a wind brace and connecting a mast to a work platform. He fell back on his lanyard and his upper arm was caught in a pinch point between the mast and the wind brace.
An employee was attempting to remove the shaft stock in a machine when the stock slipped and crushed his index finger, requiring surgical amputation.
An employee was refueling a passenger bus that was not properly parked. The employee slipped on ice and fell in front of the rolling rear wheels resulting in crushing injuries to the lower abdomen.
An employee was bolting up a 10 inch pipe. He put his hand under the valve and the valve and pipe rolled over his right hand and crushed it.
An employee was loading out components of a stacked drilling rig when a beam flipped over and struck the employee. The employee suffered a broken leg and fractured ribs.
An employee suffered a broken left arm when a large tool being unloaded from a forklift rolled onto his arm.
An employee was working on the engine of a compressor when a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's hands and face. He was hospitalized.

On 11/30/16, an employee was pulling pipe from a well when the pipe was released from the elevator before the arm that held it was in place. The pipe fell and struck the employee's right hand, crushing his ring finger above the knuckle and fracturing his middle finger. His ring finger had to be amputated.
An employee was working on the rig floor when a traveling block fell and struck him, fracturing his clavicle and ribs.
An employee was setting a pipe at a well site and was guiding the pipe with his hands. As he was lowering the pipe into a hole, his right index fingertip was caught and amputated by the pipe.
As an employee was walking away from the rig floor, he tripped and fell, hitting his shoulder on the drill line that was on the rig floor. His right shoulder blade suffered a hairline fracture.

An employee was unscrewing lock pins from a wellhead to remove a tubing hanger when an L-80 joint of tubing and hanger was ejected from the frac valve due to the pressure-to-weight differential. The tubing and hanger struck the employee's back, fracturing the L1 vertebra.

An employee was replacing a valve on a vacuum tank and was attempting to remove two bolts using an air grinder. As he started grinding the first bolt, a flash explosion occurred. He suffered a cut on his head; received third degree burns to his hands, forearms, and stomach; and fractured his left leg. He was hospitalized and required surgery.
An employee was tripping out rods on a servicing rig when his hand was caught above the rod transfer case near the swivel. His right arm was then caught and fractured on the rod transfer.
An employee was working on a water trailer pump that was under pressure. A part of the pump released and struck the employee in the lower leg causing a fracture.
Two employees were injured when a flash fire occurred on a rig. One employee was hospitalized with second degree burns, while the second employee was hospitalized for observation.

An employee was vacuuming mud at the bottom of a hill when the mud vacuum trailer rolled down the hill and hit him, pinning him next to a drilling unit. He suffered ankle, arm, and jaw injuries that required surgery.

An employee was drilling and installing a pipe into a large concrete digester when the flare went out, creating additional pressure in the digester. The pressurized digester gas shot through the short section of 6-inch pipe, knocking the employee 5 feet off a scaffold to the concrete floor. The employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide, stopped breathing, required CPR, and suffered a shoulder injury.

An employee was attempting to repair a small portable pneumatic barrel pump that appeared to be frozen. The employee had his left ring finger inside the pump plunger when it activated, amputating his left ring finger.
An employee was removing dunnage from under a rig when the right index finger was caught between the dunnage and the stem of the jack resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was fabricating pipe and components on a jig at a client location when the components rolled off the jig and landed on his waist and right leg. He suffered internal injuries to the abdomen and trauma to the right leg.

During rigging down of a drilling rig, two employees attempted to lift/move an I-beam by hand. The I-beam shifted and crushed one of the employee's right middle finger resulting in amputation of the fingertip/print pad.

An employee was moving a piece of iron on the bed of an iron truck, when he lost his balance, slipped, and caught his finger between the piece of iron he was handling and part of the iron flatbed truck. The left middle fingertip was amputated.
An employee was loading an empty coil tubing reel onto a trailer using a crane. The reel fell off the trailer and struck the employee breaking the tibia and fibula.
