An employee was adjusting a machine. The machine malfunctioned and its clamping mechanism closed on the employee's hand, causing a partial amputation of two fingers.
An employee was offloading hydrochloric acid (15% concentration) when the employee was sprayed in the face, suffering acid burns to the face and eyes.

A crew was coming out of a rig hole with tubing when the air backup on the tubing tongs slipped and bumped the injured employee, knocking him over a hand rail of the rig floor. He fell 6 to 7 feet head first, lacerating his forehead and breaking his left eye socket. He was hospitalized.

An employee was operating an iron roughneck while moving drill pipes when a pipe struck his fingers against the iron roughneck's control box, resulting in a partial amputation of the left ring fingertip. The employee's hand was outside the equipment at the time of the incident.
An employee was guiding a stay rod onto the body of an isolation tool when his left thumb was crushed between the tool and the stay rod, resulting in an amputation to his thumb.
An employee fell off the side of a vacuum truck while putting his belongings in the cab. He struck another truck before hitting the ground, suffering fractured lumbar vertebrae.

An employee was handling a racking board section. When the employee knocked a pin out of the racking board section, the racking board fell and hit the employee's left leg. The employee suffered a dislocated hip and fractured pelvis, requiring hospitalization. The racking board was not properly tied off at the time of the incident.
An employee was trying to re-light the pilot light on a combustor. It failed to ignite, then ignited when the door to the box was opened. A flash fire burned the employee's hands and face.
An employee was conducting maintenance activities on solids control equipment when his right hand was caught in the equipment's grinder, resulting in the amputation of his right-hand fingers.
An employee sustained a left ring fingertip amputation while opening a hydraulic tank.

An employee was laying down tubing. He reached to unlatch the tubing elevator with his right hand and his right index finger was caught between the joint of the elevator and the joint of the tubing. His finger was amputated just above the second knuckle, and he was hospitalized.

An employee was transferring from a blowout prevention structure to a man basket when he fell approximately 12 to 13 feet to the ground below, fracturing his pelvis and ribs. He was hospitalized. The employee's lanyard was untied at the time of the incident.
An employee fell from a truck to the ground while loading the bulk truck with material, suffering arm, wrist, and rib fractures.

Employees were servicing a tool and attempting to remove the pivot pins while the tool was in the horizontal position. The first employee was kneeling and facing the tool, while a second employee was operating the grab handle to remove the pivot pins. The first pivot pin was successfully removed. While attempting to remove the second pivot pin, the second employee rotated the handle from the unlock position to the lock position. He then rotated the grab handle downward. During this operation, the pivot pin came out and allowed the grab handle to rotate past its normal stop (lock position). The second employee's right middle finger was then caught between the grab handle and a weldment, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee fell from a drilling rig when its wing collapsed, landing about 14 feet below and suffering injuries to the right leg.
An employee was measuring tank levels when he slipped and fell on the slick/muddy ground. He broke a vertebra in his back and was hospitalized.

On October 27, 2018, at approximately 9:15 PM, a crew of five employees was working on a drilling rig when the traveling block hit the crown, which caused the travel block to fall to the rig floor. One employee was struck by debris from the damaged rig and suffered a fractured neck, broken left arm, and two broken ribs. Another employee jumped away from the rig structure and fell to the ground below resulting in a left foot amputation.
An employee was in a derrick, making a connection. The employee's right thumb was caught and crushed between the drill pipe and the elevator, suffering an open fracture/dislocation.
An employee was hoisting a snubbing unit with his hand on the unit and got his hand caught between the snubbing unit and the derrick resulting in amputation of the right thumb.

An employee was drilling a well. The employee's jacket was caught by the auger and the employee was pulled into the drill auger. The employee sustained a broken neck, shoulder, ankle and also internal injuries.
An employee was spotting for a track hoe when he was caught by the tracks, fracturing his right leg in three places.
A joint of pipe slipped through elevators and fell on an employee. He suffered head and arm injuries.
An employee suffered a sprained ankle while stepping off a backhoe.

An employee was pulling serial numbers off a hydraulic valve. The strap that was being used to hold the valve snapped and the valve fell, pinning the employee against a forklift. The employee suffered broken ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee was using a load brindle to load a truck. The truck rolled backward, pinning the employee against the load. She suffered a partial collapsed lung and was hospitalized.
An employee was participating in a coiled pipe cutting activity when the piece being cut sprung loose and hit the employee, fracturing several vertebrae in his back.
An employee was racking drill pipe from a derrick mans platform into a drill rack when a pipe likely swung at the top and struck the employee's head, resulting in a fractured skull.

An employee was observing as a crew spooled up a quarter-mile of 3-inch poly pipe. The tail end of the pipe caught on a bush and the middle section pulled inward, knocking the employee to the ground and breaking his right arm and leg. He was hospitalized.
An employee's foot turned in a rut in the ground, and the employee's ankle was broken.

An employee was trying to bend the top rail of a rig mat frame using a pry bar so that he could install a filler block. While his right foot was inside the frame of the rig mat for leverage, the bar slipped, and the momentum caused him to fall to the ground with his foot still in the rig mat frame. His leg was broken above the ankle. He was hospitalized for surgery on his right leg.

An employee was standing on the rig floor watching another employee operate a set of power tugs when the tugs slipped and rotated, hitting the employee. The employee was knocked from the rig floor and struck the ground. The employee suffered a fractured lower right leg and right wrist.
An employee was attempting to break up ice in a frozen water line when a fitting broke, causing the line to whip around and hit the employee's leg. The employee sustained leg fractures.

A trailer shifted while an employee was standing on it. He lost his balance, reached out to catch himself, and placed his left index finger in the pinch point of a power swivel he had been loading onto a trailer. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was operating a front-end loader to push flowback solids into the solids bay when fumes from a liquid were ignited causing a flash fire and burning the employee's face and the backside of a hand.
An employee was removing a vent plug on a pressure transmitter. Hydrofluoric acid and propane sprayed out of the instrument onto the left side of his face, causing chemical burns.
An employee was cutting wood on a band saw when the blade cut his right hand.

On 11/17/2018, at 4:00 AM, an employee was working in an enclosed trailer at a customer's location, preparing down-hole tools using a break wash chemical. He was in close proximity to a space heater that ignited the fumes from the chemical. This caused second degree burns to the employee's face, requiring hospitalization.
A process technician was taking a sample of heated resid. Some of the resid got on the employee's face, causing first- and second-degree burns.

An employee was ventilating a building containing a gas leak and the gases ignited when the employee opened the door. The employee suffered first degree burns to the face and neck and second degree burns to both hands.
An employee's hand was on a cable that was being used to lift a pipe from a rig when his finger was amputated.

An employee was moving a steel beam that pivoted on one end. When the beam reached the end of its travel, it swung back and struck the employee on the shin. The employee suffered a fractured tibia and was hospitalized.

An employee was rigging down an oil rig mast. While the pin was being removed from the derrick board brace, the derrick board swung and hit the employee in the rib area. The employee suffered contusion and fracture injuries in the rib and chest area.

An employee exited a backhoe to help other employees raise a pitman arm. As he was on the walking platform, it raised and tilted and he lost his balance. He fell and the pitman arm landed on him, breaking his pelvis.

An employee was lining up a water injection pump when naphtha and hydrogen sulfide were released. The employee was exposed and was hospitalized for injuries to the lungs. Personal protective equipment was not being worn at the time of the incident.

An employee was operating the V door on a drilling rig. The joint of the casing was brought up to the rig floor, and the employee was pinched between it and the stump. The employee suffered a bruised spleen and was hospitalized.
Employees were loading pigs onto a pig launcher when a flash fire occurred, burning two employees. Fire-retardant clothing was worn at the time of the incident.
An employee was hospitalized after drinking methanol from an unlabeled bottle.

Wire rope was coming out of the hole of a wellhead, being wound onto a counterwheel. As an employee tried to adjust the drum speed, the retracting wire caught his left ring finger. He suffered a partial amputation of the fingertip.

On 11/29/2018, at approximately 9:30 AM CST, an employee was conducting a pressure test of a plug valve manifold when a sudden drop in pressure occurred. He was going around the blast wall to determine the cause of the leak when a bonnet likely separated from the manifold and struck his leg, fracturing and lacerating it.

An employee was reaching between a blowout preventer (BOP) and tubing slips to pick up the BOP ring gasket when the chain broke on the BOP, causing the BOP to fall and crush the employee's right index finger. The employee's finger was amputated to the first knuckle.
An employee was punched by another employee causing them to fall to the floor and hit their head. The employee sustained a brain bleed.
An employee was screwing a saver sub into tubing when the employee's left pinky finger was caught between the chain and saver sub, resulting in a finger amputation.
An employee was rigging down a well servicing rig. As the derrick was lowered, it severed his right index finger and thumb under the knuckle. He was hospitalized.
An employee was working below a rig platform. A rod transfer device was dropped from the platform and struck the employee in the face. The employee sustained a fracture jaw and other facial bones.
While operating a rotary drill rig, an employee's right little finger was caught on a winch cable and amputated.

An employee was servicing a pump and replacing the plunger pump when their left hand was caught between the plunger and piston. The employee sustained amputations to the tips of the middle three fingers and the tip of the left thumb.
An employee was moving a well head blow out preventer (BOP) stack and the chains slipped, amputating approximately 3/8" of the employee's left index finger.
An employee was installing master bushings during the casing running operation and suffered a crushing injury to the left index fingertip resulting in amputation of the first digit.

An employee was guiding a rod into the tongs. Once it was placed in the tongs, the wind pushed the rod toward him. To prevent the thread from stripping, he slightly pushed the rod away from himself. Then the rod started rotating clockwise and the employee's glove became caught around the rod. His right hand fingers were pushed back, dislocating two fingers.

While attempting to reposition a long tubular with a flange welded onto it, an employee's finger became caught between the flange and the rig floor. The employee sustained an amputation to the right ring fingertip.

An employee was working on the rig removing rods with the aid of a cable. A rod hit the top of the rig and the cable broke. This caused a block to strike the upper right leg of a second employee who was in a basket. The injured employee was hospitalized with a broken leg.
An employee was assisting in hydroblasting operations and received a laceration to the left calf when the water cutting machine malfunctioned.
An employee was working on a pressure pump when his hand was caught between two pieces of steel. The right hand and fingers were broken.
While trying to isolate a valve, an employee was thrown 50 feet by a pressure release. The employee was struck on the head, suffering a head injury requiring eight stitches, and was hospitalized.

An employee was laying down tubing and guiding the drill pipe when it got hung up and jerked causing the employee to fall through an unguarded V-door from the workover rig floor to a hydraulic catwalk. The employee suffered a fractured skull.
An employee was performing maintenance on a heater treater. When he opened the heater treater door an explosion occurred. The employee sustained hand, body, and face burns.

An employee opened the electrical enclosure to do an inspection. The employee reached into the enclosure to check the incoming wiring and contacted the wiring on the top of the breaker with his right ring finger, middle finger and thumb. The employee was hospitalized for burns and electric shock.
Three employees were placing forks onto a backhoe. As the forks were slid onto the holder, an employee's finger was smashed between the forks and the backhoe. The fingertip was medically amputated.
An employee slipped while walking on tanks, suffering a broken leg.

Employees at a rig were removing a section of piping from a basket using an air hoist. The piece of piping was lifted from the basket and raised about 2 feet high, at which point a second piece of piping leaning against the same basket (called a reacher pipe) was bumped. The reacher pipe fell and crushed an employee's lower right leg, breaking his ankle. He was hospitalized.
An employee's finger was caught between a drill pipe and part of a rig structure during rigging up. The finger was partially amputated.
An employee was defrosting a valve using methanol. The valve ruptured and sprayed methanol on the employee's flame-resistant clothing, causing skin irritation.
While a line was being blown down at a gas lift well, an object struck an employee on the head. The employee suffered a forehead contusion with a possible fracture.
Two employees were on a rig, adjusting arms to line up the holes with the bracket of a power wrench. The bracket caught an employee's left index finger, causing a partial amputation.

An employee was loading casing on a rack with a PIT. One of the casings was hanging off of the rack. When the employee went to move it by hand, it rolled off and struck the employee resulting in a broken clavicle and lacerated spleen.
While working on a natural gas drilling rig, an employee sustained a partial amputation to their little finger.
An employee was refilling a tote tank that was on the back of a flatbed trailer when he lost his balance and fell from the trailer to the ground, fracturing his right wrist and requiring surgery.

An employee was troubleshooting the hydraulic system on a customer's skid to get the hydraulic pump to run. He started up the engine and an unexpected release of hydraulic energy occurred. He attempted to open the dump valve and the discharge hose exploded with his hand on it, releasing oil and severely lacerating his right index finger.
An engine backfired and ignited gas in the building, causing an explosion and fire that burned an employee's face and neck.
An employee was helping to lower an exhaust catalyst to the ground with a rope when it created a loop that caught the employees' right gloved finger, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was walking from a front office to a mailbox located outside when the employee slipped and fell to the floor at the front door. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery for a fractured right hip.

A crew was rigging down when a winch line became hung up on the operations platform. The platform then failed and an employee was caught between the rails and control panel, suffering bodily contusions.
An employee was unhooking the rig floor from the derrick when the rig floor struck the employee. The employee was hospitalized with leg and rib fractures.
An employee was walking in packed snow when the employee slipped and fell to the ground, suffering a fractured right femur.
An employee was struck on the lower left leg by two joints of pipe.

Employees were loading 6.5-inch drill collars onto a 40-foot flatbed trailer for transport. The injured employee was attempting to install a band around a collar to secure it when the drill collar rolled off the trailer and struck the employee's right foot. As a result, five of the employee's toes were amputated.

An employee was acting as a spotter and guiding a flatbed operator while standing on the rear passenger side of an outrigger leg when he stepped back onto a mobile crane platform and fell approximately 70 inches to the ground. He was hospitalized with an open fracture to the left ankle.

An employee was in a guard shack helping a second employee unload tickets and codes when suddenly the shack caught on fire. The employees exited the shack to help a truck driver and to put the fire out. At that time, the first employee received burns.

An employee was redressing a compact setting tool and had it in a vise. He put the mandrel in the sleeve and attempted to screw the mandrel onto the tool. When he let go of the mandrel with his right hand, it fell. As he attempted to catch the mandrel and sleeve, he stumbled and the mandrel struck/pinched his finger on the floor, resulting in a left middle fingertip amputation.

An employee was using a loader to place a 4.5-inch casing onto a pipe rack. The employee noticed the casing was rolling off of the pipe rack and exited the loader to stop it. The casing rolled onto the employee's left arm, pinning and breaking it.
After removing an air hose and a 1/2-inch nipple from a line that was being tested, a plug in the line hit and injured both of the employee's hands.

An employee was assisting others in rotating a canopy on a piece of heavy machinery which was to be placed where welders were working when his finger was caught between two pad eye stops. The employee sustained the amputation of the distal fourth finger on the left hand.

An employee was attaching a sucker rod "birdie" to remove rods. The employee's left hand was pinched between the sucker rod and a tong winch line. The employee suffered a broken finger and a fingertip amputation.

Employees were attempting to lift and move a cellar cover in order to install a work platform in the cellar for a welder. The cover came into contact with the blowout preventer spool, causing it to fall back. An employee's right middle finger was caught between the cellar cover and the tin horn, causing an amputation to the first knuckle.

An employee was attaching a pipe wrench to a saver sub in order to torque it to a power swivel. Once the pipe was attached, the power swivel unexpectedly began turning, causing the wrench to spin around and push the employee into the handrails on the rig floor. The employee suffered four broken ribs and internal bleeding.

A piece of plumbing was being removed from a piece of equipment (blender) between the discharge pump and the tub. The piece of plumbing slipped out of the clamp and fell onto an employee's right arm, fracturing it.
An employee was operating a pulling unit to pull rods when his finger was smashed under the rod elevator, resulting in a little fingertip amputation.

While checking on equipment on the back of a welding truck, an employee fell off the back of the truck to the ground about 36 inches below. The employee suffered multiple fractures and was hospitalized.
An employee was walking and guiding a piece of equipment on a well pad. He slipped and fell on a large containment pad, landing on the ground and breaking his right tibia.
An employee was troubleshooting a compressor when a fire occurred, burning his hands. He was hospitalized.
An employee was servicing a conveyor. He fell in a pile of sand and the conveyor caught his left hand and forearm, causing fractures to both. The conveyor was not guarded at the time of the incident.

An employee was signaling a truck as it backed up. The truck rolled back, pinning the employee's hand between a camlock union and the DOT bar (bumper). The employee suffered a fracture and dislocation of the left thumb, which was surgically amputated and reattached.
An employee was hospitalized with chest pains, headache, and nausea due to hydrogen sulfide exposure.
A pressure gauge was removed while observing a pressure survey on the crude unit and an employee received first and second degree burns.
An employee's leg was pinned and broken between a repair rack and a tool box.

An employee picked up a wear bushing that weighed approximately 50-60 pounds from a table. The employee carried it and went to set it down when it slipped. His finger was pinched between the bushing and the sub-setting. The employee sustained the amputation of his right ring fingertip.
An employee was crawling under a truck/trailer to service the water pump PTO when his arm was caught in the rotating PTO driveline, severing his right forearm and requiring hospitalization.

An employee was operating a forklift and staging 10" pipe on a concrete parking lot. The first joint of pipe was set down and the second joint was being retrieved when the first joint began to roll. The employee secured the forklift and went to stop the pipe from rolling, but was struck by the rolling pipe on the back of his leg. The employee fell and the pipe rolled up his leg. The employee suffered a broken foot.
While conducting well servicing operations, an employee's right hand was caught on a spinning rod resulting in amputation of the right middle fingertip.

An employee was attempting to grab a soil sample when he slipped and his left hand was caught in the chain and sprocket of drilling equipment. He suffered a small finger amputation and two broken fingers.

On January 30, 2019, two employees were attempting to remove a nut from the bolt of a blow-out preventer (BOP) stack with a torque-n-test. The BOP stack was lifting 1-2" with the pick up line connected to the block when the rigging shifted and came down on one of the employee's left index finger severing it at the second knuckle.

An employee was supervising as contractors erected a work-over rig on a drill site. As the floor of the work-over rig was being hoisted, a cable snapped, causing the floor to fall. When the floor struck the ground, it ejected the centerpiece of the floor, which struck the employee. The employee lost consciousness and was hospitalized.
An employee was rolling casing down a pipe rack. The employee's thumbs were in a pipe when it fell off the rack, resulting in the amputation of both thumbs.

An employee was standing on a drilling rig when a piece of guarding fell from the tower and struck the employee's head, causing a contusion to the left eye, a laceration to the cranium, and fractures to cervical vertebrae and the left scapula.

An employee was blowing down a vessel through a stinger pipe that was pointing up. As he reached with his right hand and opened the ball valve to release pressure, the stinger pipe swung to the left and struck his left elbow, causing multiple fractures.

An employee was servicing a pump and was struck by a 10 or 12-inch pressure hose that blew off piping at an adjacent job site. The employee sustained fractured ribs, a broken collar bone and a back injury.
An employee was struck in the abdomen by a skid steer.
An employee was observing the closing of the coker drum. Their right index finger was pinched when the coker drum closed causing a fingertip amputation.

An employee was putting pipe stoppers into a casing block and then onto a pipe rack when one of the casings came loose and rolled onto his right hand, smashing it and requiring hospitalization. The casing was 36 feet long and weighed 20 pounds per foot.
An employee was activating a coding machine when its chain and sprocket caught his right hand, resulting in the amputation of the distal joint of his right middle finger.

A maintenance technician was using a pallet jack to move blast doors when his right middle finger was caught in the pinch point created by the moving pallet jack handle resulting in a partial amputation of the finger.

An employee was preparing a line for maintenance work. The line contained a combination of propane and hydrofluoric acid. He was hooking up the hose to the valve to put a vacuum on the line and pull out the remaining chemicals. Before he could place the hose on the valve, residual chemicals came out and splashed his legs, causing skin burns. He was hospitalized.

An employee was standing near a winch truck that was being used to pull out a workover rig that was stuck in the mud. The winch cable was hooked to a cross member on the rig. The winch truck driver attempted to pull on the rig and the cross member welding broke. The cross member swung around and struck the employee's chest. The employee suffered fractured ribs, a collapsed lung, and a ruptured spleen.
An employee was aligning a pipe. The steel pipe slipped and struck the employee's left leg and fractured the tibia and fibula.

After a manifold trailer had been pressure-tested to 3,000 psi, a Renegade employee bled it off to 1,200 psi. The accumulator broke and struck the employee's face under pressure, causing lacerations inside and outside the mouth. The employee was hospitalized.
A sheave cable fell from the rig and struck an employee's hand causing a fracture that required hospitalization.

An employee was coming off a fracturing pump when he lost his footing and fell to the ground approximately 17 inches onto this left knee. The fall resulted in a broken left leg just below the knee which will require surgery. The employee was wearing the personal protective equipment at the time.
An employee was changing the pump at a wellsite. The line froze up and the trapped hot condensate shot out and burned the employee's right forearm.
Two employees were using a propane torch to thaw a valve on a water tanker trailer. There was an explosion and both employees were burned.
An employee was removing a pipe with a 36" pipe wrench. The employee was backing up when he slipped and fell backwards hitting his head on a rack.
An employee was standing on a wrench, trying to loosen a bolt. The employee slipped and suffered a broken right leg.

An employee was reaching for a rope when his gloved left hand was pulled into a chain and sprocket on the back of a truck. The tip of his index finger was amputated and his middle and ring fingers were broken. The chain and sprocket was unguarded at the time.

An employee was standing about 18 feet away from a 4-inch hose monitoring a pigging operation. The pig became stuck in the hose, causing pressure to build up; the hose whipped and struck the employee in the right upper arm, breaking his humerus.

An employee was removing a clamp to replace a blind. As he removed the bolts on the clamp, the blind came free, striking him in the chin. He suffered a broken jaw, a broken nose, and facial lacerations.
An employee's left hand was caught between an assembly machine and the equipment being assembled. His index finger was broken and he was hospitalized.
An employee was handling a mud pump liner when it shifted. His left little finger was caught between the liner and the mud pump and the tip was amputated.
An employee was waiting for the launched component (pig). The launch component was jammed in the pipe and when it released, his right arm suffered abrasions near the wrist and above the elbow.
Employees were cleaning out tubing to set a packer, using a tool that screwed onto a joint 25-30 feet in the air. The tool came unscrewed and fell, breaking an employee's pelvis on the left side.

An employee was preparing to nipple down a blowout preventer. The fingers on his left hand were caught between a metal door and the latch; the middle and ring fingers were amputated at the first joint.

An employee was working on piping products using a flanging and finishing machine. His left hand was caught between the jaws of the machine and the product, causing the dislocation/fracture of the middle and index fingers.
An employee sustained an amputation to his left ring finger while working on a drilling rig.

An employee was performing rigging operations at a well pad. He was walking on a containment pad walkway that was slippery from a recent rain/snow event. He slipped and fell. He attempted to catch himself during the fall and fractured his left wrist. He was hospitalized.
An employee was trying to stab a joint of tubing to make a connection. The string of tubing knocked the employee off the rig floor to the ground, causing multiple fractures.
A derrickman was trying to latch a stand of drill pipe at the derrick board. The stand pulled him off the board, pinning his left forearm against the safety gate and breaking it.
An employee suffered amputation of his right pinky finger while working on an oil rig.
At 7:45 a.m. on February 25, 2019, an employee was working as a well tender when he suffered a head injury.
An employee slipped and fell on icy ground while unloading a down hole pump off of a trailer. The employee sustained a fractured hip.

An employee was guiding the first joint of casing into a conductor in a cellar area. A centralizer (secured around a pipe) was pushed through the rotary table. The centralizer slid down the pipe and caught the employee's left ring finger against the collar on the casing. The employee's left ring fingertip was amputated.

On February 26, 2019, at approximately 1:00 p.m. a tool maintenance employee was prepping an isolation tool when a cup-shaped portion of the tool became caught on a bracket. The employee attempted to free the cup and the employee's left middle finger was caught in the hole of the cup and amputated.
An employee was flushing out the coil tubing due to a frozen line. He started hammering on the line and it broke apart. He was struck in the chest by the high pressure hose.

The rig crew was topping off the well with fluid when the operator noticed that the gauge was reading 0 psi. The rig operator leaned over the well head to check for flow inside the well head when an ice plug that had formed released from the well head and struck the employee in the face. The employee suffered injuries to his face and eyes.

An employee was trying to loosen a connection with a 60-inch pipe wrench. The wrench slipped off the pipe, spun around, and struck him. He suffered a head injury, an amputated little finger, a broken collarbone, and broken ribs.
An employee stepped into a chemical spill guard filled with water and sodium hydroxide. The chemical got into his boot, causing a burn. He was hospitalized.

On March 1, 2019, at approximately 10:30 PM, workers were attempting to rig down the gull wings of a catwalk. While removing the pins that were holding the gull wings in position, a worker's middle fingers were in holes at the bottom of the gull wings. When the pins were removed, the gull wings swung together and amputated the tips of his middle fingers below the first knuckles.

An employee was installing a protector onto a section of pipe that was being held up by a forklift. The pipe slid off the forks and caught the employee's left middle finger between the end of the pipe and another section of the pipe. His left middle fingertip was amputated. The employee was wearing impact resistant gloves at the time of the incident.

An employee was monitoring a mud pump and slipped on a slick surface. While bracing for a fall, the employee contacted a belt and pulley on a pump. His right middle finger was lacerated just above the first knuckle and the fingertip had to be surgically amputated.

Two employees were in a trailer. A lit cigarette ignited gas that had leaked from a propane tank in the trailer, causing an explosion. Both employees suffered second-and third- degree burns to the hands, arms, and face.

On March 6, 2019, an employee was assisting in rigging up. He was working from about 10 feet high when he slipped and fell, his face striking the beam he was standing on. He suffered a facial injury and was hospitalized. Fall protection was being worn at the time of the incident.

A Trinidad employee was helping pull a winch line with an attached hook through the substructure of a drilling rig. The hook snagged on part of the substructure, causing the line to tighten. The line was lying across the employee's foot, which it crushed and lacerated as it tightened.

An employee was trying to disconnect the chain from a birdbath that was still connected to the stinger of a loader. The loader began to back away from the birdbath, which was pulled onto the employee's legs. Both of his lower legs were broken.
Employees were attempting to dislodge a flow line from a hand rail. The rail came loose and fell on the employee's thumb, crushing it.
An employee was assisting with oil well rig-down when the rigging equipment failed. The employee was struck by a sheave, suffering broken vertebrae and ribs.

An employee was checking a pressure washer motor belt's tightness when the motor energized, catching the employee's right index finger in the belt and pulley. The employee's right index finger was amputated.

An employee was working at a well site where tubing was being pulled. As a block was being lowered to place a tube, the brake handle broke, allowing the block to fall down to the decking where the employee was working. The employee was struck by the block or other materials falling from about 6 to 10 feet above. He suffered a head laceration.
An employee was performing maintenance on a workover rig when the employee's left middle finger was pinched in the pin, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

On March 15, at 11 a.m., an employee was running a cable to the floor of a pulling unit when the employee was shocked by approximately 1,050 volts DC from the trailer truck. The employee was hospitalized with an electrical shock to the hands.
An employee was walking down stairs. An oil pipe fell on top of the employee, who suffered skull fractures, a contusion, and head trauma.
An employee was about to flip a breaker when he suffered a burn to his right hand.
An employee was re-dressing a setting tool. The employee's right little finger was caught between the setting sleeve and a mandrel porthole. The tip was amputated.
An employee was using a crane when a strap attached to a work bench broke and whipped back, hitting the employee in the hand and amputating the right middle finger.
An employee suffered a fingertip amputation while cleaning a machine.

An employee was manually pushing two sections of 3-inch pipe on two jack stands with wheels. One of the wheels on the stand struck a welders line (cable) and the jack stand stopped quickly and fell over. The pipe fell off the stand and struck the employee's left leg fracturing it.
An employee was checking for an air leak under a pump control stand. A pinhole leak in a hydraulic line caused hydraulic fluid to be injected into the employee's right index finger near the tip.
An employee was climbing a fixed ladder and fell approximately 5 feet to the deck then rolled and fell another 3 feet to the ground. The employee suffered 2 broken ribs and head trauma.

An employee was moving a metal plate with a crane. The plate moved/shifted while the employee was guiding it to set it down on top of another plate. The employee's fingers were caught between the two plates causing an amputation injury to the left middle, ring and pinky fingers.

An employee was removing slack from a sand line when the downhole tool hung up on a pipe scale. The tool slipped past the scale, creating tension on the line around the sand line drum. The employee's fingers were pinched between the line and the drum; his right thumb and index finger were amputated.
An employee was guiding an oil rig elevator while rods were being pulled. His right hand was pinned between the elevator and a rod and was amputated.
An employee fell from the steps of his truck to the ground below. He suffered torn ligaments on both knees.

An employee was standing behind a lowboy trailer, and attempting to unload an excavator. His left hand was underneath the winch cable when the winch line activated, pinching the employee's left index finger between the roller and winch cable. The employee's fingertip had to be surgically amputated.

An employee was adjusting a hydraulic torque wrench to attach a fluid end when a second employee engaged the high torque controls, resulting in an amputation of the first employee's right middle finger.

An employee was assisting a forklift driver with moving flanges. The last flange fell over. The employee walked over to stand the flange up. The employee picked up the flange and it slipped from his hand. The employee's left ring finger was crushed between the flange and a pallet and amputated.
A well tender was putting methanol in a dump-line when the nipple broke off the line. Methanol sprayed into the employee's face and eyes; the employee was hospitalized.

An employee was applying pipe dope to a thread on a tool joint. His left hand was caught between a lifting sub and elevators, causing crushing injuries that led to the total amputation of the pinky and ring fingers and partial amputation of the middle finger.
An employee was conducting maintenance on a free pump when the pump amputated the employee's left middle fingertip.

An employee was holding a flashlight for another employee who was doing maintenance on a downhole sucker rod pump. The second employee was installing a plunger back into the rod pump, using a pry bar. The bar slipped and the plunger was propelled out of the pump toward the first employee. It caught his right hand and carried it downward, pinching the third finger against the fender of the pump. He suffered an avulsion and partial amputation of the finger.

An employee was adjusting the installation of a PDC drill bit on a horizontal grinding machine. The grinding wheel started and his right glove and index finger were pulled between the wheel and the surface to be ground. He suffered a partial amputation of the finger.
An employee was pressure-testing a valve outside when it broke and struck his left leg, fracturing his pelvis and lower leg.
Employees were swabbing a well when a lubricator came down and smashed an employee's left index and middle fingers. The fingers were amputated.
An employee had been attaching barricade tape when their right foot was fractured by a crane's outrigger.
Two truck drivers got into a fight; one suffered injuries to both eyes and was hospitalized.

An MWD tool was being picked up with an air hoist. As it was being lifted and was about 8 feet off the ground, it slipped out of the lifting clamp and fell onto an employee. The employee suffered bruised vertebrae.
An employee was unloading a tractor trailer. The load became unstable while the chains were being removed; the employee fell off and was struck by a pipe rack, suffering injuries to both legs.
An employee was transferring chemicals from a chemical tote into a tanker truck when the hose whipped out of the tote and struck the employee on the chin. The employee's jaw was broken.
The cap blew off a camlock, striking and breaking an employee's right hand.

Employee was cleaning with a power washer when his foot became stuck in the mud. As he tried to pull it out, his boot came off, causing him to lose balance and activate the power washer. The power washer then amputated a toe.
An employee was exiting a vehicle to fuel up when his finger was caught in the pinch point between the driver's side door and a metal post, resulting in an amputation to his right ring fingertip.
An employee was cleaning out a frac tank when a tube came into contact with the opening on top of the tank. The employee's right index finger was crushed, and the tip was medically amputated.

An employee was unloading material from a trailer. When the employee cut the load strap, some pipe rolled off the trailer and onto the employee's legs, breaking the right tibia and dislocating the left knee.
An employee was removing casing. The casing swung from the rig and struck the employee's right index finger against the rig tongs, smashing the fingertip. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was conducting well-servicing operations. He was attempting to guide a rotating rod away from a winch line when the spinning rod, which was covered in paraffin, caught his gloved left hand, amputating the pinky finger near the knuckle.
An employee was vacuuming catalyst inside a confined space. A piece of the catalyst rolled down from the pile and struck his leg, breaking the femur. He was hospitalized.

An employee was setting stairs onto a rig platform when the stairs became disconnected from the rig platform, causing the employee to fall 6 feet from the platform and be struck by the stairs. The employee was hospitalized with four fractured ribs.
Broken test tools came free after being stuck inside tubing on a workover rig. They struck an employee, breaking the employee's foot.
An employee was on a scissor lift using a manual 2-inch hand threader, threading a piece of pipe to put a valve on. He strained his back, suffering a herniated disk.

An employee was bleeding down injection lines, using a 36-inch pipe wrench, to let hydrates thaw overnight. A valve was opened and pressure (about 900 psi) was released, causing a section of pipe to come loose and strike the employee's leg above the knee. He was hospitalized.

On April 19, 2019, at approximately 9:00 a.m., an employee was breaking down pipe with a sledge hammer when he threw out his back and experienced lower back pain. He was hospitalized with a herniated disk at the L4 and L5 vertebrae.

An employee on the walking beam of a pumping unit had just removed the horse head of a pump jack when a bolt on the beam broke and the beam tilted over. The employee slid down the beam until he hit a motor at the bottom of the pumping unit and fell to the ground approximately 6 to 7 feet below. He was hospitalized with a head laceration and left leg laceration.
An employee was on a mud pump skid, on his hands and knees, searching for a pin that had fallen. A tool fell onto the employee's right little fingertip, amputating the tip.

An employee placed his right hand on a stack of pipes to stabilize himself to step up onto a platform. The piece of pipe slipped and rolled, pinching his right pinky finger between two pieces of pipe. His fingertip was amputated between the nail and first joint.
An employee's left index finger was amputated between two pieces of metal on a portable generator.

An employee was tightening the packing bolts on a beam pumping unit in the oil field by using an air impact wrench when the head of the unit, while in a down stroke, came in contact with the impact wrench forcing it downward and mashing the tool against the left index finger. The employee sustained a partial amputation of the left index fingertip.
An employee was attempting to change tong heads when the tongs activated and amputated his left thumb.
On April 23, 2019, an employee was testing the voltage on a 34.5-kV, 4160/2400 step-down transformer when an arc flash burned the upper right part of his body. He was hospitalized.
An employee was using a power swivel to connect pipe when the employee's hand was caught between the swivel and a chain, resulting in finger amputations.

On April 29, 2019, at 4:30 p.m., an employee was assisting with the final pass of torqueing the hydraulic torque wrench when the tip of the employee's glove got stuck between the nut and the tool. The tool engaged and the employee's ring fingertip was amputated.

An employee was removing a pressure relief valve from a mud pump with a 36-inch pipe wrench. The pipe wrench slipped and caught the employee's finger between the wrench and the mud pump resulting in amputation of the left middle finger and a fracture to the ring finger.

The injured employee was working on the catwalk pedestal of an oil and gas drilling rig. While lifting a single joint of drill pipe, it fell out of the elevator and came down on the injured employee's left hand which was on the handrail. The employee sustained lacerations, fractures and nerve damage to the left hand.
An employee was installing cable. A saddle fell and hit him knocking him backwards. He landed on a rock on his back and suffered a spine injury.

A crew was in the process of tripping pipe back into the well bore. The elevator failed to latch properly allowing the pipe to fall approximately 4 feet back down to the matting board. The stand of pipe bounced off the matting board and struck an employee who was working on the ground on the right foot resulting in amputation of the fifth metatarsal.

An employee was going to heat up a burrito in the dog house (work trailer). When the employee went to turn on the stove/cook top, a flash fire occurred due to gas accumulation. The employee sustained burns to the face and neck, and had second degree burns on both hands.

The injured employee was standing next to the drilling piping, holding material over the pipe joint to channel residual mud downward, ready to swing the disconnected piping out of the way. Oil-based drilling mud came out under pressure and three employees got mud in their eyes when their hard hats and safety glasses were blown off. One employee was hospitalized for an eye injury. The eye was burning, swollen and the employee was unable to see.

An employee was connecting elevators to pipe. He slipped on the wet muddy floor and while trying to catch himself, his right ring finger was caught between elevators and a tool joint at the moment when the driller was going to pick up the elevators. His finger was smashed and partially amputated.

An employee was removing a three-inch diaphragm pump from a storage room in the accumulator house. After placing the diaphragm pump onto the ground outside the storage room, he tripped on a board protruding out from under the right side of the accumulator house and fell to the ground knocking the pump onto his right calf muscle and crushing it.
An employee was cutting coil tubing with a handheld band saw. The tubing swung back and lacerated his knee.
An employee had been operating a pumping unit at a salt water disposal facility when a fire/explosion occurred. The employee sustained third degree burns to 60 percent of his body.
An employee removed the radiator cap and was sprayed in the face by hot liquid. The employee suffered burns to the face.
An employee was assembling a separator vessel onto a concrete slab when the vessel became unstable and fell onto the employee's right leg breaking it.

The injured employee was holding a cart carrying a 10' section of drilling pipe. A crew attached a snatch block to the section of pipe to lift the piece and connect it to the rig to continue digging deeper. As the crew began to lift the section of pipe off the cart, dirt had accumulated on the chain causing the pipe to fall around 6 inches and crush the injured employee's right hand between the cart and the pipe. The employee suffered fractures and lacerations to his fingers.
On May 9, 2019, an employee was stepping down from a work platform when a forklift drove by and pinned his leg between the platform and the forklift tire. His leg was fractured.
Employees were preparing to unload material with a crane. When the front outriggers were extended it contacted an employee's right foot resulting in a crushing injury and great toe amputation.

An employee was power washing the top shed of the shakers approximately 8 feet above the lower level. As he was transferring to the ladder to leave the shed top, he fell and struck his head on the tank's metal grating. The employee suffered a torn muscle in the neck and a concussion.

An employee was setting up a board over a 3-foot deep excavation so that he could access the control valve to stop a leak. The employee fell into the excavation that was filled with hot water and suffered burns to the feet, leg and knee.
An employee fell back and struck his head on the ground after a faulty control valve back fired.
On 5/14/2019, an employee fell down stairs and fractured the right ankle, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was lifting a 5,000-pound steel plate with a small ground hoist that was rated for 7,500 pounds. The plate suddenly lowered down onto the employee's lower leg, causing him to fall to the ground. The plate rested on the side of his right foot, resulting in two bone fractures. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
Two employees were welding pipe when the 9x9 steel welding hut blew over due to a microburst. One employee was hospitalized for a fractured leg and hip.
An employee was replacing an adjustment pin on a tail bearing and amputated the left middle finger.
An employee's gloved finger was caught while aligning a swivel causing a fingertip amputation.
An employee was injured during a filter change when the filter caught fire. The employee was hospitalized with first and second degree burns to the hands, neck and face.
An employee was working on the controller drive for the down hole equipment when he received an electrical shock, resulting in burns to the right thumb and left forearm and face.
An employee opened a bleed down valve and was struck by the bleed down line in the head and shoulder causing a laceration over the right eye and injury to the right shoulder.

An employee was working with another employee on top of an oil storage tank at a field site, dismantling piping and attachments to the tank. They had removed a piece of 4-inch vent piping and were attempting to throw the pipe to the ground. While they were throwing the pipe from the tank top, the pipe caught the harness of the injured employee, causing him to fall 15 feet to the ground. He broke his right wrist and pelvis. The employee's fall protection harness was not tied off at the time of the incident.

An employee was changing out a mud motor on the directional drilling rig. To make sure the motor was aligned, the employee did a bump test with a wrench. The wrench then swung and hit the employee in the hard hat, causing a small fracture to the head and slight bruising.

While conducting fracking operations, an employee was digging out sand from the auger to a blender when the auger released and struck the employee's left middle finger, resulting in a laceration and amputation of the fingertip.

Employees were replacing a gasket on a well head that was tied to a crane. When they removed the bolts from the flange, the well head tipped over and fell onto the injured employee. Both of the employee's shoulder blades (scapula) were fractured as well as multiple vertebrae.
An employee was handling a tag line for a unit assembly when the employee fell approximately 5 feet and suffered a back injury.
An employee was serving as the spotter while iron was being offloaded from a loader. The iron struck him, causing fractures to the face and jaw.
An employee amputated a fingertip while using a hydraulic cylinder and wrench to remove a nut from a blow out preventer.
An employee's foot was caught between a metal storage rack and a 6-inch beam that a forklift was pushing. The employee's left ankle was broken.
An employee stepped down from an uneven surface and fractured their right tibia and fibula.

At about 10:30 a.m. on June 3, 2019, an employee was on an oil rig that was being rigged down. As the rig was reaching half mast, the employee was on the rear of the rig, placing the weight bucket onto the storage hook. As he dismounted the rig, he lost his footing and his right hand was caught in a pinch point between the top and bottom sections of the derrick mast as it came down. He suffered injuries, including an amputation injury, to the index, middle, and ring fingers.

On June 4, 2019, at approximately 11:45 AM, an employee was judging the weight of a piece of metal (solid slag metal for centrifuge) by lifting it. The metal piece slipped and fell catching the employee's left index finger between the metal and the ground or pallet jack and caused a fingertip amputation.
An employee was sandblasting from a scaffold. The scaffold fell and the employee struck the ground, suffering broken vertebrae.

An employee was at the side of a truck (a pulling unit) removing tools. As the pole on the unit was extended, the elevator came unclasped off the hook, fell, and struck the employee on the side of his head. He suffered a skull fracture.

An employee was assisting with removing the chain tongs from the drill string. The chain struck his finger and pinched it against the drill head. The employee was hospitalized with a broken finger. The employee was wearing impact gloves.

Employees of ExxonMobil Global Projects along with another contractor employee were in an office trailer conducting office duties when a tornado hit the trailer causing destruction of the trailer and laceration and fracture injuries to the personnel inside.

An employee was performing maintenance on a wireline tool that was hooked up to a control panel. He closed a panel on the tool with a command at the control panel. As the panel was closing, he was turning the tool and his fingers were caught in the backup shoe of the tool resulting in an amputation injury.

An employee was helping a vacuum truck operator during pigging operations when a fitting broke, allowing the vacuum hose to whip and strike the employee's heel. The employee suffered a left heel contusion.
An employee was working outside in a rail car cleaning process area. The employee began to suffer heat-related muscle cramps and was hospitalized.
An employee was reinserting a burner tube into a separator when his left index finger was caught between the tube and separator, amputation the top half-inch of his finger.

An employee was standing near the front of a loader carrying pipe. Several pipes rolled off the loader and one of them struck the employee's right foot, rolling up his leg and causing a fracture of the lower leg.

An employee was on a man basket near the wellhead on an oil and gas rig. The employee was screwing an entry guide onto a blowout preventer while a crane was removing it from the wellhead. The lubricator/blowout preventer moved and caught his right middle and ring fingers between the entry guide and the cap on the frac head. The middle finger was amputated and the ring finger required surgical treatment.
An employee was climbing down the steps of a pump trailer when he slipped and injured his left knee, resulting in a torn patella tendon.
An employee was using a pinch-off tool when the tool struck his head/jaw.

An oil rig floor hand was connecting elevators to a lifting sub. When the elevators were lifted, the floor hand's right middle fingertip was crushed between the elevators and the lifting sub. The fingertip was surgically amputated.

An employee was teaching another employee how to operate a backhoe. He was standing on the top step by the cab when the other employee hit a rough area. He then fell off the backhoe to the ground, breaking his left upper femur just below the pelvis area.

An employee was working 4 to 5 miles offshore on board a utility vessel and helping to retrieve a box core (device that goes to the bottom to scoop sediment) when his fingers were caught in a 24-volt winch, resulting in the partial amputation of his left ring finger.
An employee was removing a transducer when high pressure fluid struck his hand, penetrating his skin.
At 10:00 p.m., on June 19, 2019, an employee was helping a coworker line up a flange prior to bolt-up when he lost his footing and fell to the ground, fracturing his femur. He was hospitalized.

An employee was disassembling a guardrail on a rig floor when his safety harness became caught on the guardrail and the weight pulled him down to the ground, breaking his left leg. He was hospitalized.
An employee was struck by a company vehicle while taking out the trash, suffering a knee injury.

An employee was approximately 1 foot high on an uneven surface, removing the cross-over pin from a casing collar, when the employee slipped on the uneven surface and fell to the ground. The employee fractured the first four vertebrae.
An employee was bitten on the left thumb by a snake while picking up valves to discard them.
An employee was threading pipe that was chained to a winch when the chain lurched and caught four of the employee's left-hand fingers. The employee suffered four broken and de-gloved fingers.

Two employees were moving a 2-inch iron pipe to their acid pump truck when the injured employee's right ring finger was caught between the pipe and the pipe rack it rested on. He suffered an open fracture to the fingertip.
An employee was attaching a casing ring tool to an overhead crane when the employee's left middle finger was caught between the hook and the pad eye amputating the finger pad.
An employee was assembling a wire line gun. His finger was pinched between the gun and a workbench causing an amputation to his right ring finger.

An employee was pumping chemicals in a hot oiler pump truck. A chemical reaction caused an explosion that propelled the employee into the back of another vehicle. The employee suffered facial contusions.

An employee was standing on a ladder trying to remove an anode when the anode struck him and he fell 4 feet off the ladder onto a dirt berm. He landed on his right waist area and was hospitalized with kidney and liver lacerations.

An employee grabbed a drilling line that was being used to lift gin poles and the line pulled the employee's hand into the top sheave of the gin poles, smashing four of his left-hand fingers at the mid-knuckle and resulting in an amputation.
An employee was working on trucks when his shop rag ignited from a spark, causing his clothing to catch on fire. He sustained burns on his arms and legs and was hospitalized.

An employee was fitting/welding on a structural type weldment while standing on a ladder approximately 3 to 4 feet off the ground. The employee stepped off the ladder and onto the weldment. The weldment then became unbalanced and fell to the ground. He suffered a fractured left shoulder and broken left ankle.
An employee was flagging a forklift driver when metal slag broke off a piece of steel being welded and hit the employee in the leg, causing a fracture. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was attempting to close a manual valve after flushing a hydraulic choke. When the manual valve would not close, he went to retrieve a tool (wrench) to help close the valve and tripped over a flow line. He fell to the ground and broke his left arm.
An employee was removing thread protectors and was caught between two joints of pipe. The employee suffered four broken ribs and was hospitalized.
An employee was changing the elevated blade on a bulldozer when the blade slipped, resulting in a full left middle finger amputation.
An employee was guiding a load being lifted by a crane. The employee's right little finger was caught between the crane hook and the load and partially amputated.
An employee was hospitalized after being struck in the head by a falling pipe.
An employee fell 20 feet from a mast to the ground, suffering a broken wrist.
An employee was welding on a pipe bracket between a pumphouse and tank batteries at a salt water disposal site. A flash fire burned the employee.

An employee was performing maintenance on a natural gas compressor. He was turning over an engine by barring over when his left pinky finger was caught between the bar and the guard for the bull wheel. Two centimeters of the tip were amputated.
While removing a power swivel and tank from a drill site, two employees sustained chemical burns on their legs from an unknown caustic chemical.

Two employees were traveling in a UTV on a gravel road. The UTV slipped off the road. While it was being maneuvered back onto the road it slipped and hit a tree. The driver was ejected and suffered a broken femur and knee damage; the passenger suffered fractures to the ankle and arm and a head laceration. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was cleaning the rig floor and felt sick from dehydration.
An employee was working on a drilling rig as a pipe was being raised out of the hole. The pipe struck the employee resulting in hospitalization for broken ribs, a punctured lung, and a broken back.
An employee was washing the shaker screens when he felt short of breath and light-headed. The employee was hospitalized with pneumonitis that was induced by diesel fuel inhalation.
An employee started working from an aerial lift after returning from lunch when he started to feel ill. The employee was hospitalized for heat stroke.
An employee was using a tag line on a pipe with a sling. The pipe slipped out of the sling and pinched the employee's hand between the pipe and the pipe stand resulting in smashed fingers.
An employee was standing on a pipe rack and fell 3-4 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fracture to the T3 vertebra.
An employee was cleaning a tank of sand using a high-pressure water hose. The high-pressure water ran across his right foot and cut the big toe.
While walking to the back of the building, wet ruts caused an employee to stumble and fall to the ground. The employee sustained a broken thumb.

An employee was completing a fluid treatment process. The employee had just closed a 4-inch valve on a "T" manifold when he tripped and fell forward, striking the shin of his right leg against a valve handle and then landing on the ground. The employee's right leg sustained a spiral fracture requiring hospitalization and surgery.

A wireline operator was rebuilding a hydraulic setting tool. He finished rebuilding the bottom section of the tool and noticed it was partially stroked out. He went to use the weight of the setting sleeve to finish stroking the tool vertically. His finger was in the hole at the end of the setting sleeve and when he hit the ground with the tool, it stroked and amputated his right ring fingertip.
An employee experienced heat stress.

An employee was getting ready to place a pin in the rod basket. The employee slipped and fell approximately 14.5 feet from the top of the derrick to the ground below and sustained a fractured skull, fractures to the face, and a fractured right hand.

An employee was working to remove a broken bolt out of the top drive unit. While removing the swivel/quill, it shifted and fell back into place causing the partial amputation of his left index finger.

An employee was waiting for a crane to bring him lifting chains so that he could attach them to a compressor being swapped out at an oil well site. He lost his balance and struck a muffler, which his fall protection was tied off to; the muffler fell to the ground and carried him with it. He suffered broken ribs and was hospitalized.

An employee was moving hoses on a frac spread. He had the hoses over his shoulder when residual biocide from one of them flowed onto his shoulders and back. He later lost consciousness and was hospitalized to treat dehydration and skin rashes.
While being cut, a 20-inch metal pipe separated and a section struck an employee's lower right leg, causing broken bones.

An employee was checking on an in-service gas well because the gas had stopped flowing. As hot water ran through the system to melt built-up paraffin, the cap blew off the pipe and the hot water sprayed the employee's face. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was closing a 2-inch ball valve on a test separator to make repairs to the down side of a low-pressure sand knockout. The employee was about 2 to 3 feet from the ball valve as he closed it; when he got the valve three-quarters closed, the bell reducer pipe on the back side of the ball valve separated in two, releasing pressure in the test separator. The employee suffered sand blast burns to the left side of his body, a broken arm, a sprained ankle, a fractured back vertebra, and a head laceration.

An employee was manually lighting burner boxes on hot oil trucks. When using a cigarette lighter to ignite a pilot burner a liquid propane gas flashback (woof) occurred and the employee suffered flash fire burns to the face and lungs.

An employee was using an electric jackhammer to break up rock under a pipeline. Flammable gas reacted with the electric motor of the jackhammer, causing a flash fire. The employee was burned on the forearms and face.
An employee was pressure washing a rig when the employee began to see spots and experienced dizziness due to dehydration.

An employee had climbed onto a plasma cutter table to retrieve cut-outs. While the employee was stepping off of the plasma table, part of the grate bent, causing him to fall and hit his head on the plasma track. He suffered a large laceration on top of his head.
An employee was using a pipe wrench to tighten a fitting when the wrench amputated his little finger.

An employee was assisting with services related to cementing (closing) an oil well when a valve detached from the wellhead under pressure. Part of the valve hit the employee's legs, fracturing the left tibia and fibula.
An employee was operating tongs when the tongs lacerated the employee's right thumb.
An employee was moving a sub into a sub box when the sub structure crushed his right thumb.
An employee was pressure washing a roll-off box when the employee contacted the pressurized water, suffering a left foot injury.
A hose, pressurized at 9,000 psi, ruptured while being tested. An employee's left tibia was injured.
An employee was changing a condensate filter. A fire erupted, burning the employee's arms, legs, neck, and face.
An employee was hydroblasting the tubes in a spare condenser with a lance. As he moved the lance from one tube to the next, the lance engaged, jumped back, and lacerated the employee's right hand.
After working the day shift cleaning and repairing a compressor at an oilfield site, an employee began to exhibit signs of illness. The employee was hospitalized with a possible heat-related illness.

An employee sandblasting a pipeline. The sandblasting medium was not blowing well, so he approached the compressor; when the hose was disconnected, the machine sandblasted his left hand. He was hospitalized.

An employee was transferring a stabilizer from a forklift to a catwalk. One end of the stabilizer slid off the catwalk and fell onto the employee's lower left leg. The employee's tibia and fibula were broken.

An employee was removing the catwalk on a tank battery. The catwalk tilted down and the employee's fall protection came off; the employee fell about 20 feet, suffering knee injuries and a head injury requiring a stitch.

An employee of Aries Wells Service was visually and physically inspecting a tubing line. He glove got stuck on the line and his right index finger was pulled into the drum, which pinched it, removing skin. He was hospitalized and the finger was medically amputated.
An employee was at an oil rig. The line he was tied off to was cut, and its weight pulled him down to the rig floor about 12 feet below. He suffered a spleen injury.

An employee was assisting a customer to position a shaker basket on a shaker skid utilizing a forklift operated by the customer. Three of the employee's fingers on the left hand were caught and injured between the shaker basket and the cross support of the shaker skid.
On August 19, 2019, an employee was riding on an ATV to check leaks in pipe lines when the ATV flipped over in a washout. He was hospitalized with eight fractured ribs.

An employee was holding the guide wire rope of a rig that was being relocated. The employee walked into the loop of the guide wire over the base beam as a cable moved forward and was caught between the base beam and the loop of the wire, breaking the left lower leg.

An employee was helping to assemble scaffolding near a fluidized catalytic cracker at a refinery. He began having heat-exposure-related symptoms. He was hospitalized and treated for low electrolytes and dehydration.

An employee had just replaced a rubber O-ring on a manifold and was trying to put the bull plug back on the missile when it slipped off and took the employee's hand down, striking it against the flat metal plate below. As a result, the employee suffered a partial fingertip amputation.

Two employees were capping off an old gas well when the pressure of the well reached a high level and the well head blew off. One employee sustained fractured facial bones, contusions and burns to the chest, and shrapnel in the skin of the lower and upper torso.

Employees were at site to plug a well and were pulling casing from the well and laying them on a skid. An employee who was standing on a metal bench/stool lost his footing. The case fell off the rack and struck him in the right leg, breaking his tibia and fibula. He was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee was setting up a flange machine during training. The machine shifted, pinching his right hand against the flange. The hand was broken and lacerated, and he was hospitalized.

An employee was in a forklift that was stuck in mud. A truck was pulling the forklift with a chain to get it out of the mud when the chain broke and snapped, hitting the employee who was in the forklift. The employee suffered fractured ribs and a fractured shoulder blade.

Employees were moving a pipeline inspection tool barrel. The injured employee was pulling on the rigging in order to allow a forklift to move the barrel through an open door. As the barrel was coming through the door, the rigging slipped off the fork and the barrel landed on the employee's foot. The employee's two left toes adjacent to his big toe were amputated.

An employee was using a bench grinder to clean up 2-inch sub assemblies when his right index fingertip was caught between the grinder and the workpiece, resulting in a fingertip amputation at the knuckle.
An employee's fingers were pinched in tongs, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was delivering well parts at a worksite. A flash fire burned the employee's upper body, back, arms, and head.
An employee was setting a 90-degree elbow while another employee operated the crown. The block dropped and crushed the employee's right hand.
An employee was cleaning a semi-truck engine when his right arm caught on fire, sustaining second or third degree burns.
An employee was helping another employee lower a platform on the side of a pump. A pivotal latch caused the amputation of the first joint of his left little finger.
An employee came in contact with process fluid at a petroleum refinery. The employee suffered burns to the right arm and torso and was hospitalized.

While a crew was completing a casing connection, which involves pieces of pipe being torqued together, an employee's fingers were caught in the top drive wheel. The employee's right middle finger was amputated, and the index and ring fingers were lacerated.
An employee's hand was inside a derrick girder when his hand was struck and fractured by the rig's top drive.
While operating a pump, an employee's left thumb tip was amputated.

An employee was using an oxygen acetylene torch when its flame went out. He turned off the oxygen supply to the torch. The flame then returned and the torch's hose separated, causing a large flame that caused second-degree burns to his arms and abdomen. He was hospitalized.
A rattlesnake bit an employee. The employee was hospitalized.
Employees were pulling slips while running drill pipe in a well bore. An employee suffered a hernia.
An employee installing insulation on the top of a treater shack fell approximately 8 feet from the top of the treater shack to the ground. The employee sustained fractured ribs and neck vertebrae.
A crew was using a pump to circulate fluids to a tank when there was a release from a well and a flash fire occurred. Two employees suffered burns to the face and body, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was travelling down a public road in a telehandler. When the employee pulled to the side of the paved road to allow vehicles to pass, the tires on one side went off the pavement and the telehandler rolled over. The employee sustained an amputated foot, broken legs, a broken pelvis, and a punctured lung.
An employee was checking the belts on a pumping unit. The unit came on, catching his thumb. The employee sustained the partial amputation of his left thumb.
An employee was working as a floor hand in support of an oilfield operation. He became ill from heat stress and was hospitalized.

Two employees were rigging up centrifugal equipment. One employee was on the solids control equipment stand when it gave way, causing him to fall and sustain three fractured ribs and a punctured left lung. The other employee was on the ground near the stand when it collapsed, resulting in a fracture to his lower left leg.

An employee was circulating bad oil into tanks. He then went to remove a leaking dump valve from a compressor to conduct repair. While the dump valve was being removed, fluids sprayed out and were ignited by the hot manifold of a compressor. The employee sustained second degree burns to the palms and top surface of both hands and was hospitalized.

Employees were rigging up a work-over rig. One of the rig wires caught on a 1-inch ball valve and the pressure from the rig rising caused the valve to be sent up as a projectile. It struck an employee on the right side of the face and forehead, fracturing his skull. He was hospitalized.

An employee was standing on the floor of a drilling rig while hooking up a Kelly hose to a pipe. The hose struck him below the left shoulder blade, and he rolled off the rig and fell to the ground. He suffered kidney trauma, broken ribs, and a liver laceration.
An employee was servicing a compression unit. When he began to shut the unit down, a flash fire occurred. He suffered primarily first- and second-degree burns. He was hospitalized.
On September 16, 2019, an employee was operating a telehandler when it went off the road onto its side. The employee suffered several face and head injuries.
An employee was on a ladder when a wasp attacked him. He fell backward from the ladder and suffered broken ribs and an abdominal injury.

An employee was hooking the trailer to a pickup truck. Some of the weight of the trailer came down on the employee's left index finger, crushing it against the hitch ball. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was coming down a wireline truck ladder. As he stepped down, his ankle rolled and he fell to the ground. He landed on and broke his right femur, and was hospitalized.
An employee was pulling tubing at a well site when an object fell off the derrick and punctured the employee's leg.
An employee was helping re-spool the winch line on a tubing tester truck when the line caught his right hand. Four fingers were amputated.

While performing a break-out and disassembling equipment on-site, an employee removed the meter cover. Then, while removing the bypass blades with pliers and a screwdriver, the screwdriver contacted the meter box, causing an arc flash. The employee sustained second degree burns on his face, chest, and left hand, and sustained a second/third degree burn on his right hand.
An employee was unstrapping a pipe rack when it fell over on the employee, who suffered fractured vertebrae.
An 18-inch pipe rolled off the forks of a loader when the clamps were lowered. Two employees' legs were pinned between the pipes.
An employee was loading well pipe into a trough when it bounced and dropped on his right index finger. The finger was amputated at the first knuckle.
An employee was helping install an aboveground storage unit. While the employee was helping lift two 26,000-pound panels, his left thumb was caught and amputated between the panels.

Three employees were detaching an elevated walkway from a tank battery. After being cut, the walkway gave way while two of the employees were on it, and they fell about 15 feet to the ground. One of them suffered a compound fracture to the right femur and a concussion. The other suffered a crushed left heel.
An employee exited a truck, which then rolled over him. The employee sustained injuries to the skull and legs.
An employee was moving a pump motor when it fell on his foot, breaking it.
An employee was trying to remove a rattlesnake from a worksite when it bit him.
An employee was using a drill with a brush attachment. The power cord wrapped around the tool, causing amputations to the employee's right-hand fingers at the first joints.
An employee was lowering supplies onto a truck and buggy drill. The employee slipped and fell onto the truck bed/rail, suffering broken ribs.
An employee was unlocking a saddle so it could latch around the pin that was holding it in place. When it was unlocked, it released down and caught and amputated the employee's left middle fingertip.

On 9/30/19, an employee went up the ladder of a separator tank. He was on top of the ladder when a pop-off valve released. He was exposed to gas and lost consciousness, falling 20 to 30 feet to the ground. He was hospitalized with a fractured left fibula, fractured right hip, and ruptured kidney.

An employee was using tongs to run tubing. As the employee went to set the tongs on a post, the employee's right thumb was caught between the tongs and the post. The employee was hospitalized with a lacerated and fractured right thumb.

Employees were replacing stripping rubber. As they were pulling the line up with a lifting hook, the line became caught on a kick-out beam. When the line released from being snagged, it snapped up and the lifting hook struck the injured employee in the mouth. The employee lost three teeth, suffered a broken palate and maxilla, and had one tooth embedded into the roof of his mouth. He was hospitalized.
An employee fell while walking on a sidewalk. The employee's right shoulder hit a welding machine, causing a fracture to the right upper arm.
An employee was gauging a tank at an established well site. He lost consciousness and was found on top of the tank, with his head down in the manhole and with rib injuries. He was hospitalized.
