A technician was removing a discharge valve from a cylinder at a machine shop. The valve and chair came out, causing the discharge valve to drop slightly. His left middle finger was pinched in the opening and the fingertip was severely damaged. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was a spotter for a forklift operator. He was walking backwards when he stumbled and fell to the ground. The forklift driver stopped and the load (pit liner material roll) rolled off the forks, striking the employee and breaking his legs.
An employee was removing bolts from a steam line when an adjacent steam line burped, releasing steam that burned his lower rear section.

While cleaning equipment prior to rig down, an employee was working with a rig contractor to rig down a centrifuge slide with a forklift. The employee was sitting on a beam under the centrifuge and behind the slide when the slide slipped off the forklift, swinging and pinning the employee against the beam of the centrifuge. He sustained a fractured tibia and fibula just below the left knee.
An employee's leg was crushed and broken when a semi-tractor trailer he was working on rolled over his leg.

An employee was installing a pumping unit at a well site. The employee was measuring a rod with a tape measurer when the rod slipped through the safety clamps. The employee's fingers were crushed between the rod clamp and load cell, resulting in amputations of the right index and left ring fingers.

An employee was approximately 3 feet up on a free standing ladder looking at and cleaning site glass on a water knock when the ladder twisted, causing the employee to fall to the ground. The employee sustained a head injury.

A frac pump was running at a well location. An employee heard a rattling sound and walked over to investigate. A maintenance packing bar was laying on top of the pump. When the employee got even with pump, the packing bar slipped into the pump, which kicked the packing bar back out. The packing bar struck the employee in the right eye, causing right eye orbital socket fractures.
An employee was extinguishing a grass fire and was overcome by smoke inhalation. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was trying to attach a bridle to a horsehead on a pumping unit. The horsehead became detached and fell from the walking beam on the pumping unit, striking the employee in both legs. The employee suffered a broken right kneecap.
An employee was putting on a bolt when a machine was activated and smashed the employee's hand. The employee was hospitalized and suffered amputation of the right ring and pinky fingers.
An employee was draining water from a water booth vessel when steam/hot water released from a loose fitting onto the employee's midsection, causing first and second degree burns.
An employee was winterizing a gas compressor when a flash fire occurred. He received burns to his face, neck, and hands.
An employee was attempting to light the pilot light on a heater treater when a faulty valve allowed gas to escape and ignite, causing second degree burns to the employee's face.
Employees were attempting to attach forks to a backhoe. The injured employee was holding the forks when he fell off the casing trailer. The forks landed on his chest and he sustained broken ribs.
An employee was in the office shutting down for the day. The employee impacted the back of their head on an unknown object and was hospitalized with a head injury.
An employee was exiting a truck when he lost his footing while descending the cab stairs. He fell to the ground and injured his left elbow, requiring hospitalization.
An employee was walking into the break room when the employee slipped on the wet floor and sprained a knee, requiring hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was trying to light the pilot on a buster at a tank battery when a flash-back occurred which blew him back 15-20 feet. The employee sustained second degree burns on part of his face and hands and was hospitalized.

Two employees were putting a down joint of pipe on the back of a fracturing pump unit for mobilization. The down joint was to be placed between the ladder and the step handle. One employee's right index finger was caught between the joint of pipe and trailer deck of the unit. The finger was injured and was surgically amputated.
An employee was trying to release solids in a centrifuge that had packed off. His left ring finger was caught between a belt and a pulley and the fingertip was amputated.

A water tank driver was offloading at a job site when the employee's elbow struck a valve. The cap from the valve came off and struck the employee in the stomach, cutting the abdomen. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was involved in lifting a pipe out of a double service well rig and taking apart the slip bowl assembly. The operator had attached the lift sub to bring the pipe up when the threads failed, causing the pipe to come back down and amputate four of the fingers on the employee's left hand.

An employee was attempting to remove the pony rod from a pump when his finger was caught in between the pony rod and the pump metal base. He received fractures to his left-hand index finger and was hospitalized.
An employee was operating a mini jerk machine when his hand was smashed between the lever and the machine.
As they were leaving a control room, two employees fell 30 feet through a floor opening immediately outside the door to the concrete below and were hospitalized.

An employee was operating a load press machine, working on a metal casing, when the part did not eject. The machine was under pressure and expelled the part just as the employee was reaching to get the casing. The ejected part struck the employee's ring finger causing a contusion and laceration to the ring finger.
An employee sustained an electrical shock from an overhead line as he was leaving a lease road.
An employee was reaching for a hoist cable over a guardrail. The employee and the guardrail fell to the ground about 25 feet below and the employee suffered broken bones.

Employees were working to remove and change the air swivel on the down the hole hammer (DTH) machine. They were using a 60" pipe wrench weighing 60lbs. to loosen the drill steel by over-torqueing the pipe wrench and wedging it against the mast while rotating the drill steel in a counter direction. After some attempts, the DTH operator approached to help Employee 2. The drill then rotated and the pipe wrench contacted the right side of Employee 2's face, knocking him to the ground. The wrench then struck the DTH operator on the hard hat. Both employees were taken to the hospital. The DTH operator was released from the hospital after an evaluation. Employee 2 was hospitalized with multiple fractures to his jaw and cheek bone on the right side of the face.
An employee was doing maintenance work on a cement truck. The trailer rolled backwards and the employee was caught and injured between the axle and the ground.
An employee was heating oil with a hot oiler on frac tanks when a fire started. The employee was hospitalized with second degree burns on the face, hands, and back.
An employee was holding an apparatus designed to help pull a piece of equipment when his thumb was caught and crushed. The employee sustained an amputation to the nailbed of the left thumb.

While working on a saltwater disposal system, an employee was checking the rotation of a pump and noticed the oil tank was bulging at the bottom. The employee ran to get away from it when a flash fire erupted. The employee sustained second degree burns to the face, lower back, and both hands.

An operator was lowering a poly pipe into the bell hole for a poly fuse tie-in. The injured employee was in the hole receiving the pipe when the pipe shifted and crushed his hand against the poly machine. The employee's right thumb and right index finger were crushed. The thumb nail and part of the thumb were removed. The index finger was degloved and later amputated at the hospital.

An employee was monitoring a 2-inch hose that was being thawed out using steam and was about to uncouple it to drain the line. When he unlatched the cam locks, built-up steam in the line released and burned the employee's face.
An employee was working on a frac tree. The tree fell, catching the employee on the leg and breaking it.

An employee was attempting to repair a vibration pad. While working on the pad, the employee was sitting on the battery box. When the employee connected two wires, the vibration pad raised up and pinched the employee's ankle, breaking it.
An employee was draining natural gas condensate from a level transmitter. When a valve was opened, the escaping gas ignited. The employee suffered first- and second-degree burns to the face and neck.
An employee was power washing the shop when he was struck by a reversing forklift that ran over and broke his right leg.

Casing was being run at a drilling site. The employee was reaching for a safety chain on an elevator door when the casing was pushed into the employee's right arm, smashing it against the pipe and tool that was in the hole. The employee's arm was broken.

An employee was pulling rods from a well and placing them in a basket on a truck. A rod fell from the basket and struck him on the shoulder. He suffered a collapsed lung and broken bones in the shoulder, and was hospitalized.
Employees were using a skid steer to load flat rails onto a trailer. One employee's fingers were caught and crushed between a rail and the trailer.

A maintenance employee was installing a harmonic balancer on a crank shaft on a frac pump. He was pulling himself up using a strap when the strap sheared a bolt holding some of the components together. This caused the metal lifting eye to fall and strike the employee's hand, resulting in an amputation of the right pinky finger.
An employee was on top of a tank when it exploded. He was thrown from the tank and required hospitalization for multiple fractures.
An employee was guiding a fence panel that was suspended by a crane. The employee's finger was crushed between the suspended load and an object on the ground. The finger was amputated.

An employee was walking with a relief crew, inspecting rig-down operations. The employee fell through an open hinge floor plate, landing 3 1/2 feet below and suffering a dislocated left shoulder and broken left humerus.
An employee was threading a machine when the machine's 50-inch blade amputated four fingers on his left hand.

An employee was moving the tubing tongs on a workover rig over the head when the tongs caught the head and the level became stuck while the motor was in high gear, causing his gloved hand to become wrapped in the coil. His left distal phalange was degloved, resulting in an amputation.

Two employees were observing a crew who was in the process of reconfiguring a well head. Trapped pressure was released within the well and blew shrapnel (nuts, bolt, plastic parts of the inside of the valves that are part of the well head tree) at the two employees. One employee received an amputation injury to his right thumb. The other employee received shrapnel injuries to his body requiring him to be hospitalized and undergo surgery to remove the shrapnel.
An employee was walking toward equipment when the employee tripped on a 2-inch pipe on the ground. The employee hit their nose and upper lip and suffered a dislocated shoulder.

An employee was on top of a working platform. While exiting the platform around the tank, a pressurized line came loose and knocked the employee to the ground. The employee suffered a fractured right arm and fractured ribs.
A drilling rig was tripping pipe out of a hole. An employee grabbed the drill stand before the spinners latched, causing amputation of the employee's left middle finger.
An employee was injured by an arc flash after equipment was re-energized. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was picking up a bushing when it amputated the tip of his middle finger.
An employee slipped on the floor and fractured an ankle while rigging a blender unit.

An employee fell from a rolling ladder while operating a valve, landing on a concrete surface about 4 feet below. The employee suffered a broken left femur and a dislocated right elbow and was hospitalized, undergoing surgery.
An employee was rolling a 10-inch pipe on a pipe rack when another 10-inch pipe fell on his left hand, crushing it.
An employee was using a winch and a cable when his hand was caught between the winch and a truck frame. The employee suffered an amputation.

During drill rig set up, a raised piece of drill pipe slipped out of the pipe stop housing that keeps the pipe from moving when placed in the upright rack and an employee's left thumb was caught and crushed between the pipe and the housing. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee was felling dead ash trees when an adjacent ash tree fell and struck his head. He was hospitalized with a fractured spine.
An employee was performing maintenance on tongs when the tongs engaged, amputating the employee's right index fingertip.
An employee slipped while descending stairs on a drill rig, falling and breaking his ankle.
An employee was cutting banding around a steel pipe when the pipe rolled off the rack and struck the employee's right leg, fracturing the tibia and fibula.
An employee was conducting a pipe laydown operation. An elevator struck a mast, kicking the pipe out so that it struck the employee in the face. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was de-burring a part in the lathe while it was rotating using a sand paper strip. The employee was pulled into the lathe, suffering a fractured right arm and lacerated right thumb.

The injured employee parked the vacuum truck on the SW end of the pulling unit. Another employee used the winch line on the pulling unit to grab a pipe. He wrapped the winch line around the vacuum truck's bumper tow pin and back up around the pipe to just below half-way up the pipe. The pipe began to bow in the middle. The pipe gave way and hit the injured employee on the left side, stomach, and back knocking the employee to the ground.
An employee was lowering a pickup truck's tail gate when his right ring finger was caught between a cable and the tailgate's upper rail. The fingertip was amputated at the first knuckle.
An employee was working on equipment when it fell and struck his foot causing a fracture. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was operating an auger when the employee was pulled into the auger, suffering broken ribs and a broken right arm and wrist.

An employee was working with others on top of a derrick to drill a pipe into the ground. He placed his hands on the pipe to steady it and his fingertips were caught between the collar and elevator, resulting in middle and ring fingertip amputations.
An employee was testing a tool by running it down into a pipe with a gun when the employee's right middle finger was caught between the pipe and the testing tool. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was moving a pumping unit into the top-dead-bottom position. He stood behind the pump jack motor and began pushing on the belt to help roll the pump unit. The unit moved and suddenly shifted. The employee then slipped and lost his balance. His left hand contacted the bottom belt and was pulled into and around the motor sheave, amputating his left pinky fingertip and lacerating and fracturing his left ring and middle fingers.
An employee was installing a skillet blind when the employee's left index finger was caught between a wrench and a bolt, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was opening the top steam vent on the main fractionator. The trapped hot condensate from the vent leaked out and landed on the employee's back and shoulders. The employee was hospitalized with second degree burns.
An employee was struck in the head by a pipe while servicing a compressor, requiring hospitalization for a head injury. A hard hat was not worn at the time of the incident.

Employees were working to remove a blow-out preventer (BOP) by dragging it with a tandem bed truck on the BOP skid from between two rig subs during rig-down operations. An employee was spotting the BOP skid as it was being pulled out by a tandem bed truck so it did not contact the rig sub's cylinders. He was standing on each side of the BOP skid directly beside the gas well cellar that the BOP had been removed from in order to watch the skid pass the cylinders and communicate with the bed truck operator as he pulled the skid away from the spotters. At the time, the well cellar guards had been removed from around the BOP, as is required to disconnect the BOP and lay it over on the skid. The employee stepped back into the cellar opening and fell 4 feet down onto a metal work platform and toe board, resulting in a broken collar bone, broken ribs, and a punctured lung.
An employee mistakenly drank methanol that was in a soft drink bottle and sustained poisoning.
An employee was using a feeding hose to remove material from a tank when a flash fire occurred within the tank and contacted the employee's face, causing second degree burns.

Employees were at a dewatering line filling a tank on a subcontractor's truck when the tank pressurized and forced water from a hatch. The pressurized water made contact with two employees. One of the employees was hospitalized with head, back, face, and eye injuries.
An employee was standing around talking inside the office on ground level when he stepped back, turned, and lost his balance. He fell, struck the floor, and was hospitalized with a broken femur.
An employee was attempting to jump over a pipe that was being lowered into a bell hole when the employee hit the pipe. The pipe then fell and struck the employee's lower abdomen and hip.
While exiting the doghouse of a nitrogen unit, an employee fell from a ladder to the ground, suffering a back injury.

An employee was driving an ATV when it ran over a fallen tree branch. The branch popped up and went through the ATV's floor, striking the employee. The employee suffered a broken arm, a bleeding spleen and liver, and a head laceration.
An employee was manually rotating a belt pulley during oil servicing. The employee's left hand was pulled into the pulley system, resulting in amputation of the middle and ring fingertips.

An employee was attempting to load a rough terrain forklift onto a flatbed trailer. The forklift slipped off the trailer onto its side and the employee suffered a fractured pelvis and three fractured ribs.

An employee was on a 5-foot ladder repairing a hydraulic valve and changing the internal packing. He used pressurized air to push the piston up. He then bled the fluid out of the valve. Once he removed the last bolt, pressure released, and the valve housing struck the employee in the rib area knocking him off the ladder. The employee sustained bruised ribs and back pain.

Employees at an oil rig were breaking down its blowout preventers. After removing the preventers from the wellhead, they put a wooden board on the ground to set the preventer on and keep it from getting muddy. When one employee unhooked his tagline from a preventer, the preventer shifted and the locking stem on its top struck the top of the employee's left boot. He suffered a laceration to the foot and two broken toes.

An employee was standing behind a winch truck. The truck rolled back and ran over the employee's left leg. The employee suffered a thigh injury, a head laceration, and bruising to the right-side ribs.
An employee was struck by crane as the company was performing a rig move. The employee suffered a fractured left heel.
As a crane truck was rigging down, an employee's hand was caught between the outrigger and the crane. Three fingers on the employee's right hand were crushed and the employee was hospitalized.
A team of employees was carrying a 10-foot section of iron tubing. One of them slipped and the tubing struck the back of his head. He suffered dizziness and blurred vision.
An employee slipped on a damp walkway and overcompensated to keep from falling down, resulting in a fractured left ankle. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was performing well servicing operations when a swivel amputated a thumb tip.

An employee was acting as a spotter for the loading of a rig pump. The employee tried to remove a pin that was in the way of the resting point of the pump and his right thumb was caught in a pinch point, resulting in an amputation of the thumb at the first knuckle.
An employee was bending down to pick up a hose to connect to a pump to pressurize it when he felt pain. He was hospitalized and required surgery for a hernia.
An employee was operating a storm water lift pump and hot water condensation blew out of the atmospheric muffler vent onto the operator's back causing first and second degree burns.

An employee was draining condensate from an air compressor when a catastrophic failure occurred on a check valve on a natural gas line. The natural gas began blowing toward the running compressor and the gas ignited causing an explosion. The employee was hospitalized for second and third degree burns to the face, hands, left leg, and left midsection.
An employee was approaching a skid-steer from the side when the skid-steer ran over his left foot and fractured a toe.
An employee was walking back to the work area, slipped, and fell to the ground fracturing the right tibia and fibula.

An employee was blowing excess sand off a pneumatic trash compactor skid that had recently been sandblasted prior to painting. While repositioning himself onto the platform, the weight shifted to one side, forcing the equipment to tip and pin him to the ground. The employee's right fibula and tibia were broken.
An employee was checking a pumping unit to see if the belt was loose. The pumping unit activated and the belt amputated this right pinky fingertip.

During swabbing operations, an employee was changing a drain hose from one bucket to another when hydrogen sulfide gas released from the hose. The employee fainted and was hospitalized for hydrogen sulfide exposure.

An employee was pushing a stand of drill pipe to its stowed position. While pushing the drill pipe, he slipped and fell forward. He placed his right hand on the deck to catch his fall. The stand of drill pipe swung back towards the injured employee as the driller was lowering the top drive to catch the stand, before it swung across the mast. The stand of drill pipe was then set down on the injured employee's right hand, amputating his ring finger.
An employee was receiving a pig from the pipeline, when the pig exploded through the cover. The employee sustained a fractured hand and a concussion.

Employees were laying down an 8" drill collar from the catwalk using the main rig hoist. During this, the injured employee was placing a 3x6 wooden board under the collar. When the collar came in contact with the board, it caused the end of the board to rise up, partially degloving the employee's left shin that required a skin graft.
An employee was function testing the wench line for leaks, slipped on the oil rig floor, and fell onto a sheave, amputating two fingers on his left hand. The sheave was partially guarded at the time.

An employee was cleaning the yard and burning trash. An empty barrel that had held flammable material exploded on the trash pile. The employee suffered second-degree burns to the hands and face, and another employee from a different company also received hand and facial burns. Both employees were hospitalized.

A well service floor hand was connecting pipe to a power swivel. The employee's left thumb was caught and crushed between the tubing elevators and a lifting cable. The employee was hospitalized, undergoing a surgical amputation to the thumb.

The injured employee was collecting produced water from a well site when he observed a person collapse. The injured employee attempted to render aid to the person, when he succumbed to hydrogen sulfide (H2S). The injured employee was hospitalized for H2S exposure.
An employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide and was hospitalized for an inhalation injury.
A mechanic was working on a pump truck's belt drive radiator fan system. His left little finger was caught between the timing belt and a pulley, and the fingertip was amputated.

An employee assisting in hydro-excavation operations sustained injuries to the left foot from a pressure washer being operated by another employee. The injured employee sustained lacerations on the left foot a few inches above the ankle and between the little toe and the fourth toe.

The injured employee was overseeing that the rod connections were going well. A work crew was coming out of the well with 1.5-inch, fiberglass rods and double stands. They had just made the connection. An approximately 60-foot fiberglass rod unscrewed from the holding, slipped out of the transfer, fell out of the barrack, and hit the rig floor. It then bounced off the rig floor onto the ground and struck the injured employee on the left side of the head, knocking him unconscious.

An employee was performing an inspection of the inside of a pipe near a solenoid valve. The valve actuated while his left hand was inside the pipe resulting in a partial amputation of the index and middle fingers.

An employee was positioning an oilfield drill bit when it fell from the connection fixture it was connected onto. The bit fell onto the employee's left ring fingertip and crushed it against the work surface. The fingertip was medically amputated.

An employee was inspecting and writing down the serial number of a casing adapter tool in the yard. The employee rolled the tool over and the tool proceeded to roll over again, striking and amputating the employee's right index finger.

An employee was removing a clamp from the cable on the swivel. The decking had been removed and the employee was standing on the beam. The employee slipped and fell, landing on the surface casing valve. The employee sustained broken ribs and a punctured lung.

During rig down, an employee was attempting to move a hose supported on a spreader bar. The hose came free from the spreader bar and swung into a machine, and the employee's left little finger was caught between the hose and the machine. The distal phalanx of the left pinky finger had to be medically amputated.

An employee was performing maintenance on a vertical two-phase separator. The employee was reconfiguring the sight glass and using various wrenches to loosen the existing fittings and tighten the new fittings. The fitting that connected the vessel to the sight glass piping broke behind the closed valve. The swage (fitting that broke) caused the pressurized hydrocarbons to release into the air, which found an ignition source and started a fire. The employee received second and third degree burns to the hands, legs, and arms and was hospitalized.

An employee was pressure washing a piece of drilling equipment when he slightly slipped, lost his balance, and ran the tip of the pressure washer wand across his foot, causing an injection wound. He was hospitalized with a foot laceration from the high-pressure water.
An employee was spotting for a backhoe when its track struck the employee. The employee's left leg was amputated from the knee down.
An employee was troubleshooting the dehydration unit at the compressor station when he sustained burns to the hand and face from a fire. He was hospitalized.

An employee was using a pressure washer to wash grease off of equipment. The employee was moving the power washer wand from side to side, when the wand went across his right foot. The pressurized spray cut through his boot and caused abrasions and lacerations to his right foot. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were troubleshooting a PSV that was lifting prematurely. A release of hydrocarbon/hydrogen caused an explosion and fire. One employee suffered burns to the face. A second employee struck a rail during egress as a result of the pressure wave and suffered a fractured kneecap. Both employees were hospitalized.

An employee was climbing up a fixed ladder to verify a process valve lineup. He fell off the ladder, landing 10 feet below on a rail and gravel. He suffered lacerations to his left elbow; collapsed lungs; and fractures to the ribs, elbow, and pelvis.
An employee slipped on recently mopped wet tile in an elevator landing at work, falling to the wet floor and breaking her hip. She was hospitalized.

An employee had unloaded a tracked drill rig off of a trailer and started to drill when the employee's pant leg became caught in the drill auger. As a result, the employee suffered a fracture to the left fibula with contusions and a hematoma, requiring hospitalization.

An employee was guiding/lowering a Kelly hose off to the side of the work floor with a winch line when a counterweight slid down the winch line and struck the employee's left hand, causing an open fracture that required hospitalization.
An employee was cleaning the inside of a tanker truck and passed out, requiring hospitalization.

An oil/gas well employee was pushing down on a liner washer tube with a pin. The pin slipped, and the employee's right thumb was caught and smashed between the piston and the liner. The employee suffered a partial amputation to the thumb.

An employee was lowering a transfer hose between two liquid cargo barges. The winch started to free-spool and the hand crank came out of its seat. The employee was putting the hand crank back in to stop the winch from free-spooling, when the gears on the winch caused a partial amputation of a finger on the right hand and a fracture.

Three employees were cleaning a heater treater when a gas build-up caused an explosion in the building. Two of the employees received minor injuries; the third was hospitalized, having suffered a severe laceration across the forehead, burns to the face and neck, and a fractured spine.

An employee was working to remove a section of catwalk that was approximately 30 feet high when he stepped from the catwalk section being removed onto the assumed catwalk to be left in place. The planking of the catwalk bent, causing him to lose his balance and fall to the ground. He suffered a broken right arm.
An employee was performing maintenance and starting a gas plant by turning the valves when a flash fire and explosion occurred. He suffered burn injuries to his hands and face.

An employee was tightening a nut on a polished rod's 2-bolt clamp on a horse head while standing on a well head cap 2 feet off ground when the employee slipped and fell back, hitting a concrete block. The employee suffered a head contusion.

Two employees were installing vent pipe and supports on top of a bulk storage tank. There was an explosion in the tank causing the employee working on the tank roof to fall from the tank to the ground. The employee was hospitalized for a fractured shoulder. The second employee was in an aerial lift at the roof line when the tank exploded. The second employee did not fall, but sustained flash burns to the face and arms.
An employee fell from a flatbed trailer to the ground. The employee suffered a broken skull, with brain bleeding, and was hospitalized.
An employee was inspecting heavy weights in the yard when he experienced stomach aches and cramps, requiring hospitalization due to potential heat exhaustion.

An employee was cleaning up trash around a pumpjack unit. The unit turned on, caught the employee's shirt, and pinned the employee against the unit's fence enclosure. The employee lost some skin on the left leg, as well as torn ligaments in the left knee.
After performing general maintenance around a plant, an employee started experiencing muscle spasms and was hospitalized for a possible heat stress injury.
An employee was struck on his left leg by a high-powered pressure washer and sustained a deep laceration.
An employee was power-washing a vessel when the water stream struck his foot, causing a wound that became infected. He underwent surgery to clean the wound.
An employee was sitting in a buggy entering measurement data for drilling, when he started feeling ill. He was hospitalized with heat stroke.
While tasked with checking inventory in the warehouse, an employee was stung on the left thigh by an insect. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was on a rig floor walkway removing a wireline top tree flange when the walkway collapsed to the ground. The employee suffered a broken leg and a head laceration.

An employee was tightening straps on a 3,000-pound wire ram. Straps on the opposite side became loose and the ram began to dig into the ground, then fell and pinned the employee to the ground. The employee suffered a lower lumbar compression.

An employee was painting the exterior of a home from a 12-foot ladder. The employee fell from the ladder and landed on a patio, suffering multiple broken ribs and a large gash on the head. He was hospitalized.

On a rig at a well site, a hydraulic line ruptured and sprayed diesel fuel onto a turbo, which caused a fire. Two rig employees hit the kill switch and jumped off of a 15-foot platform. One employee suffered a fractured ankle and was hospitalized.
An employee was cutting a concrete pile when a cut off section of the pile broke loose and crushed the employee's right hand, resulting in a thumb amputation.

An employee was removing a valve cap on a compressor at a compressor station. Trapped pressure caused the cap to fly off and strike the employee on the right side of his face. Glass from his safety glasses was embedded in his right eye, necessitating surgery to remove the eye.
An employee was installing a 10-foot long pipe to a new separator. The pipe came loose and struck the employee's thumb against a support bracket. The thumb tip was medically amputated.
An employee stepped out of a pickup truck, which began to move. The employee fell and the truck ran over the employee's right leg, causing tibia and fibula fractures that required surgery.

An employee was reversing the lock out/tag out while on a pumpjack, removing the chain and binder from the unit. The employee slipped and fell onto an angle iron on the outer side of the concrete base. The employee sustained injuries to his right side, including his right hip and elbow, as well as transverse process fractures in two locations.

Employees of Sundown Operating, Inc., and Axis Energy Services, LLC were working at an old oil/gas well plugging the well and getting ready to rig down. The Axis Energy Services employee was working from the platform operating the snubbing equipment. The casing from the well bore connected to the primary BOP broke causing the secondary BOP and the platform where the employee was working to fall to the ground approximately 28 feet below. The Axis Energy Services employee was hospitalized for a fractured leg. The Sundown Operating employee was assisting with the snubbing operation and was struck on the leg by the falling lug nut to the hydraulic BOP. The Sundown Operating employee was hospitalized for a fractured hip.

An electric gate at a third party facility would not operate. The pin pad had been disabled and the chain had been unhooked from the operator for the gate. An employee was manually opening the gate (pushing it open) when the chain got caught on a bolt or other object. While the employee was trying to release the chain, the gate moved, causing the employee's hand to go through a roller. He sustained contusions and lacerations to four fingers and a partial amputation of his left middle fingertip.
An employee was throwing away scrap. In the scrap bin, the employee moved a mandrel hanger to an empty spot and his right little finger got caught against another mandrel resulting in amputation.

An employee was swabbing a valve at an oil well site when the swab tool spun around and struck him in the torso. He sustained a broken right arm, broken sternum, and a concussion. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee of West Texas Boring was 2.5 feet from the edge of a pit trying to measure the distance of the water line. The ground gave way under his feet and he slid down into the pit. The employee was buried up to his waist in approximately 4 cubic yards of heavy rock and dirt. He sustained fractures to the ribs and a leg.
An employee sustained heat stress and dehydration while working on the rig.

An employee was using steel tongs to attach a 15-foot metal rod to the existing drill rod string. The drill rod began rotating and the employee was stuck by the pipe tongs causing a left forearm fracture.
An employee was operating a hydrovac when a hose burst in it, cutting the employee's right bicep.

An employee was conducting maintenance on a natural gas glycol dehydration unit when the housing unit ruptured and hot glycol fluid made contact with the employee, leading to hospitalization for third degree burns on top of the head, neck, and back.
An employee was opening a hatch to check liquid sulfur draining into a pit. The liquid sulfur splashed onto the employee's hand and face, causing chemical burns.

An employee was taking pressure readings on a hull when his right foot fell into the hull opening where grating had been removed. The employee was hospitalized with broken ribs and torn tissue in his knee.

An employee was mowing the grass when the mower slid into a drainage ditch and landed on top of them. The employee suffered amputated fingers on the right hand (3rd, 4th, 5th fingers) and a portion of the palm, leading to hospitalization and surgery.

An employee swung a sledge hammer to hit a hammer union. The sledge hammer missed and caused the employee to lose balance and fall approximately 3 feet, hitting his back on a mud pump module and suction pipe. The employee sustained fractures to the L2, L3, and L4 vertebrae.

A service technician was tasked with moving equipment. As he was moving a carrier basket from a pallet, the equipment fell and crushed his right index finger. The employee was taken to the hospital where the tip of his right index finger was amputated.
An employee turned on a combustor at an oil and gas production site. A flash fire caused second-degree burns to the employee's hands and first-degree burns to his nose and ears.

An employee was removing a tarp covering a mechanical fabrication area. The employee was standing on the fourth rung of an 8-foot ladder when he lost his footing and fell to the ground sustaining a broken tibia/fibula.

On 8/31/2020, a Noble Casing, Inc., employee was on location performing rathole operations. A nearby skid steer operator was unloading a joint of pipe from a trailer and had the pipe elevated while backing to clear the bunks. The pipe then slid off the skid steer forks and trapped the employee between the pipe and trailer. The employee suffered a dislocated left elbow, broken left femur, single vertebra fracture, and bleeding in the brain, requiring hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was climbing onto a frack pump. He fell to the ground about 5 feet below, suffering a broken arm.
Employees were turning a well back on. An employee was standing next to a tester when a flex line failed under pressure and blew, striking and fracturing the employee's left collarbone and jaw.
An employee was draining gas from a scrubber when a fire erupted and burned the employee's face and hands.

An employee was removing a fracturing pump suction/discharge manifold. The discharge manifold shifted, and his right index finger was pinched between it and the suction manifold. The top part of the finger was amputated.

An employee was retrieving boxes from the roof of an interior lab/office. The employee fell through the roof approximately 10 feet to the floor below. The employee suffered a fractured left femur and patella as well as head lacerations.

An employee entered the subfloor to survey the area before submitting a plan for repair. There is a submersible pump and an electrical outlet for the pump to plug into under the subfloor. The employee touched an electrical source and sustained an electrical shock. The employee sustained a burn injury, internal damage, and was rendered unconscious. The employee was hospitalized.
While working in a crane truck, an employee lost balance and fell out of the bed of the truck, suffering injuries to the wrist and arms that required surgery.
An employee was trying to relieve pressure at the valve of a workover rig. The valve broke under the pressure and the employee's face was lacerated.
An employee slipped and fell to the ground while exiting a water truck via the ladder. The employee was hospitalized for a foot/ankle injury.
An employee was removing hot sulfur slugs and sulfur splashed onto his face. The employee sustained a second degree thermal burn on his cheek.

An employee was arranging pipe on the trailer. When he went to get down from the trailer the employee slipped on an oily surface and lost his footing. He fell off the trailer and landed on his right side fracturing his hip.

On September 24, 2020, at approximately 11:00 a.m. an employee was walking from an area to the next well. A guide bar for the rear drilling area was lodged on a matting board. As the employee attempted to dislodge the guide bar, he was struck by the bar resulting in a fractured lower right leg.

An employee was removing a sensor from the wellhead when a pressure release caused the sensor to blow into the employee's chest. The employee was knocked backward eight feet and landed on piping. The employee sustained a broken collar bone, humerus, and femur and a right leg laceration.

On September 26, 2020, the cable line of a workover rig failed, causing the block to fall and strike a platform where an employee stood. This caused the employee to fall from the platform. The employee landed about 34 feet below and suffered broken bones and a laceration.
An employee was walking beside a scissor lift, operating it via remote control. The lift's wheel struck and broke the employee's left ankle. The employee was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
An employee was on a derrick connecting drilling rods. His fingers were caught between a drilling rod and a winch line and a finger was amputated.

Employees were disconnecting a motor tool with a pipe wrench. The pipe fell approximately 6 inches, pinning an employee's finger between the motor tool and the hand rails. The right pinky fingertip was amputated.

While working in the Rigger Shop, an employee was using channel lock pliers to disconnect two pieces of pipe that were bolted together. The pipe was raised by a crane. When the top bolt was removed, a portion of the pipe was pulled upward, and the other portion fell to floor. The employee's finger was pinched between lower handle of pliers and the portion of pipe supported by the crane. The employee suffered an amputation to his left ring finger.

An employee was transferring water from the frac tank/settling tank to another tank. The transfer continued until sludge built up in the pipe. The employee then had to clear the sludge from the pipe. The employee blew the line out using nitrogen, at 40 to 50-pounds, then heard a leak coming from a cam-lock connection. The employee was securing the broken cam-lock mechanism when a plug shot out of the pipe and broke the employee's finger. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee was running a line moling machine to clean the inside of pipe. When the employee went to pressure up the system using a 20-k water line, water from the hose injected into the pinky finger on his left hand.
An employee was steaming the inside of a production tank when a flash fire occurred inside the tank. The employee suffered second-degree burns to the face and third-degree burns to the hands.

An employee was operating the snubbing unit snubbing a pipe out of the hole and laying down pipe using a single latch elevator on the driller side rig winch. The elevator got hung up on the tubing board above and the latch on the elevator opened allowing the pipe joint to come free, fall, and strike the employee in the forehead. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was trying to bolt up approximately 15 feet of pipe to a spool piece coming out of the pump intake. As he was trying to insert a gasket, the spool piece dropped on his hand and amputated part of his pinky finger.
An employee was working on the rig floor. Equipment fell to the rig floor and the employee jumped off the rig onto the ground suffering a compound fracture to the right ankle.

An Enterprise employee was performing maintenance activities on the P-113 small volume prover. While attempting to remove the chain on the prover, the employee's left thumb was caught between the sprocket and chain and fractured. The employee was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee was doing maintenance on a blowout preventer. His left thumb got caught between the torque wrench he was using and the nut, and the first joint of his left thumb was amputated.
An employee slipped and fell while walking resulting in broken ribs.

After cleaning a heater treater and flushing it with water, employees were preparing to conduct pinhole welding when a flash fire occurred. An employee suffered burns to both arms, from the elbows to the hands.

A hoist was being used to move a 700 lbs. object. While holding a chain to help direct the object, an employee tripped and was struck by the object. The employee suffered a head/scalp injury, an injury to the left hand, and a left pinky finger injury. The employee required surgery for all injuries.
An employee was trying to remove a plastic cover from a completed drill pipe. The coating cage basket fell on the employee's right forearm, breaking it.

A ship's crew was moving a ship along a dock. One of the ship's lines broke and struck an employee who was walking on the dock. The employee suffered an arm amputation below the elbow, a broken pelvis, and abdominal injuries.
Employees were installing a blowout preventer. One employee's hand was caught between the actuator assembly cage and the top drive. His right index finger was crushed and later amputated.
An employee was using a rag to clean the polish rod on the pumping unit when he right index and middle fingers were amputated.
An employee was unloading material from a telehandler when their fingers were caught in a pinch point between the hook and chain resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was loading a roll of rubber mat into a pickup truck. The mat fell and caught the employee's finger against the bed rail. The employee suffered an amputation.

An employee was holding tension on a winch cable while reeling it in when their left hand got pulled into the guidance pin and bridle loop. The middle, ring, and pinky fingers were crushed and the pinky was medically amputated.
An employee was using a saw and cut their finger.
An employee was checking the contents of a hydro-vac truck. The truck's door was closed while the employee's right arm was inside it, causing lacerations to the upper arm.
An employee was walking at a jobsite, stepped on a hose, and slipped in friction reducer compound. The employee fell on the ground and broke a kneecap.

An employee was working on a generator. His right hand came into contact with a rotary blade, which caused multiple lacerations and two broken bones in the back of the hand. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.
An employee was changing hoses when he was sprayed by liquid butane, resulting in cold burns.
An employee was hooking up an air line on a piece of equipment. A crane load struck the employee, who suffered multiple leg fractures.

An employee was climbing a ladder with guard rails to access the rig floor. The ladder twisted to one side causing the employee to fall to the ground. The employee sustained displaced vertebrae in the neck and bruising and soreness.

An employee was driving a powered industrial truck when it struck a pillar. The employee was ejected and his head came into contact with the structure of the truck. He suffered a head injury and was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

The pulling unit crew was running rods in the hole from the derrick. The rig operator raised the rod string and began to lower the rods into the well. With the rod transfer still in place on the rod triple, the blocks were lowered, causing the chain holding the rod transfer to break. The rod transfer then fell and struck an employee, who was standing on the work floor, on the top frontal area of his hard hat resulting in the loss of an eye.
An employee was struck in the leg by a steel wire-braided discharge hose that jumped when pressure was applied. The employee suffered a broken leg.
While walking at grade under an asphalt rail car loading rack, an employee tripped on concrete that was protruding from the walkway. The employee fell and sustained five broken ribs.
An employee was unloading bore gel from a trailer when they fell in a hole in the trailer decking, resulting in broken bones in their foot that required surgery.
An employee attempted to clear debris from a drill auger and was pulled into the machine, resulting in injuries to their right arm and head.
An employee was acting as a ground guide for a vehicle as it backed up. The vehicle struck him and broke his left tibia and fibula.
An employee was operating a drill press when their glove got caught in the drill, resulting in an amputation of the left pinky finger.

An employee was driving an ATV on a gas well access road. As the employee drove down a hill, the ATV's rear end slipped on leaves. The ATV slid into a rut in the road and flipped over, throwing off the employee. The employee struck the ground and suffered a broken collarbone and three broken ribs.
An employee fell from a tractor trailer while disconnecting the brake and electrical lines, resulting in hospitalization for a broken femur in their left leg.

An employee was mounting a scanner box on the stump when their right middle finger was pinched between the sling hook and the D-ring, resulting in a fingertip amputation with the loss of the distal phalangeal tuft.
While performing pump maintenance at a well, an employee dropped a fluid end side cap on his left hand resulting in a laceration and broken bones.

An employee was making his rounds and checking equipment when the wet ground underneath him gave way. He fell in a hole that was about 1.5 feet deep and contained hot water and steam condensate. The employee was hospitalized with burns to both lower legs and ankles.

Employees had been pumping out oil and gas waste water from a tanker truck. Vapors/fumes from the condensate mixed in with the waste water caught fire when a torpedo heater started up and a spark shot out of the back. Two employees sustained multiple second and third degree burns and were hospitalized.

An employee was inspecting a pump jack on top of an aerial lift. The jack unit activated and pinned the employee between a crank arm and a pitman arm. The employee suffered a broken hip and a broken rib.

An employee was descending a platform ladder after setting up an oil rig platform when a crane hook caught the ladder and pulled it off the platform, knocking the employee to the ground and resulting in broken bones.

The injured employee and a coworker removed a valve body to unclog pods in an auger. After they unclogged the pods and reloaded them, they proceeded to reinstall the valve body. As they were picking up the valve body, the coworker slipped and the valve fell onto the injured employee's left pinky finger, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was closing a manhole cover in the floor of a mud pit when a disconnected 6-inch discharge line lying next to the cover shifted, pinching the end of the employee's finger between the floor grating and the discharge line. The employee suffered an amputation of the tip of his left middle finger.
An employee placed a stripper head down on a deck and pinched his thumb between the stripper head and the deck, resulting in a fractured thumb.
An employee was on an elevated platform, turning valves to prepare for cleaning the melter. He lost footing and fell 6 to 8 feet to the main floor. The employee sustained bruised and/or cracked ribs.

The sheaves of the crane were frozen due to ice and snow conditions, which caused a backlash with the auxiliary cable of the crane. The operator attempted to straighten out the backlash on the superstructure near the drum. The frozen sheave freed itself, allowing the cable to run, and the operator's right arm got tangled in the cable. The operator sustained an open fracture of the humerus and a dislocation of the radius.

An employee was working at the back of a tanker trailer with a handheld impact tool. A flash fire ignited due to the friction from the impact tool and the fumes mixing, resulting in 2nd-degree burns to approximately 15% of the employee's body.
An employee was handling a 55-gallon drum of material on the floor. His right middle finger was pinched between the drum top and a hard piece of metal. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee slipped on ice while walking from a gravel surface to a cement one. The employee fell down, suffering a broken lower right leg.
On February 17, 2021, an employee was completing rounds through a natural gas planet when he slipped and fell on an ice spot. He was hospitalized, having suffered a broken left hip.
An employee was working on a drilling rig floor. A piece of ice that had frozen to the drilling mast melted and fell off, landing on the employee's back and breaking three vertebrae.
An employee was loading a skid tank onto a winch truck. The employee was removing a rock from under the tank when the tank came down on the employee's hand, causing finger amputations.

An employee was checking control voltage in an electrical panel when an electrical short occurred, causing an arc flash which resulted in third-degree burns on the hands and second-degree burns on the face of the employee.

An employee was standing in front of a heater, watching a casing being floated into a hole to seal it. A ball valve failed and burst apart, fracturing the employee's cheekbone and lacerating his cheek.

An employee was tightening the on/off tool onto the sucker rod at a well site when their fingers were crushed between the rod table hole and the rod. The employee sustained a right ring fingertip amputation and a deep laceration to the right middle finger.
Employees were preparing a unit for turn-around and chemical cleaning. There was a release of un-hydrotreated naphtha that resulted in a fire. Six employees sustained burns and were hospitalized.

An employee was helping push a landing joint onto a catwalk trough at the v-door on a rig floor. The employee's right middle and ring fingers were caught between the locking ring and landing joint. The employee suffered a fracture to the middle fingertip and an amputation to the ring fingertip at the nail.

An employee was doing maintenance work on a pump. The employee was sprayed in the face with pressurized hydraulic fluid, which lacerated the employee's right eye. The employee was hospitalized and underwent debridement of the eye.

SPN Well Services employees were inspecting gas production unit chokes for sand washing. They had inspected three units and were bleeding off pressure on a fourth when a flash fire engulfed it in flames. One of the employees suffered first-, second-, and third-degree burns.

Two employees were unloading and loading propane cylinders. A leaking propane tank was placed in front of a makeshift structure. Propane gas accumulated within the structure and an explosion occurred. Both employees suffered second and third degree burns that required hospitalization.
An employee was climbing into a skid steer when he slipped and fell, suffering a broken hip.

An employee was dumping a mini dumpster, mounted on a forklift, into a large trash container. When the mini dumpster tipped, the employee's finger was caught between it and the forklift's forks. The employee's fingertip was amputated.

An employee was using a hydraulic torque wrench to loosen the nuts that held a pump's fluid end to the stay rod bolts. His right little finger was caught between the wrench and a nut that the wrench was braced against. His finger was crushed, and he was hospitalized.

Employees were rigging up a work over rig and using a crane to move a blowout preventer off a trailer. The blowout preventer moved and swung once it was lifted from the ground, hitting an employee in the chest. He suffered minor internal bleeding and was hospitalized.

An employee was working to clear a pump for maintenance and was sprayed with hot oil. He sustained first degree burns to the right wrist and lower portion of his face; and sustained first and second degree burns to his left wrist. The employee was hospitalized.

While hooking up a crane, the crane rigger signaled the crane operator to slack off. The operator slacked off and one chain was removed. When the rigger went to remove the second chain, the counter balance fell to the ground. The counter balance hit the rigger's left foot and severed their boot, resulting in injuries to the big toe and the toes next to it.

An employee was attempting to install a cap (a two-part assembly) onto a casing head. The cap was stuck, and as the employee tried to manually thread it onto the casing head, its upper part came down and caught the employee's left thumb. The employee suffered an amputation to the thumb and was hospitalized for surgery.
An employee sustained a partial left index finger amputation when high winds caused the compressor building door to slam on the employee's finger.
An employee was closing the tailgate of a pickup truck and caught their left ring finger in the hinge of the gate, resulting in an amputation to the fingertip.
An employee was operating a pressure washer. A fitting failed and high-pressure water was injected into the employee's leg.
An employee was using an impact torque wrench on a fluid end cap when the wrench spun and crushed the tip of his right middle finger.

An employee arrived at a location to shut some production wells. While walking through the location, the employee tripped on a 1-inch piece of pipe and fell to the ground on their right side. The employee sustained a fractured hip requiring hospitalization.

An employee was setting up a well rig when the counterweights spun free and caught his fingers. He suffered an amputation to the right ring finger at the top knuckle and an amputation to the right little finger at the tip.

An employee was collecting a sample at a closed loop station. Recently installed tubing came loose, spraying the employee with spent acid. The employee suffered second-degree burns to the right forearm and left wrist.
An employee was walking on the rig floor when he slipped on an open drill hole 10 inches in diameter, falling to the floor and fracturing both elbows.

An employee was swapping out sides of a choke manifold during drill out operations when the threaded end of a 10K needle valve parted from the end cap and struck the employee causing a laceration to the right leg.

Employees were conducting catalyst changeout activities in a reactor. A pipe wrench fell 23 feet into the space and struck an employee on the back of the right hand, amputating the right middle finger up to the first knuckle.
An employee was operating construction equipment and ran off the road at a construction site. The driver suffered broken bones and was hospitalized.
An employee was handling a pipe and amputated the tips of their right ring and middle fingers.
An employee was using a setting tool when their right middle and ring fingers were caught between the sleeve and the mandrel of the tool, resulting in an injury.
Hydrogen fluoride was released from piping near an alkylation unit's auxiliary acid dump drum. Two employees were exposed to the hydrogen fluoride and were hospitalized.

Employees were removing fuel from an underground containment sump at a gas station. The fuel vapors flashed, burning two employees. One suffered first- and second-degree burns to the face and neck; the other suffered first- and second-degree burns to his arms.

An employee was releasing the pressure from a setting tool. As the employee was screwing a wrench into the burst disc retainer, the retainer nut came free and the pressure escaped from the chamber. Debris struck the employee in the right shoulder and face, leaving foreign material in his eyes and causing contusions to the shoulder and the right side of his face.

A five-man crew had been subcontracted by Laredo Petroleum to replace the fire tubes on a heater treater and clean the inside of the tank. Three employees with Dorado Construction Group were contracted as a roustabout crew to clean the tank and replace the fire tubes, one employee of Mulholland Energy Services was contracted to operate the vacuum truck and remove the sludge from the tank, and one employee of Permian Service Co., LLC was hired to operate a hot oil truck to provide water to the roustabout crew for cleaning. At approximately 1:00 p.m. the employees had completed pulling out the old fire tube and had begun the process of cleaning the inside of the tank from the open hatch when an explosion occurred. Three employees were hospitalized for second and third degree burns to their arms and face.

Employees were cleaning out a heater treater using hot water to remove debris. When an employee opened the door to the heater treater, remaining hot water hit him in the face, chest, and hands, causing first- and second-degree burns.

An employee opened a valve to see if a drum was free of hot residual oil. The oil was plugged behind the open valve, but the plug dissolved. Hot oil (300-400 degrees F) splashed out of the drum's receiving receptacle and onto the employee's right thigh and right arm, as well as the right sides of the employee's abdomen and face.
An employee tripped going over a containment curb and fell. A Unistrut clip caused a laceration and degloving injury to his abdomen.

A crew had put their tools down after pressure-washing the outsides of two oil tanks. As they walked away, one of the tanks exploded. One of the employees suffered second- and third-degree burns on the back, from the waist up.

An employee was operating power tongs and running casing into a hole. The CRT tool fell 40 feet from the top drive striking the casing stump and the employee. The employee suffered four amputated toes on their right foot and a puncture wound on their back and was hospitalized.
An employee fell about 20 feet from an aerial lift while pulling cables.

While conducting a hole in tubing test, a pressurized release of natural gas and debris knocked an employee off balance causing the employee to fall into the debris and gas. The employee sustained a right pinky finger dislocation and abrasions on their back.
An employee was turning on the injection pump at a work site when a pressurized release of water struck the employee causing a laceration to their abdomen and chest and an injury to the left arm.

A crew of three Bassler Energy Services employees were about to clean out a heater treater vessel bottom. The vessel had been depressurized and its contents had been evacuated below the manway. When the crew opened the vessel to begin pressure-washing the manway face, fumes ignited and the resulting flash fire burned two of them. One suffered burns to the face, cheeks, and neck; the other suffered burns to the hands. One employee was hospitalized.

An employee was at an oil rig, cleaning a window while standing on the second rung of a ladder. The ladder shifted and he fell. He landed on the rig floor and suffered fractures to the left lower tibia and fibula.

An employee and a co-worker were cleaning out a tank. The employee had drill mud all over their boot and the co-worker was helping spray mud off the boot with a pressure washer gun when the pressurized water cut the employee's foot.

An employee was walking across the rig floor carrying a large bolt, called a connecting pin, when he tripped on an object and fell to the floor. The bolt impacted the end of his left ring finger and amputated the fingertip.

Employees were moving an oil rig's horse head out of the way so they could install a blowout preventer. As the operator picked up the winch lines, the two floor hands began moving the horse head to the side. The horse head flipped over, and an employee's finger was caught in the winch line and the horse head's bridle cable. The finger was lacerated and the fingertip was amputated above the nailbed.
An employee slipped and fell on a piece of equipment, suffering two broken ribs and a collapsed lung.
An employee was walking through an open area when high winds caused a crane boom to collapse. Debris struck the employee and broke the employee's right tibia and left foot.
An employee was filling forklift cylinders with propane gas when the nozzle connected to the cylinder released and the employee was burned by the propane gas.
An employee was working on a workover rig when a suspended rod and clamp struck their little finger and crushed it on an elevator sitting below, resulting in multiple finger fractures.

An employee was connecting a 4-inch metal flex hose to a connection point. The hose slipped off the connection point and pinched the employee's right leg against a wellhead isolation valve, causing an open fracture to the femur.
An employee was pouring oil into a refill port when the oil shot back out onto the employee, resulting in burns to the chin that required hospitalization.
An employee was tightening a hose clamp. The hose broke and hot liquid sprayed onto the employee causing third-degree burns to both hands.

A three-person crew was unloading pipe. Two crew members were outside of the truck handling the pipe on the rack. They loaded the three joints of pipe and moved to load the polish rod. One end of the rod was stuck into the ground so they picked up the opposite end and stood the 22' rod into the air to lay it down. The rod contacted a live, overhead electrical line and the two employees were electrocuted. Both employees also sustained electrical burns.
An employee was unloading pipes from a trailer. A pipe (3.5 inch in diameter) rolled off the trailer and struck the employee's legs. The employee sustained a right leg fracture.

An employee was getting a tarp crank handle out of the way by pushing the handle behind the ledge of a roll-off box. He then turned to pick up a chain that was on the ground to hook to the box. Tension on the handle caused it to release and hit the employee in the head/face. He was hospitalized with a forehead contusion and a laceration to the bridge of the nose.

An employee was working on a stand-alone rig. The employee had just broken off the tubing swivel with the tongs and was preparing to make the last connection. He placed his left hand near the opening of the tongs to push the tongs off the connection, but the Kelly hose was caught on the back of the tongs. The employee used his right hand to push the Kelly hose out of the way. The hose caught the operating handle and engaged the tongs causing the amputation of his left index and middle fingers and an oblique fracture of his left thumb.

An employee was spotting for a forklift that was transporting compressor cylinders. The cylinders slid off the forklift's forks, struck the employee, and pinned him against another cylinder on the floor. He suffered lacerations to the abdomen and face and was hospitalized.
An employee was attempting to free a hydraulic line. When the coil tubing was freed it struck the employee in the head causing a skull fracture and a laceration that required stitches.
An employee sustained injuries from a fire that occurred at a wellhead.
During the process of nipping down the well head, a flash fire occurred and an employee was burned on the face and neck.

An employee was assisting with installation of a pipe cutting machine. During the installation, the machine slipped off the pipe. The employee attempted to grab it and their right little finger was pinched between the machine and the ground, resulting in a partial amputation of the fingertip.

Employees were creating a joint in casing. When the employees reversed out the tongs, the tension in the casing pushed the tongs toward the injured employee. The injured employee's finger was pinched between the casing safety door and the tongs and their fingertip was amputated.
An employee was detaching a 200-pound bale at or near an oil well site. He tripped on a rock and fell backward and the bale fell on his abdomen, causing internal bleeding.
An employee was working with high pressure oil and sustained a high pressure wound under his left index finger. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.
An employee slipped and fell while descending a ladder. The employee landed on the ground about 3 feet below, suffering a dislocated ankle and a broken lower leg.

An employee was performing maintenance on a load cell. Their right hand was on an RPM sensor of rotating weights when the pump jack cycled on, resulting in amputation of three fingertips on the employee's right hand.

A crew, working for Red Diamond Energy Services, was laying down 2 7/8-inch tubing. The employee on the floor would unlatch the elevators slightly above the floor. The joint would bounce and the employee on the ground would grab and slide the tubing down the rack. While the 29th joint was being laid down, the employee's right ring finger was crushed between the tubing and the floor as the joint bounced resulting in amputation.

An employee was transferring potassium hydroxide (50-70%) from an IBC tote into a blending tank using a pneumatic double diaphragm pump in the transfer area at the facility. The hose disconnected during the transfer and potassium hydroxide (caustic potash) caused chemical burns on the employee's face, neck, and upper torso. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were screwing a running tool into a wellhead assembly. The injured employee's finger was in the wellhead assembly checking alignment when the assembly was manually rotated and the running tool amputated the employee's left index fingertip.

A mechanic was on top of the HHP in Bay 1 drilling out broken bolts. Another operator was running the overhead crane using a handheld remote, moving it from the south side of the HHP to the north side to pick up a fluid end. As the crane moved over the top of the HHP, it struck the mechanic, knocking him off the HHP onto the cement floor of the shop 13 feet below. The injured employee was hospitalized for broken ribs, a sprained wrist and stitches to the face.
An employee was standing on a trailer adjusting its load. A piece of equipment shifted, causing the employee to fall to the ground and strike his head. He suffered head trauma.
An employee was moving a 55-gallon drum. A rotary valve lacerated the employee's left index and middle fingers resulting in a partial amputation.

On July 26, 2021, an employee was hydroblasting using a 5,500 psi water blast gun with a 66-inch barrel. The barrel was run across the top of his left boot, lacerating the top of the foot. He was hospitalized, requiring cleaning and stitches for the wound.

An employee raised a well pump jack and placed the top and bottom rod clamps on the lifting rod. The bottom rod clamp slipped, causing the well pump jack to lower and amputate the employee's left thumb.

Two employees were working on a rig floor, separating the connection on a drill pipe. As they were starting to push the stand of the pipe, one employee slipped in some oil-based mud on the rig floor, fell forward, and put his hands out in front of himself to minimize the fall. The drill pipe moved back slightly and pinched his fingertip against the rig floor, resulting in the amputation of his right index fingertip above the first knuckle.

Two employees were investigating a 4-inch spent sulfuric acid line to see what was needed for repairs. The line ruptured and sprayed acid on both employees. One suffered burns to his hands and the lower part of his body. He was hospitalized.
An employee was making a connection when a swivel bounced back and caught his right middle finger between the swivel and the stump, resulting in a partial fingertip amputation.
An employee was under a vacuum truck checking a driveshaft installation. The truck rolled over him, crushing his pelvis and breaking ribs.
An employee was reading gas meters when a ram attacked him. The ram struck his lower left leg from behind, resulting in a fractured tibia that required hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was retrieving a load of water-based drilling mud with a vacuum truck. The employee slipped on the mud, fell, and struck his left side on the mud pump base. He suffered broken ribs on that side.
An employee was getting gas at a gas station when their truck rolled backward and ran over their left foot, resulting in a broken foot.

An employee was pushing the forks of a forklift to widen their position. He needed to get the forks around the hook it sits in. Once it cleared the hook, the fork slid quickly, catching the employee's right middle finger against the headache rack support. The finger was amputated.

An employee was doing maintenance on a gas well pump jack. The brake did not hold when he set it, and a belt and pulley caught his hand. He suffered an amputation to the little finger, about 7/8 of the way from the end.

On 8/19/2021, at approximately 0400 hours, the injured employee was assisting another employee to remove a fluid end on a frac pump in the repair bay. A wrench was activated and the employee's ring finger was caught and amputated between the HTW and the fluid end.

An employee was helping rig up a drilling rig. While he was driving a securement pin on an upper spreader beam, another spreader beam (stacked on the first one) slid over and struck his left foot. The foot was broken.
An employee was trying to raise the mast of a service rig. Something let loose or moved, causing his right hand to be caught. He suffered lacerations to fingers on the hand.

An employee was at a well site, adjusting studs in a tubing head with a blowout preventer and the tubing head in the air. The blowout preventer twisted and the employee's finger was crushed between the nut and the backup. The employee suffered an amputation to the finger.
An employee was working on a pumping unit. The employee's left middle and ring fingers got caught in the sheave and belt on the pulley system of the pumping unit resulting in fingertip amputations.
An employee was tripping pipe on a drilling rig. His right hand was caught with the drilling rods in the hole as the rods were being unscrewed, and his little finger was amputated.
An employee was helping connect tubing on a hydrowalk. His middle finger was pinched between the tubing and the hydrowalk. The finger was amputated.

An employee was trying to slide a work platform back into its housing. His middle finger was caught between the midrail and the side safety gate of the platform. The pad of the finger was severely lacerated, and was medically amputated.
An employee was replacing the valve on a frac pump. Fingers on his left hand were caught in the pump's moving pistons and injured; the middle finger required surgery.
An employee was performing a drilling operation when their thumb was caught in the drill and fractured.

An employee was responding to a seal leak on a crude pump when a nearby switchgear arced, causing a pressure wave to knock him to the ground. The employee sustained multiple lacerations to his face and hands.
An employee had been working on the pulley board. The employee fell 5 or more feet into the well cellar and hit his head on a 4-inch pipe sustaining a laceration on the back of his head.

An employee was folding soil matting in preparation for excavation and land reclamation when he was struck by a rubber-tracked skid steer. The employee was hospitalized with two fractures to the right leg.

An employee was preparing to connect drilling pipe when the elevator came open causing the 30 foot by 4.5-inch drilling pipe to fall onto the employee. The employee was struck on the shoulder, ribs, and back area, and sustained a punctured lung. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was attempting to loosen a horsehead that was being removed via rigging from a pump. The employee's left hand was caught in a pinch point, resulting in amputations of the third and fourth fingers and a nailbed laceration on the second finger.

A subcontractor was monitoring a wireline. Employees were filling lubricant to start a pressure test when a piece of iron flew out of the lubricant, striking the injured employee on the right side of the chest. The employee suffered three broken ribs and a hematoma on his liver.
An employee was rigging up a workover rig when their left thumb was pinched between the stationary structure of the rig and amputated.
An employee was cleaning a mud pump. A retaining cap dislodged from the pump and struck the side of his head, causing a laceration and a head injury.

Two employees were removing a well head bolt using hammers. The hammers hit each other, causing one hammer to shatter. A fragment of the hammer went under an employee's safety glasses, causing an injury to their left eye.
An employee was plugging and abandoning a natural gas well when he was struck in the face by a 30-foot section of steel tubing. The employee sustained multiple facial fractures.
An employee was welding a tank battery in the field when the welding torch ignited flammable gasses, causing an explosion that resulted in second and third degree burns to both hands and their face.

An employee was climbing up a rough-terrain crane. He hit his hard hat on the jib above him, lost his balance, and fell to the crane deck and then to the ground about 4.5 feet below the deck. He suffered rib fractures.
An employee was driving a water truck along a lease road when he hit a pothole and the vehicle dropped, jarring the employee's spine and resulting in fractured vertebrae.

An employee was conducting oil drilling rig derrick lifting operations. The employee was holding the bridle line while taking in slack when their right hand was caught in the crane sheave, resulting in broken bones and lacerations to their right hand.
An employee was supervising the loading of trucks onto a trailer. He fell from the trailer, suffering a closed fracture to the left wrist and a fracture to the left upper femur.
An employee was rigging down oilfield equipment. The tip of the employee's left thumb was amputated between a hydraulic torque wrench and a flange.

An employee was unscrewing and separating a connection of a drill pipe when drilling mud sprayed out of the connection, causing the employee to fall backward and strike his face on a piece of equipment. The employee suffered a laceration on his lip and a facial fracture.

An employee was racking drill pipe on the rig floor. As a stand of drill pipe was being set down on the rig floor, the employee slipped and fell. The stand of pipe was set down on his left hand resulting in a partial amputation to the middle finger.
An employee was watching the level of catalyst filling a fill bin from a discharge hose when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained burns to his ear, face, and lower leg.
