An oil derrick hand fell off the oil derrick platform and struck the derrick during the fall resulting in a fractured back.

An employee was helping to dig up a swivel. While they were getting ready to add the thread protector, the wire broke on the boom line and sliced the tip of the employee's right middle finger, pinching it against the bellhousing on the swivel and resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was removing pipe from a drilled water well when a spark caused an explosion and the rear of the drilling rig caught on fire. The employee sustained burns to the face and neck.
An employee was performing maintenance on rig tongs. The rig tongs became energized and pinched the employee's gloved hand, and their left ring finger was amputated at the first knuckle.

An employee was moving a water pump with a skid steer. When the employee reached the top of a hill, the water pump slid off the skid steer's forks and hit the cab. It entered the cab and struck the employee, who suffered a laceration to the left calf.
An employee was draining water out of a flare line. The employee opened the valve and was walking away when a flare ignited, resulting in second and third degree burns.

An employee was in a manlift basket with a co-worker, washing a drilling rig in preparation for the rig to be moved off site. The manlift basket became caught on the rig, and when the basket released, it bounced and caused the employee to be ejected. The employee fell approximately 20 feet to the ground, resulting in a broken left arm and pelvis.
An employee was using a pneumatic wrench to tighten a clamp when their thumb became pinched in the clamp, resulting in amputation of the thumb tip.
An employee was moving pipe on a trailer when his leg was struck by a joint of 6-inch pipe that rolled off a flatbed trailer. The employee sustained a leg fracture, which required surgery.
An employee was changing the attachment on the front of a telehandler forklift. His finger was caught between the attachment and the forklift. He suffered a partial amputation to the finger.
An employee was putting a pipe in place and pushing on a rotating sucker rod, which caught his glove and wrapped his arm around the rod. The employee sustained multiple arm fractures.
An employee was removing a guy wire from a base beam, slipped on grating and fell onto a casing valve, resulting in eight fractured ribs and a spleen injury.
An employee was loading a dozer into a trailer when he fell off the dozer onto the trailer platform and then onto the ground, resulting in a laceration to his left elbow.
An employee was repositioning a utility vehicle. The vehicle struck a bollard post; his left leg was caught between the vehicle and the post, suffering compound fractures.
An employee was operating a 3-point roller forming metal blanks when their left hand was caught in a pinch point, resulting in amputation to two fingers.

An oil derrick operator was reaching out to remove slack in a cable. His right hand was caught between the cable and the rod elevator as the rig operator came down with the blocks. His ring finger was crushed and his middle finger was amputated.
An employee was preparing rods to be guided in a machine. The rods fell on his foot, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was using a wrench to remove a rod box at a well head. The rod box broke free and released energy to the employee's right leg, resulting in a right leg fracture.

Three employees were performing maintenance on a natural gas compressor. Part of the job was changing the belt on the cooler (fan) from the compressor. Prior to changing the fan's belt, an employee removed a section of the fan guard and set it over the compressor. The metal guard section was 3 feet by 2 feet and 8-inches thick and weighed approximately 40 lbs. The guard fell from the engine more than 5 feet and struck the injured employee's hand, resulting in amputation of their index finger.

At about 3:40 a.m., a frac crew was pumping a stage when a conveyor belt on a sand hulk became clogged. An employee had just removed a clog in the equipment when the belt began to run again and pulled in the employee by the left arm. The employee suffered an injury to the hand and arm and was hospitalized.
While starting a mill machine, an employee's left hand slipped and was cut. The employee was hospitalized and his left little fingertip was medically amputated.
An employee slipped on ice while getting into his truck. He fell to the ground and suffered a dislocated and fractured hip. He was hospitalized.
An employee was replacing a drill rig's transfer case. The case shifted and amputated the tip of the employee's right index finger.
An employee was removing tongs when the door to a tong interlock opened and crushed the employee's right thumb. The employee suffered an amputation to the thumb.
An employee tripped and twisted his ankle while stepping down from a machine. He suffered a displaced fracture to the right fibula and a sprained ligament in the right ankle.
An employee was changing out tong heads and attempting to place a retaining pin. The lever and gear rolled over and crushed the employee's left thumb, resulting in amputation.
An employee was caught between pieces of drilling equipment (ST-80 and mast leg) while making a connection on the rig floor, resulting in a lacerated liver.

An employee was on a landing above a frac tank. The employee put a strap stick into the tank; when it hit the bottom of the tank, the fluids in the tank ignited. The flash fire caused the employee to jump or fall, and he suffered two broken legs as well as burns to the arm.
An employee was removing nuts from a pump unit. The employee slipped and their right index fingertip was crushed between the pump and a rachet. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was walking around the back of his truck when he slipped on ice and fell to the ground, breaking a hip.

An employee was clearing ice on top of a drilling rig doghouse landing. Hinges broke when the employee jumped to clear the ice, and the employee fell to the ground 20-plus feet below. The employee suffered fractures to the lumbar region, wrist, and ankle.
An employee missed a step and fell while descending from the back of a tractor. The step lacerated his upper left leg area and he was hospitalized.
A radiator was being lifted with an overhead crane. The load shifted and caught an employee's right index finger against the lifting strap. The finger was amputated.
An employee was repositioning a tubular onto a platform when the tubular rolled off the platform and contacted the employee's left leg, resulting in a broken tibia.
Employees were using a rotating rod to wrap up a pit cover from a frack site when an employee's pant leg got caught in the rotation, causing their leg to be broken in three places.
An employee was changing a reamer on a directional bore machine. He was using a large pipe wrench to loosen it when it slipped and broke his fibula.

An employee was attempting to bleed off pressure on a casing into a cellar so they could work on the casing at a drilling pad. Gas started to leak, resulting in a flash fire. The employee suffered burns to the face, ears, and hands that required hospitalization.
An employee suffered a cut on their left leg from an electrical saw.
An employee was reeling in a poly line onto a trailer. The line snapped and struck the employee's fingers, resulting in fingertip amputations.
An employee was hit in the abdomen by a dislodged cheater pipe, causing internal bleeding. Surgery was required.

An employee was in the process of rigging up equipment. While releasing ratchet straps with his right hand, the employee was supporting himself by placing his left hand on a gusset in the mast. As the second ratchet strap was released, the tong counterweight shifted and slid down about one foot, pinching the employee's fingers between the counterweight and the gusset and resulting in several broken fingers.
An employee was positioning equipment on a semi-truck when they slipped on grease and fell on the truck bed, resulting in a broken leg.
An employee slipped while exiting a truck and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a broken femur.
An employee slipped on ice in a parking lot and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a fracture to the right leg, below the knee, as well as a shattered ankle.

Three employees for J&R Transport were onsite when a flash fire occurred at an oil/gas wellsite. J&R Transport was hired to clean heater treater equipment at the wellsite. The heater treater had been removed from the oil/gas well system and was placed adjacent to the well head. A roustabout crew from another employer was onsite and removed the bolts and fire tube from the heater treater. When the tire tube was removed, a black liquid came out of the heater treater and spilled onto the ground and surrounding area. J&R Transport performed vacuum truck operations to remove the liquid from the ground. When that was complete, two J&R Transport employees began power washing the inside of the heater treater. One employee operated the power washer wand while the other employee operated the vacuum truck's suction hose. During this operation, a flash fire occurred inside the heater treater vessel resulting in fire shooting from the open end of the vessel where the two employees were working. One employee was thrown backward and suffered fractures to his collar bone, ribs, and shoulder and burns to face and arms. The other employee suffered second degree burns to his hands and first degree burns to his face. One employee was hospitalized.

An employee had been using tubing tongs to tighten loose bolts on a hanger bracket. As the employee was setting the tongs down, they triggered while the employee's fingers were between the tong clamps. The employee suffered an amputation to the right middle fingertip, as well as crushing injuries to the index and ring fingers.
An employee had just begun driving a truck down a lease road. The truck had driven about 350 feet when a flash fire began in the cab, causing second-degree burns to the employee's face and hands.
An employee was removing bolts from a wellhead tree when the tree fell onto his left leg, resulting in lower leg fractures.
An employee was operating an ATV/UTV and had an accident, resulting in fractured ankles.

An employee was redressing a 3.5" setting tool. In order to stroke the tool, he slammed the end of the tool down on an outrigger mat. His right ring finger slipped inside the setting sleeve on top of the tool. The mandrel inside moved upward when the tool was slammed and amputated his right ring fingertip.

An employee was performing loading operations on a tanker truck when they fell 11 feet and 2 inches from the truck to the ground between the caged gangway access and the truck, resulting in fractures to the left wrist, orbital cheek bone, and pelvis.

An employee was troubleshooting a compressor that had shut down. The employee believed that a 1-inch choke nipple was plugged and drained fluids via the dump line to check the choke nipple. The employee then loosened a union and a flash fire occurred, burning the employee's hands and face.

An employee was assisting in rigging up a well servicing rig on a new job site. When the employee completed his task he jumped approximately 36 inches from the deck of the rig to the ground below. The employee sustained a fractured right ankle.
An employee's right ring finger was crushed in a closing truck tailgate, resulting in an amputation at the first knuckle.

An employee was preparing a well for chemical preservation. The employee attached a 2x6-inch metal nipple and a 2-inch metal elbow to the casing valve. The employee then opened the casing valve to bleed down the casing pressure and stepped back to allow the pressure to bleed off. The employee started to reach down to partially close the valve, but before they could make contact with the valve, the nipple and elbow disconnected from the casing valve and struck the employee on the right leg, resulting in a fractured tibia and fibula.

An employee and a co-worker picked up a 48-inch steel pipe wrench to size up a saver sub. While sizing up the wrench, the swivel engaged and the pipe wrench hit the saver sub, causing the wrench to swing around and strike the employee in the left arm and chest area. The employee suffered a lacerated spleen.

An employee was tightening a clamp on a polish rod for an oil well. A bottom clamp slipped and caught his right index finger against the carrier on the bridle of the pump jack. The right index finger was amputated near the middle joint.
An employee was unloading a pumping unit with a winch truck. The winch cable bounced, striking the employee in the head. The employee lost consciousness and was hospitalized.

An employee was removing an elevator bell when the winch line caught slack, causing the bell to fall and crush the employee's right hand. The employee's right ring and middle fingertips were amputated.
An employee was unloading diesel to an above-ground diesel tank. When opening the fuel valve, the employee fell backward onto the ground, resulting in a broken leg.
An employee was pressure washing pipes when the fitting on the spray wand broke and the hot water contacted the employee, resulting in burns to his stomach and thighs.

An employee was flowing a gas well. An ice plug formed in the line (upstream) and restricted pressure downstream. The employee began bleeding off the line downstream and the ice plug released. This caused a pressure difference, sending the ice plug downstream. The ball valve that was used to bleed the line was blown off, striking the employee in the right bicep and causing a laceration. The employee was hospitalized.

An temporary employee was pressure-washing the deck of a vessel. As he walked, his foot slipped into an opening in the grating on the scaffold. He fell into the opening and his lower right arm passed through the 40,000 psi water stream, which cut it and an artery.

On March 2, 2022, an employee was using a pressure washer to clean a natural gas compressor. When the employee attempted to adjust the slack on the pressure washing hose the water stream struck his right foot, resulting in a laceration to the top of the foot that required hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was holding tubing slips as they were lowered. The slips caught the employee's left little finger. The finger was amputated and the employee was hospitalized.

During rigging down at a drilling rig, an employee was about to move his positioning device when he fell through a hole in the rig floor. He landed on the ground about 14 feet below and suffered a dislocated right hip and broken left and right wrists.

An employee was helping move a drill pipe into position. While the pipe was being lifted, the lifting eye came out and the pipe fell, striking the employee in the abdomen. The employee suffered an internal injury and was hospitalized.
An employee was running sucker rods back into an oil/gas well. The transfer chain broke and struck the employee in the head, lacerating it and causing him to lose consciousness.
An employee was pulling tongs onto a pipe. As he placed his hand on the tong door handle, the door caught his right hand against the pipe. His middle and ring fingertips were amputated.

An employee was tripping out pipe using a workover rig. The blocks were coming down with the elevators and the employee was pulling down on the ears when his left index finger was caught between the ears and the pipe. The finger was amputated.
An employee cut into a hollow rod that was filled with fluid pressure, which caused a bar to flip and hit the employee's left arm. The employee's forearm was broken.
An employee was walking into a cabin when a gust of wind blew the door shut. The employee's right index fingertip was caught in the door and amputated at the first knuckle.
During a core sampling operation, an employee's right index finger was pinched between slip bowls and the drill pipe. The finger was amputated.

An employee was holding square tubing in place while another employee used a sledgehammer to hammer it. The employee was trying to straighten up the tubing when the sledgehammer smashed his thumb. He was hospitalized and underwent a medical amputation to the thumb tip.
An employee was walking on a rig deck. A cap failed when the employee stepped on it, and the employee's leg entered the hole. The employee suffered lacerations to the upper rear thigh.
An employee fell from a ladder, resulting in fractures and multiple internal injuries that required hospitalization.

An employee was walking toward a pump on which he was installing a new suction manifold. He tripped over the old manifold, lying on the ground, and fell. He suffered a compound fracture to the left forearm and was hospitalized.
An employee was straightening a load suspended from a forklift. The load came off the forklift and struck the employee's arm, breaking it.

An employee was bringing up pipe from down-hole. The employee's left ring finger was caught between the tongs where the employee was working and the arm of the tongs on the opposite side. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was operating hydraulic tongs during operations to remove a drill pipe from an oil and gas well. A 5 1/2-inch tubular struck the employee's right hip. He suffered non-displaced fractures to the pelvis, a rib, and the right ulna; as well as lacerations above his right eye and on the top of his head.
An employee was working on a precision machine tool. The machine caught the employee's glove and pulled in the employee's right hand, resulting in the amputation of the middle finger.

An employee was connecting power cables/cords on the floor of a rig. The employee was partially standing on the bat door when it activated, causing the employee to fall approximately 30 feet to the ground and sustain eight fractured ribs, a punctured lung, and bruising to the kidney, liver, and spleen.

On April 7, 2022, an employee was conducting a high-pressure wash of a frack tank when oil and gas frack water entered their eyes, resulting in blindness in the right eye. An eyewash station was not available at the time.
An employee was working on a pulling unit when their left little finger was caught between some polish rod slants and moving equipment resulting in amputation of the finger.

An employee was untangling cable on the drum located on the back of a wireline truck. Both of his hands were caught in the cable and pulled into the compensator shield resulting in amputation of his left little finger.
Employees were installing well head equipment. An employee's left middle finger was caught between a bolt and a flange that was being installed. The finger was amputated.

At about 11:20 a.m. on April 16, 2022, an employee was using a wrench to tighten a polish rod at an oil well head. The wrench slipped off the collar. As the employee reached behind the wrench to replace it on the collar, the stuffing box slid down, trapping the employee's right index finger against the wrench. The fingertip was amputated near the nail bed.

A load securement strap on a flatbed trailer was being loosened when the load of pipes shifted and fell on an employee. The employee was hospitalized with fractures to the jaw, shoulder, ribs, and femur.

A casing swage (weighing approximately 50 pounds) was being installed to a joint of casing in order to circulate drilling mud through the casing. The swage was approximately 40 feet in the air when it came free and fell striking an employee in the hard hat. The employee sustained a skull fracture.
Two employees were installing a belt in a pump motor's belt and pulley system. When the pulleys were rotated, one employee's right ring fingertip was caught by the belt and pulley and amputated.

An employee was diagnosing a leak on a frac pump. A 2-inch hose separated, and the employee fell backward. His right leg was caught between the railing and the fluid end and was broken above the ankle.

A crew was changing out a vertically oriented 8-inch check valve on a pipeline. When a flange was opened by loosening bolts, pentane and other flammable hydrocarbon products in the pipe released from the pipeline, creating a vapor cloud and resulting in a massive fire and explosion. The vessel and associated equipment/piping were engulfed in fire for about eight hours. Eight employees were sent to the hospital. Six employees were treated and released. Two employees were admitted for treatment of thermal and chemical burns to the face, neck, and hands.

An employee was using a hammer and wrench to loosen a nut on a valve. The employee's right little finger was caught between the wrench and the valve body, causing the amputation of the fingertip above the first knuckle.

An employee was cleaning out the screen on a plug catcher. The employee's left middle finger was caught between the screen and the deck of the plug catcher. The fingertip was amputated at the tuft of the last phalanx.

An employee was lifting a 20-foot long, metal pole for the meter run in the dog house. The pole touched a live electric line over the doghouse and the employee was shocked. The employee then dropped the pole and fell to the ground. The employee sustained electrical burns on both arms and the front of the torso.
Two employees were trying to adjust a 1,500-pound accumulator. It tipped over and caught one of the employees, breaking his right leg.
An employee was placing chemical hoses at the top of the tub of a blender. His right ring finger was pinched inside an inlet valve actuator and was amputated to the first joint.
An employee was helping purge a product line with nitrogen. A piece of solidified plastic came out of the product pipeline at the open flange end and impaled the employee's hand.
An employee was removing a standpipe with his hands on a wrench and bolt. Once the bolts were loosened, the standpipe flange slipped and fell on the employee's right forearm, crushing it.
An employee was performing maintenance on a forklift when they fell approximately 2 feet off the forklift and landed on a tote, resulting in multiple fractured ribs.

A crew was tripping out and laying down pipe. The injured employee was holding the mud box to capture fluids. The joint of pipe was started into the wrangler trough. The elevators were pulled rapidly sideways, releasing the pipe. The pipe came down and struck the injured employee on the hardhat, knocking him unconscious and causing a laceration to the head.

An employee was transferring joints of casing from one side of a pipe delivery system to the other when the casing rolled forward and pinned the employee's right leg against the side of the pipe delivery system. The employee sustained a fractured tibia and fibula.

An employee was tasked with checking a centrifuge on the centrifuge stand on a drilling rig. While descending the stairs, the employee slipped and fell to the floor, sustaining a broken bone in their foot, a broken ankle, and back and chest pain.
An employee opened a generator cap and received third degree burns requiring hospitalization.
An employee was pushing tongs away from casing collars. The tongs were let down and pinched the employee's right ring finger against the casing collars, causing an amputation to the fingertip.
An employee was turning to walk away from a compressor when a 2-inch pipeline detached and struck the employee's back. The employee suffered a back fracture and was hospitalized.

Employees were assisting with a rig down by picking up trash and lumber. While cleaning the site, an employee of Caltex was struck by a forklift. The employee sustained a tear to their spleen resulting in hospitalization.

An employee was spotting as a storage tank was offloaded from a truck to the ground. The winch cable caught on a post; the post then broke loose and was thrown into the air, striking the employee's head.
A nylon strap parted, causing VFD power cables to fall onto an employee.
An employee was relighting the pilot light within the fire tube of the treater. Flame blew out of the exhaust barrel and caused second degree burns to the employee's face.

An employee used a wire brush to clean the threads of two 10-foot joints of 2-inch figure 1502 iron pipe, which were sitting on the rack of a monorail trailer. As the employee rotated the pipe inward to clean the threads of the innermost joint, the opposite end of the pipe dislodged from the rack and fell to the ground. As it fell, the end nearest to the employee levered upward and pinched their right thumb between the two joints of pipe. The employee sustained a laceration and fracture to the thumb.

An employee was using two rod wrenches to tighten a stand of rods as they were placed back down a hole. While wrenching the rods, the employee went to tighten the rod boxes. The employee lost grip on the wrenches and their left little finger was caught between the wrench handles resulting in amputation of the fingertip.

An employee was doing maintenance work on the power-end crankshaft of a fluid pump. His little finger was caught between the crankshaft and the main bearing, causing a laceration to the upper finger area and a partial amputation.

An employee was lifting a 100-pound exhaust manifold off an engine using a service truck crane. While he was maneuvering the manifold toward the bed of his truck, it struck his left index finger and caught it against a pressure relief valve. He suffered a laceration and fracture to the finger and was hospitalized.

The injured employee was helping another employee with the insertion of a securement pin when their right middle finger was caught between the pin and the slot, causing a partial amputation to the fingertip.

Employees were rigging down. The injured employee was hooking up a flow line to a manifold. When he stepped back, he fell through a gap in the floor of the shaker, landing on his head on the ground about 12 feet below. He suffered multiple skull fractures and bleeding on the brain and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a truck to barricade a road. A motor vehicle, traveling at about 65 miles per hour, rear-ended the truck. The employee suffered a lip laceration, fractured vertebrae, and a tear in the inner layer of the aorta.
An employee was attempting to remove an air line from a fireball pump when their right hand got caught by the piston on the pump, resulting in a fingertip amputation on the ring finger.
A hose failed during the removal and replacing of a pump filter. Hot fluid from the hose burned the left side of an employee's body.
While walking down steps, an employee twisted his ankle, then fell and hit his head. The employee was hospitalized with a concussion.

An employee was assisting a co-worker in fitting a stand pipe into the mousehole of a drilling well. As a joint of the drill pipe was being lifted up, the employee placed his right hand around the drill pipe. The drill pipe moved unexpectedly, causing the employee's right middle finger to be caught between the pipe and the hydraulic power unit. The employee suffered a fingertip amputation above the first knuckle.

Employees were watching a hot oil truck pump hot oil down the well. The vac truck driver was instructed to shut the vac truck valve off to bleed pressure. The hot oiler bled pressure off into the vac hose causing the hose to have too much pressure. The hose blew off and struck three employees. One employee was hospitalized for multiple fractures to their right leg.

An employee went up on a derrick to unchain the block. The tubing line came back in and pushed him. He fell 12 feet from a gird at a pulling unit on the derrick and landed on a metal plate on the back of the rig floor. The employee sustained broken ribs and a puncture wound to the throat.

An employee was operating a vertical mill when their glove became caught in the mill head and their left hand was pulled into the machine. The injured employee sustained a laceration/avulsion to the left hand.

An employee lit a cigarette lighter to check the volume of chemical in an ISO tank. The flame ignited the remaining vapors in the ISO tank causing a flash fire. The employee suffered second degree burns on the face and arms.

Two employees were loosening a union. One of the employees was striking the union to loosen it when the ball valve broke off the pipe on the pressure side. The ball valve struck the employee's head and knocked him over. His head landed on a piece of piping.
An employee was making confined space entries to clean a tank when they began to experience symptoms of heat-related illness, cramps, and heat exhaustion. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was using a tail rope to guide a stand of drill pipe into the mousehole from the derrick board. The tail rope became caught in the single joint elevators and tangled around the employee's lower right leg resulting in fractures to the tibia and fibula.
Employees had been nippling up the blow out preventer (BOP) system. The work floor of the rig unfolded and descended on top of an employee resulting in contusions to multiple body parts.

A rig crew was preparing to push back the mud motor to set it down behind the rotary in order to install a bit breaker into the rotary. As an employee moved from a squatting position, his right foot slid underneath the mud motor and became caught between the mud motor and the rotary mat. The employee sustained fractures to the foot and two toes, as well as a laceration to the bottom of the foot.

Maintenance was being performed on a machine that inverts coal cars to dump product out of the cars. The machine was in the inverted position at the time. An employee was standing on fiberglass grating when it came loose causing them to fall 21 feet to the surface below. The employee sustained a broken arm. The employee was wearing fall protection, but it was not connected at the time of the fall.
An employee was securing a well cap when it slid off the side of the sub-base, pinning his right leg against the sub-base and breaking his femur.

An employee was cleaning a derrick with a power washer. The employee slipped on a wet surface while untangling the power washer hose. As he reached out to catch himself, part of the derrick caught his right little finger and removed the flesh, exposing the bone.
An employee was measuring the sheave of a pumping unit for replacement when his right ring finger was caught between the panels of the weight guard, amputating the fingertip.

An employee was walking across a job site carrying half-full 5-gallon buckets of fluid when the loop of his left boot lace caught a lace hook on his right boot, causing him to fall to the ground on his left side. The employee suffered broken ribs and a punctured lung.
An employee was pulling a rod out of a drill stem. His left hand was caught between two pieces of steel on the rig, and the pinch point amputated the tip of his little finger.
An employee was walking under a rig floor when a piece of floor gap filler came loose and landed on the employee's head. The employee suffered four broken vertebrae.

An employee was investigating the condition of the flame inside an oilfield separation vessel when the sight glass cover was expelled, allowing the heat to burn and blister the employee's right cheek.

An employee was tasked with offloading a marine vessel. He was resetting the loading arm back into place when his left hand was caught between the load arm head and a fixed dock component, amputating his index and middle fingertips.

Combustible gas had been vented from a combustor so that its pilot assembly could be safely relit. When an employee relit the pilot light, some remaining gas ignited, and the resulting flash fire burned his left hand and right forearm.

An employee was driving an ATV on a private roadway to respond to a well control event. The employee lost control of the ATV and used their left leg to try and prevent the ATV from flipping over. The employee's left leg was fractured.

An employee was trying to prevent a block from swaying as it was attached to a crane. The crane moved, and the employee's left hand was caught in the sheave of the main block. The employee suffered amputation of 1/4 of the left ring fingertip and a laceration to the little finger.
While rolling a drill pipe on a pipe rack, an employee's left middle fingertip was crushed between the pipes and the pipe rack resulting in amputation.

An employee was rebuilding a setting tool, attempting to seat the lower cylinder onto the cylinder head by tapping the setting tool onto the trailer floor. As the employee pushed down on the setting tool, the mandrel stroked in the setting sleeve and pinched and amputated their right middle finger.

Two employees were performing maintenance on an amine pump in the plant. A flash fire occurred, causing burns to both employees. One employee was hospitalized with burns to the face, shoulder, and back. The other employee was treated and released.

A forklift was lowering two drill collars onto two boards that had been placed on the ground. An employee was standing in line with the collars, with his right foot positioned to stop them if they rolled off the boards. The collars rolled and pinned his right foot, breaking his ankle.

An employee was handling a hydraulic skid cylinder using a forklift. His left hand was pinched between the cylinder pad eye and the skid guide slots. He suffered partial amputations to the ring and middle fingers.

A drill pipe fell. Its joint struck an employee on the right side of the hard hat, then hit his right shoulder. The employee lost consciousness and suffered a laceration to the head and shoulder, fractures to the spine, and a broken shoulder blade.
An employee was checking around a work area. The employee tripped on a ground rod that was sticking up about 2 inches from the ground and suffered a broken left knee.

An employee was holding a tong that was gripping a string of pipe that was within a mouse hole on a drilling rig. The crew was trying to remove 2 of the 3 sections of pipe from a string. On the third attempt to attach a pipe spinner unit, the pipe spinner unit impacted the employee's left thumb. The thumb was broken and lacerated.

An employee was carrying pipe slips across the rig floor to place them on the drill string in the rig floor when his right foot slipped into the floor opening and he fell. The pipe slips fell on his ankle causing a fracture. Additionally, the employee's knee was dislocated.
An employee was stepping from a ladder to an elevated work platform, when they slipped and fell 22 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured right leg that required hospitalization.

On the morning of July 21, 2022, two employees were at a stacked rig, removing 4-inch high-pressure piping. They began to break the nuts loose on the saddle clamp bolts under the valve tree. As they were breaking loose the last nut, the piping suddenly rotated in the saddle clamp and the transducer valve tree (about 4 feet tall, weighing 250 pounds) pivoted 90 degrees toward the ground and landed on one of the employees. The hammer union ears at the top of the valve tree struck him in the middle of the shoulder and back, causing contusions.

An employee was about to change out the choke parts to fix a leaking choke on the belly dump of a gas production unit (GPU). While the choke was being unbolted, pressure came through it, blowing the employee backward and causing lacerations and broken bones in their face.
An employee was working on the rig floor when they began to experience dizziness and cramping in their legs and arms due to dehydration and heat stress. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was using a screwdriver to scrape wax off a pump. His hand was pulled into the stuffing box, and the rod inside the box broke his thumb and caused amputations to his fingertips.
An employee was installing oil drilling tubing when his middle finger was caught between a ram and a blowout preventer. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was carrying a 65-pound metal plunger on his left shoulder when he tripped over a hose and fell forward. The plunger fell on his left hand, causing two fractures and crushing the index finger and the middle fingertip.
An employee was using a hydraulic tugger to lift a driller cage. The chain that the driller cage was hanging on broke and the driller cage struck the employee's face resulting in a mouth injury.
An employee was tripping pipe out of a hole on a 96 F day when he passed out due to heat exhaustion.
An employee had been training and running casing. After returning to the office he was hospitalized for heat exhaustion.

On August 3, 2022, an employee was working throughout the day, lifting boards onto pipe racks and truck trailers. Before lunchtime, the employee started to feel weak on the right side of his body and the left side of his face was drooping.
An employee began to feel sick after working for 12 hours in the sun. The employee was admitted to the hospital due to dehydration.
An employee was helping rig up a vibrating line. The line's end came loose and struck the outside of his calf, causing swelling and a hematoma.

An employee was pushing back a stand of drill pipe on a rig floor. He slipped and fell forward, putting his hands out in front of him to brace his fall. The drill pipe moved back slightly and pinched his right index and middle fingers against the rig floor, resulting in the amputation of the two fingertips above the first knuckle.

Employees were troubleshooting a triethylene glycol (TEG) pump on an ethylene glycol vessel system. After shutting down the pump, employees closed the valve on the system. Pressure built up and blew holes in the vessels (through the walls of the pipe). The employees were sprayed by hot liquid glycol and one employee sustained burns.

An employee was cleaning subs (wireline parts) by hand in the parts washer using a wire brush when a small sliver of metal punctured his left index finger. The employee was later hospitalized with an infection and required surgery.
An employee was repositioning a piece of equipment on a trailer when their finger was caught between the piece of equipment and a hydraulic fitting. The employee's fingertip was partially amputated.

Employees were taking down a cratered pumping unit. The pump jack beam had been removed from the unit and the employees were preparing to take off another piece when the beam fell onto one employee's legs, breaking both of them. The employee required surgery.
An employee was running rods into a well. When the tongs were engaged, they caught the tip of his left thumb, causing its amputation.

An employee was performing backflow operations at a tank battery. After shutting a valve, pressure built in the line causing the line to rupture. The employee was standing near the line when it ruptured and their right arm and the right side of their torso were struck by hot oil, water, and sand (approximately 147 degrees) resulting in severe burns requiring hospitalization.

The injured employee was observing another employee utilizing a forklift to lift a tool off a testing cart. After the forklift lifted the took, the driver began to back up. The forklift rolled over an uneven surface which cased the lifting strap holding the tool to disengage from the forklift forks and drop to the ground. As it dropped, it contacted an additional tool stand near where the injured employee was located. When the injured employee noticed the tool stand falling over, he put his left hand out and it was caught between the tool and the stand resulting in amputation of the middle and ring fingertips.

An employee was maneuvering a steel pipe (blind) during a rigging operation. A malfunction caused the blind to land on the employee's left hand resulting in amputations to the index and middle fingers at the first joint.

An employee was standing over a hydraulic cylinder, unpinning a saddle clamp that held the cylinder in place. When the clamp came free, the employee fell to the deck and suffered a broken knee and wrist.
An employee was working on a rig floor when a swivel flipped over and pinned the employee to the deck. The employee suffered a broken collarbone.

An employee was removing a drill pipe from a derrick. When the employee reached out to remove the winch line, the pipe rotated and the line caught the employee's left index finger. The finger was amputated at the first joint.
While draining a pump, an employee was splashed with sulfuric acid and sustained burns.
An employee was sprayed with 12.5 percent sodium hypochlorite when a line burst on a pumping unit. The employee suffered a chemical burn.
An employee was disassembling a U-joint. The U-joint was in a vise, and the employee was striking it with a ball peen hammer to break it free, when a piece of metal entered the employee's eye.
An employee was tripping out pipe and racking it. The employee lost their footing and their right hand was caught between pipes, which broke two of the employee's fingers.

A dump truck was trying to avoid rocks on a trail when its left-side wheels left the trail. The truck rolled about three times, and the driver suffered a neck strain, bumps and bruises, a laceration to the forehead that required stitches, and a laceration to the right forearm.

An employee was investigating a jammed garage door on a storage shed. One of the two door cables had come off the pulley; the other was stuck. When the tension was released on the stuck cable, it fell off the pulley, pulled taut around the employee's right thumb, and amputated half to three-quarters of an inch from the tip. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was doing repair work on an oil/gas well. While the rods were being spaced out, the elevator caught the bottom of the horse's head and knocked it off. It hit the ground and rolled over on top of the employee, who was working on the floor. The employee suffered a broken pelvis and a broken right femur and was hospitalized.
An employee was clearing sand from an auger. Once the sand was freed, the auger engaged and amputated his left little fingertip at the first knuckle.

An employee was troubleshooting the internal part of an electrical plug. An energized wire popped free from under the plug and contacted the employee's right index finger, burning the finger and the web of skin between it and the thumb.
An employee was assisting with a car fire and became ill. The employee was hospitalized with a cardiac issue.
An employee suffered burns to the left hand, left arm, and face while working on a flare.
An employee was working on a rig floor, removing a bowl and slips from a wellhead. The slips moved and crushed his left hand.

A crane's auxiliary line was tangled with its anti-two-block device's weight. An employee pulled on the line to free it; the slack released, and his left little fingertip was caught between the weight and the line. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was loosening a flange in a hydrogen unit. Residual gas escaped and ignited, causing second-degree burns to the side of the employee's face and elbow.
At about 4:30 p.m. on September 7, 2022, an employee fell while walking down a flight of steps outside. She suffered a compound fracture to the femur.

An employee had climbed the derrick of a workover rig to cut a rope that was caught in the tubing board. When the tubing board fell and released, it bounced the rig and the employee fell. He caught himself on a section of the derrick frame about 10 to 15 feet below, stopping his fall but suffering a spinal injury at the neck, internal bleeding, lacerations, and contusions.

An employee was trying to untangle a chain from the trough of a catwalk. A winch was connected to the chain. The winch activated and the employee's hand became caught between the edge of the catwalk trough and the hook from the winch, amputating the employee's finger and thumb.
An employee was using a pipe wrench to loosen a collar on a drilling tube. The pipe wrench broke loose and pinched the employee's right ring finger against the ground. The fingertip was amputated.

An employee was taking apart a meter. As the employee was taking apart the flow control choke valve, it came apart under pressure and a piece of it struck the employee. The employee suffered a laceration and a skull fracture above the left ear, as well as an injury to the left forearm.

Employees were reconnecting a well head and hanging it back on the pumping unit. The block of the workover rig slipped, fell from the rod basket, and struck an employee. The employee sustained a crushed right leg below the knee and a fractured pelvis.
An employee was run over by a telehandler. The employee suffered a broken pelvis and was hospitalized.

An employee working at a well site was preparing to deliver chemicals, which were in bulk totes mounted on a truck, to the field tank. While disembarking from the rear of the truck, the employee slipped and fell approximately 4 feet from the truck's ladder to the ground, resulting in a boot top fracture to his left tibia and fibula.

A drill collar was being lowered from a higher elevation pad next to the location where the rig was located. An employee placed a board as a chock under the drill collar. As the forklift forks were being removed from under the collar, the collar started to roll. The drill collar caught the right edge of the employee's boot and began to pull his leg under the collar. The employee sustained compound fractures to both bones in his lower right leg.

Two employees were performing routine maintenance activities on instrumentation equipment when a caustic line going into an instrument began to release sodium hydroxide and propane, resulting in burns to the face and upper body due to contact with sodium hydroxide. Both employees were hospitalized.

An employee was standing at the top of the rig floor stairs guiding the rotary hose that was being hoisted with the rig winch. The hose was nearly at the rig floor when the wing half at the bottom of the hose was caught underneath the stairs. The stairs became disconnected from the rig floor and the employee at the top of the stairs fell approximately 15 to 18 feet to the ground.

An employee was walking alongside a burned-out truck that was being moved into a yard by a tow truck. The employee's right foot passed in front of the driver's side tire rim, and the tire ran over the employee's steel-toed footwear. The employee suffered a lacerated little toe, a broken middle toe, and another laceration.
An employee was transferring an oil/gas scrubber into a scrap bin. The employee's arm was caught and broken between the scrubber and the wall of the bin.
An employee was loading valves onto a truck. A valve was dropped and debris from the trailer struck the employee in the left eye, injuring it.

An employee was unloading product from a sack, carried on a forklift, into a hopper. The forklift lowered the sack, which pinched the employee's left forearm against the hopper. The employee was hospitalized with a muscular injury requiring surgery.
An employee was driving a tractor when it flipped and pinned him, breaking his leg.
An employee was helping as a crane lowered a large metal plate. As the plate was being put into place, it struck the employee's left foot and broke it. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was working on a piece of equipment. The employee's right ring finger was caught between a tool and the piece of equipment. The fingertip was partially amputated.

An employee was on top of a haul truck trailer, taking tiedowns for a pumping unit's crank guard to be lifted with a crank. The employee fell approximately 5 feet off the trailer and landed on one foot, resulting in fractures to the tibia and fibula, which caused a muscle injury. The employee was hospitalized and had surgery.

Employees were preparing a main fractionator pump for blinding when the case drain developed a leak. Butane and alkylate were released and the vapors reached an ignition source resulting in a fire. Two employees sustained burns to the upper chest and face. One employee was treated and released and one employee was hospitalized.

Employees were making a tie-in on an 8-inch natural gas line by attaching two squeeze-off tools to shut off the line. When the polyethylene pipe was cut, one of the squeeze-off tools failed, causing a leak that resulted in an ignition. One employee was burned over about 50 percent of their body; the other was burned over about 10 percent.

An employee had been lowered down to a catwalk with a hoist. He was unhooking the hoist from the rotating head when it fell over. His left leg was pinned between the rotating head and a pipe retention post, resulting in swelling and inability to bear weight on his leg.

An employee was on the rig floor standing on the off driller's side at the stump to help run pipe casing. As the next joint was being brought in, the employee's finger was caught between the stump and the projector on the joint. The employee's right ring finger was amputated.
An employee was climbing a ladder on the side of a trailer. He slipped and fell to the cement floor, striking his head and sustaining head injuries.

An employee was working on an effluent water treatment unit. The employee began to feel discomfort in the upper respiratory tract, eyes, and abdomen and was hospitalized, having suffered from possible sulfuric acid exposure.
On October 18, 2022, an employee was struck on the back by a falling wellhead. The employee was hospitalized for a back injury.
An employee was measuring the voltage of an electrical transformer following a new installation when an arc flash occurred. The employee sustained burns to both right and left hands and fingers.
An employee was inspecting a mud pump when its piston shifted. His fingertip was caught and amputated between the piston ring and the cylinder liner.

An employee was installing a wiper rubber on tubing before pulling the tubing out of a well. His right ring finger was caught between two pieces of metal on the tubing tongs, and the fingertip was amputated.
An employee was inspecting a gas regulator when the gas ignited and he was burned by a flash fire.

A crew was servicing a well. The injured employee was using a manual backup tool to hold a pipe while it was pulled from a well to be put into an x-ray machine. The pipe slipped and the employee's finger was caught between the tool and the x-ray machine, causing the left ring fingertip to be crushed and amputated.

Oil and gas employees were working with casing strings when a side door elevator's door came open and struck an employee. The employee was knocked down and sustained a rib and collarbone fracture as well as other small fractures. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was cleaning out a conveyor belt chute when the hinged access door fell, striking the employee's right hand. The employee sustained a crushing injury to the hand and a laceration to the palm.

An employee was taking measurements from a scaffold to fabricate and install an insulation cover on a boiler system. A nearby 1/2-inch screw pipe with a pressure transmitter broke and sprayed the employee with hot boiler feed water. The employee sustained burns to the back of their legs.

An employee was driving an all-terrain vehicle to inspect a well. The vehicle struck an uneven surface, ejecting the employee from the vehicle to the ground. The employee sustained bilateral leg fractures.

An employee was assisting with rigging up a derrick. He was at the back end of the rig when he grabbed a bar with his right hand. As the rig was going up, his right hand went under the tail screw, which crushed his little finger, resulting in amputation.
An employee was under a truck checking its brakes. The truck was moved and struck him, breaking and lacerating his right leg.

On November 9, 2022, while troubleshooting a furnace, a bit was pushed from the pre-heating dome and fell to the cart below, striking the injured employee and pinning his left leg between the cart and the bit. The employee's left ankle was fractured and required surgery. The employee also sustained burns to the right hip and thigh, left ankle, and right hand.

A crew was on a drilling floor making a drill pipe connection. One employee was using a 5-foot bar with the pipe tongs, to apply pressure, to make the pipe fitting tight. The bar slipped and struck the employee in the chest, resulting in rib fractures to the right side.

An employee was in the basket of an aerial work platform pressure washing a shaker roof. While rotating the wand, an unexpected pressure release occurred. The wand was one inch from his right knee and injected him with fluid at 2,900 PSI.

An employee was removing a pigging tool from a receiver barrel on a natural gas pipeline. When he opened the receiver door, residual pressure in the vessel (caused by plugged blowdown valves) caused the door to strike his left leg and break his left femur.

An employee was walking through a hydraulic fracturing work site performing manual fueling operations. As they were walking, the employee slipped on a chemical known as SAFE-BFH-2 (High pH Buffer) and fell to the ground. Their right lower back, bilateral legs, and bilateral lower hip areas contacted the chemical and the employee was hospitalized for chemical burns.

An employee was changing rams in a blowout preventer on a snubbing unit. A nearby co-worker handed the employee a block when it slipped and fell onto the employee's left little fingertip, resulting in amputation.

A derrickman was positioned in a rod basket to remove a rod elevator. After doing so, the employee began wiping the rod with a rag and the rag became entangled around the rod. The employee's glove was caught in the rag, resulting in a degloving injury that resulted in medical amputation of the left little finger.

An employee was using a high-pressure hose to wash a tank. The valve at the end of the hose broke due to the pressure, causing the hose to then strike the employee in the throat. The employee sustained severe injuries to the pharynx and neck.
An employee was walking across the pad when they were struck by a pickup truck that was backing up. The employee sustained a neck fracture, rib fractures, and a crushed shoulder.

An employee was working in a man basket at a wellhead when a fire caused flames to engulf the wellhead. When the fire reached the man basket, the employee jumped. His chest struck valves on the ground about 15 feet below. He was hospitalized, having suffered four broken ribs and a hematoma.

An employee was changing the bearings on a measuring head wheel for a wireline unit. The new bearings were placed and as the wheel was lowered back into the housing, the wheel pinched the tip of the employee's finger, resulting in a left middle fingertip amputation.

An employee was prepping cardboard trays for use by nearby equipment when they were struck by a box clamp truck. The clamp attachment struck the employee's left leg, knocking her to the ground. Then the clamp truck ran over her right foot. The employee sustained fractures and lacerations to the foot and toes.
An employee was prepping for the inspection of a pickup bed when asphalt became unstuck and slid down, striking the employee. They sustained a left foot, ankle, and right leg fracture.
An employee was repairing an overhead door when they fell from a mobile stair platform to the floor and sustained a fractured left leg.

An employee was helping a crew rig up a tree. The employee was holding a wrench with his right hand to keep the bottom nut on the tree from turning when another crew member began to torque up the top bolt. As the bolt turned, the employee's fingertip was crushed between the wrench and the tree. The employee sustained an amputation to the middle fingertip.

An employee was working with makeup tongs (manual pipe tongs) to make them clasp. The top drive torque spun counter clockwise, causing the tongs to clasp and the snub line to pull tight. The entire pipe stand flexed and the pin end lost contact with the floor, skidding backward toward the injured employee. The tongs and stand of drill pipe struck the employee on their left side resulting in fractures to the left tibia, fibula, and ulna.

An employee was gathering straps for maneuvering pipe in the field while a trackhoe was being relocated. The track of the vehicle caught an 8x16 wooden mat, which struck the employee on his right leg, resulting in a fracture and hospitalization.

An employee was removing casing from the well bore when a lift nubbing came out of the box end of the pipe. This caused the joint of the casing to fall through the elevator and strike the employee. They sustained a fractured clavicle and scapula.

Employees were working on a drilling rig. They were putting bushings in with a hydraulic hoist when the cable became tangled in the derricks above. The hydraulic hoist cable came loose and threw the injured employee 15 feet into a piece of machinery used to screw together joints of drill pipe. The employee lost consciousness and sustained a head laceration that required staples and a knee laceration that required surgery.

An employee was inspecting and repairing a tank when they fell seven feet through the floating aluminum roof of a tank to the tank floor. They sustained a laceration near the right ear and a contusion on the back of the head.
An employee was maneuvering an 85-foot vertical pipe into position on an oil rig when it slipped from the clamp and fell onto his foot, resulting in amputation of the big toe.

An employee was working with a crew on the rig floor tripping pipe into the hole. They applied the manual tongs as and the line that supplied air to the clutch froze. When the driller started the draw works forward, the rotary turned unexpectedly. One of the snub lines, which anchor the tongs in place, was secured to the rig but not to the tongs. The tongs turned and struck the worker in the chest and the employee sustained collapsed lungs, a bruised liver and kidneys, a damaged spleen, and broken ribs.
An employee was responding to a gas release at the refinery when the gas ignited, causing the employee to sustain burns to the face.

An employee was working with a catwalk, changing out a cable. After removing the skate cable, the employee and a co-worker were adjusting the skate to install the new cable. The co-worker positioned himself on the driller side of the catwalk; the injured employee was on the off driller side. As the employee made his way down the catwalk, he placed his right hand on the index pin of the catwalk trough to gain leverage. As the skate's momentum carried it forward, it pinched the employee's right thumb against the pin. The tip of the thumb was amputated.

An employee was on a ladder accessing the top of a vessel. He was using a hand wrench to tighten an outlet piping flange. The wrench slipped off the flange, causing the employee to fall 8 feet to the ground and sustain 4 rib and 3 back fractures. Fall protection was not worn at the time.

Employees were performing a tubing integrity test. As they were blowing down the pressure from the casing, the nipple assembly came off the casing valve flange onto the ground. The nipple threads and casing valve flange threads failed with the pressure, causing the employees to be pushed to the ground. The injured employee sustained a head injury and was hospitalized.

An employee was measuring the produced water depth using a gauge line. After measuring, the employee began climbing down the storage tank ladder and fell. As he fell, his boots became caught between the ladder rungs, causing a right femur and left hip fracture.

An employee was unloading a motor from a flatbed trailer when his foot caught on a board on the trailer, causing him to fall. As he was falling, his right index finger got caught between the motor and its transport carrier, resulting in a fingertip amputation that required surgery.

An employee was putting a collar clamp on 8-inch drill collars in a mouse hole. His right index finger was caught between the collar clamp and a shop hammer (used to tighten collar clamp). The fingertip was amputated and required surgery.

A crew was installing skid rails. The injured employee was checking the alignment of two sections of skid rails when the pieces moved and his right middle and ring fingers were caught in the pin hole connection of the two sections. Both fingertips were amputated.
An employee was leaving the back area of the rig when he stepped between a flare line pipe and a skid. He slipped and fell, fracturing his right leg.

An employee was participating in lifeboat emergency escape training. The lever to drop the lifeboat was actuated while the employee was seated on a solid bench inside the lifeboat. The lifeboat dropped onto the water below. The impact caused the employee to sustain fractured vertebrae and a lacerated liver.
An employee was changing out valves when a piece broke loose. The employee's left little finger became pinched between the valve and piping, resulting in amputation.

An employee was connecting a drill pipe to a stump using a drill string and top drive when the drill pipe contacted their left foot, resulting in amputations of their big and index toes as well as damage to the middle toe.

An employee was drilling an inner mast guide roller and used his hand to balance himself. The guide roller contacted his hand and his finger became crushed between two rollers, resulting in a partial finger amputation.
An employee was exiting the separation area when they slipped on gravel and contacted barbed wire fencing. The employee sustained a puncture wound between the right thumb and index finger.

An employee was disconnecting a winch truck's load line from a load when the winch truck rolled forward, tightening the line. The employee's right hand was caught by the hook and chain of the load line and the index fingertip was amputated below the fingernail.

An employee was setting up lights on opposite ends of beams. Vibrations caused a beam to slip and crush the employee's left index finger against another beam. The employee sustained an open fracture to the finger.

A crew was pinning two cross braces between substructure beams. As the outer cross brace was being pinned, the inner brace (6-inch square tubing, weighing 524 pounds) fell from the transport bracket, catching the employee's finger between the brace and the frame. The employee sustained a left index finger fracture.

An employee was slacking off with the top drive and blocks so the elevators could be latched to a drill collar on the hydraulic catwalk. The employee went to grab the horns of the elevators to help maneuver them around the pipe. His left middle fingertip was crushed between the elevators and lift sub on the drill collar resulting in an amputation.
An employee was assisting with maintenance on a machine when his glove was snagged and his fingers were pulled into the moving parts, resulting in crushed and broken fingers.

On January 9, 2023, a crew was working on a rig at a well site. At approximately 12:30 PM, the rig block fell and struck an employee in the lower right leg, resulting in a leg fracture. The employee was hospitalized.
On January 12, 2023, an employee was moving a drill pipe when they were struck by the drill pipe. The employee sustained a crush injury that resulted in a left ring finger amputation.
An employee was using a torque gun on a bolt head. His left hand was on the flange when the arm rotated down, amputating his left index finger.
An employee was working on the belts of a circulating pump when his fingers were pulled in by the belt. He sustained a right index finger amputation at the second knuckle.
On January 14, 2023, an employee was using a pipe wrench to free up a tube during a back-off procedure. The pipe wrench swung and struck the employee in the head, causing a contusion.
An employee was rotating a lifted bonnet when their finger was pinched between the fork and valve, resulting in a right middle fingertip amputation.

Three employees were using an air motor or "rattle" to remove cement and break up a blockage from the inside of a drill pipe joint. As the injured employee was maneuvering the tool in the drill pipe, it struck a pocket of air buildup between the tool and the blockage, causing the tool to be forced out of the drill pipe and strike the employee in the left rib cage. The employee was hospitalized for fractured and bruised ribs.

On January 20, 2023, an employee delivered a drum to a customer's location, put it on a drum stand, and began adjusting it by sliding it a few inches on the stand. As the drum slid, it pinched the employee's left ring finger against the drum stand frame, causing the fingertip to be amputated.

An employee was preparing to repair a leaking hydraulic hose on a catwalk. The catwalk trough was raised so that the employee could insert maintenance stops that go underneath the trough on both sides. After the employee inserted the maintenance stops, the employee lowered the trough. The trough continued to come down, causing the maintenance stop to come out and strike the employee in the abdomen, resulting in a contusion.

An employee was bolting up internal manways inside a tower. The employee was performing closures on the manways covers when they fell approximately 7 to 9 feet to a lower level. The employee sustained a collapsed left lung, a laceration behind the right knee, and a fractured left scapula.

An employee was helping a crew set up a derrick. The employee was holding the counterweight line away from the derrick to make sure the counterweight itself didn t make contact with the derrick. The counterweight got caught on the derrick, and the line that was pulling the counterweight up was parted. The counterweight came down the guide line that the employee was holding, striking him in the upper left thigh. The employee sustained injuries to his left thigh and the bones around his left eye.
An employee was pulling up wellheads using a slip puller when the tubing line parted, causing the traveling blocks to fall on the employee's arm. The employee sustained an elbow fracture.
An employee was replacing bearings on a compressor shaft when the shaft fell and struck the employee's hand. The employee sustained a laceration and fracture to their left ring finger.

An employee picked up one end of a 300-pound motor, stepped back to put it on a stand, and slipped on ice. As he fell backward, the motor struck him mid-chest. His sternum was fractured in two places and four of his ribs were broken.
On February 2, 2023, an employee was lifting a heating coil when the lift rigging broke. The employee suffered a severe hand injury requiring surgery.
An employee was working under water, using a cavitation cleaning system to clean marine growth off a vessel hull. The machine left a hole at the crease of the finger.

Employees were unbolting the head of a product purge bin utilizing a high-speed cut saw. As the crew was cutting the last of 15 bolts on the purge bin head, a flash fire occurred resulting in burns to four employees.
An employee was doing welding work on a cylinder. The cylinder fell from a skid frame. As the employee went to catch it, it partially amputated the bottom of his left middle finger.
An employee was testing a pipe at an oil/well site. The pipe moved and caught his finger, causing the amputation of the fingertip.

An employee was using a manual metal brake when his hand was caught on the handle, causing his hand/finger to become pinched near the brake shear. The employee sustained an amputation of the right ring fingertip.

An employee was moving casing from the rack to the casing handling system on the rig. The tiering arm scoped out too far and came apart, causing a piece of casing to fall on the employee's leg. They sustained a broken right tibia.

An employee was loosening bolts on a wellhead when they slipped and fell backward approximately 8 feet through an area that was missing floor plates. The employee landed on his back on the ground and sustained a T-12 vertebra fracture that required hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was preparing to move a rig. The employee was on top of the top drive, unlatching the block, when their left little fingertip was amputated.
An employee was cutting a 2 x 4 board using a cordless band saw. The saw moved and lacerated the employee's left index and middle finger, resulting in a middle finger amputation.
An employee's left little finger was pinched between a wrench and a forklift bucket, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was preparing to work on a flare when it discharged oil. The oil struck the employee, causing burns to the body, wrist, and hand.

An employee was assisting in pulling a dryer shaker into position when the tow chain broke and a link from the chain struck the back of his head and knocked him unconscious. The employee sustained a concussion.
An employee was shutting down the pump on a 3-phase separator when it ignited. The employee was hospitalized with burns on their arms, face, chest, and back.

An employee was assisting with pinning a set of stairs when the stairs shifted and struck the employee. The employee was pinched between the stairs and a stationary forklift, resulting in a pelvis fracture.

Employees were pulling up piping on a workover rig. The anchor on the piping got caught on the slip, then the slip got caught on the work floor, pulling it up while the employee was standing on it. When the work floor broke away from the slip, the flooring fell back down to the ground. This caused the employee to fall and sustain a right leg fracture that required hospitalization.

An employee removed plywood that was covering a hole so that a crane could fly in a flange. The employee fell through the hole in the floor, contacting a flange approximately 41 inches below. The employee then fell approximately 47 inches, contacting an aluminum step stool, before falling approximately 19 inches to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with a spinal injury that required surgery.

Two employees were working on a perforating gun when it detonated in the shop. One employee suffered burns to the hands and hearing loss. The other employee's left hand was amputated and they sustained burns to the upper torso. Both employees were hospitalized.
An employee was lowering rods into an oil well when a clamp slipped and crushed their left thumb and index finger, resulting in amputation of the index finger.

An employee was using a crank and cable to lower a light tower due to windy conditions. The light shaft became hung up and released the tension in the cable, which wrapped around the employee's left hand, resulting in amputations of three fingers.

An employee was turning the stompers in preparation to skid the rig. While adjusting the stomper, the guide alignment plate fell off the sector plate, striking the employee's right ring finger. The finger was amputated to the first knuckle.
An employee was participating in work over rig operations. As they were tying ahead, they were caught in the spool and sustained fractures of the tibia, fibula, scapula, and pelvis.
A well tender was working on a gas pipeline when gas ignited. The employee sustained burns to their face.
An employee opened the hatch on an oil tank. The exposure to hydrogen sulfide and other gases caused the employee to become ill, dizzy, and lightheaded; the employee was hospitalized.

An employee was getting ready for work operations when a large gust of wind got under a containment, which then knocked the employee into a pipe rack. The employee suffered a damaged artery in the right leg, with swelling and internal bleeding.

The injured employee was cleaning up and needed to have the trackhoe moved. Another employee moved the trackhoe. When the bucket was lifted, the injured employee's hand was crushed between the bucket and a pipe. The employee sustained a laceration between the middle and ring fingers that required hospitalization.

An employee was assisting a rig crew with stabbing drill pipe into a rotating head. The employee's fingertips became caught between the rotating rubber head and a trip nipple causing lacerations to four fingertips on the left hand and partial amputations to his right ring and little fingers.

An employee was unpinning a beam and removing it from the pinned position. As he pulled it from the pad eyes, the beam fell approximately 18 inches to the ground. The employee's right middle finger was caught between the beam and the ground, resulting in a fracture to the distal portion of his finger that required surgery.

An employee had been working on the rig floor. While pulling rods, the rod elevators jumped off the rod hook and came free from the rod. The rod elevators then fell and struck an employee on the head resulting in a head laceration and a neck fracture.
Employees were changing stabilizing filters on a compressor when condensation caught fire. Two employees sustained second- and third-degree thermal burns to their face and hands.

On March 16, 2023, an employee was working at a well site. The employee, wearing a fall harness, was being lifted off the rig floor with a winch line to close a valve. The winch line caught between a tubing board hinge and a derrick and pulled up, causing the employee to strike the tubing elevators and suffer a broken pelvis. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee had arrived at the work site; he was stepping out of the passenger side of a vacuum truck and miss-stepped. He fell backward to the ground and sustained injury to the back of the head.

An employee was nippling up the stripping of a stripper head. The bottom section of the stripper head came unthreaded from the top section and fell 5 feet, crushing the employee's left thumb against the blowout preventer bolts. The thumb was broken.

An employee was assisting a snubbing unit operator to service the well. While operating hydraulic tongs, the injured employee's glove was entangled in the rotating tong head, resulting in a right finger amputation that required hospitalization.

An employee was repairing a trash pump used to treat water for drilling and fracking. The trash pump vapor locked and the employee was trying to get the pump started when the hose ruptured and they were exposed to a 12.5% bleach solution. The employee sustained chemical burns to their arm and leg.
A safety pin came out of a piece of equipment and struck an employee on the back. He then flipped over a handrail, fell 6 to 8 feet to the ground, and suffered a broken rib.
An employee was troubleshooting an electrical cabinet when there was an arc flash, which burned his right hand and face.

An employee was trying to dislodge a 4-inch metal cone off of a 15-inch metal rod by striking the rod against a fixture. His left index finger became caught between the cone and the fixture, resulting in amputation of the fingertip.
An employee was working on the well head when the service brake broke causing the elevator to fall on their hands. The employee sustained bilateral hand fractures and was hospitalized.

On April 10, 2023, an employee was moving fluid from one end of the pit to the other. To perform this task, a metal grating hatch had to be opened. While standing up, the metal grating hatch closed, amputating the employee's left index and middle fingertips.

An employee was performing maintenance to remove a hose connection when they slipped and fell backward. His left leg struck a bracket and the employee sustained a ligament tear in their left calf that required hospitalization.
An employee was at the pump area pumping salt water to the well when the chain broke and struck the employee. The employee sustained a right femur fracture and broken pelvis.

A crew was removing bolts from the pump's spool piece and rigging the hoist to hold the elevated spool piece out. The crew replaced the witch's hat inside the pump and began to reinstall the spool piece when a burst of fire came out of the pipe and struck the injured employee's face and hand resulting in burns.
An employee was switching the attachment on a pay loader from a bucket to forks. The employee was adjusting the fork width when the fork attachment pinched their right middle finger and fractured it.
An employee was standing on the rig, spooling the line, when the tubing line got caught around both ankles. The unit engaged and he sustained a left ankle fracture and right ankle sprain.
An employee was assisting with latching the elevators around the drill pipe when their right thumb was pinched between the elevator horn and the drill pipe and amputated.
An employee was sampling vacuum tower bottoms when one unplugged and fell on the employee's left hand, resulting in burns to the left hand.

An employee was separating a valve stem from an actuator stem by removing two-piece split nuts that hold it together. The actuator shaft shifted, causing the top half of the split nut to impact and pinch the employee's right thumb against the frame. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was descending a scaffold ladder. He fell from the ladder, landing about 10 feet below and suffering a broken left leg. He was hospitalized and underwent surgery.
Employees were installing a gullwing for a PDS. The gullwing got in a bind; the bind then released and struck the injured employee in the face, causing fractures to the nose and eye socket.

An employee was adjusting the forks of a forklift while the forks were resting on a dividing retention bar. The forks swung and pinched the employee's finger against the bar, causing a laceration that required surgery.
An employee was working at a remote drilling site. The employee was in the derrick preparing to come down when they fell approximately 55 feet to the deck below.

An employee was opening a hatch on a bulk cement truck when pressure inside of the truck caused the hatch cover to slide off and up, striking the employee. The employee sustained a non-displaced pelvis fracture, a right linear temporal fracture and a subdural hematoma.

An employee was helping to install a blind between a pipe flange and a block valve. The flange needed to be separated in order to remove the gaskets and install new gaskets and the blind. The device that was used to maintain space between the flanges flipped, and the employee's left index fingertip was pinched by the device. The employee sustained a partial amputation and required surgery.

A crew was pinning an expanded metal walkway to the side of a shipping container during rigging operations. A forklift was being used to hold the walkway up against the side of the shipping container but needed to be repositioned. While doing so, the walkway fell on top of the injured employee and they sustained right ankle and clavicle fractures.

Two employees were completing a post-job inspection of a centrifuge. One employee rotated the centrifuge rotating assembly to test if it could be turned by hand. The injured employee went to stop the rotating assembly when their left little finger was caught between the belt and pulley system. The employee sustained an open, non-displaced distal phalanx fracture and a fingertip amputation to the left little finger.
An employee was inspecting equipment when his right index fingertip was amputated by the machine.
