An employee and a co-worker were loading a 4-foot-tall piece of high-pressure iron pipe into a line truck. When the employee was setting down the pipe, his right middle finger was caught between the hammer union wing and another piece of high-pressure iron pipe, resulting in a finger amputation.
An employee was working on a well when they were struck by a detached tubing joint, resulting in a left arm fracture.

An employee was stepping off a tank trailer bumper onto a two-step utility step stool when they fell backward and rolled their left ankle. The employee sustained a left fibula fracture that required hospitalization and surgery.
An employee was servicing a gas lifting system when the system released pressure and struck the employee. The employee sustained injuries that required hospitalization.

An employee was inspecting noise from a pumping unit. As he went to push on the belt guard, the employee was pinned between the crank arm and the base of the unit, resulting in a lacerated liver, and bruising to the chest, arms, back, and shoulders.
An employee was moving a mud bucket from a work area to a storage area when the bucket got caught on a drain line and tipped over onto the employee's left leg, resulting in a fractured tibia.
An employee was putting spacers on bore pipes when his left index finger was caught between the spacers and the pipes, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was tightening bolts on a gasket flange. When he descended from a 6-foot A-frame ladder, he fell from the third step from bottom to the ground. The employee sustained a compound fracture to the left ankle and was hospitalized.
An employee was changing a belt when their fingers were caught between the belt and pulley, resulting in the amputation of three right-hand fingertips.
An employee had stopped on the side of the road to secure the open tool box in their truck bed when the wind blew the truck door closed on their hand and partially amputation their left ring finger.

On June 1, 2023, an employee was helping inspect a trackside hose when hot flowback water was released from the hose. It sprayed onto the employee, burning the employee's neck, forearm, sides, and back.

An employee was waiting on a natural gas well to vent after performing maintenance. A cigarette was lit, causing a flash fire. The employee was hospitalized for burns to his face, hands, and the top of his head. The employee also sustained lung damage.

An employee was performing maintenance on a pump. He was assembling a stuffing box onto the fluid end assembly when the box shifted and pinched his right middle finger resulting in a displaced fracture of the distal phalanx and an incomplete amputation.
An employee was assisting with installing meter runs. While adjusting straps on a piece of fabrication, the piece shifted and rolled onto the employee's foot, resulting in fractures.

A mechanic was spotting for a crane that was lowering an engine onto a frame. As the employee cleared the threads of the engine mount, the weight of the engine shifted, amputating his left index fingertip before the first knuckle.

Employees were using a machine to connect two pipes at the joint. One pipe was in the joint while the other pipe was held level by a crane with a synthetic sling. The injured employee's right ring finger was caught between the sling and a pipe component, resulting in amputation.

An employee was moving an 1,100-pound fluid end backing plate using a fork truck. The plate had shifted out of place. When the employee went to reposition the plate on the forks, the plate slipped and caught their left middle finger against the forks, resulting in partial amputation.

While standing on the bumper of a pickup truck, an employee was grabbing a hand tool from a toolbox in the back of the truck. The employee slipped, causing his right thumb to be pinched between the tool and the bumper of the truck. A portion of the thumb was medically amputated.

An employee was preparing to pump chemicals from a tote on a truck bed into a continuous injection tank. While walking on the tote and transitioning to another container, the employee slipped/tripped and fell to the ground sustaining fractures to vertebrae and the left wrist and a head laceration.
An employee was in a hole using tongs to torque an electrical connection when his left little finger got caught between the latch and the head of the tong, resulting in a partial finger amputation.

On June 15, 2023, at 11:30 AM, an employee was moving a belt on a pumping unit when he slipped, causing his right hand to get caught between the belt and sheave. His right wrist was dislocated and required surgery and his left ring finger was amputated at the last joint. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was hospitalized for heat illness.
An employee was refueling a pump when a flash fire occurred and burned the employee's left arm. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was rebuilding a compressor engine on an offshore facility. As they were troubleshooting a connecting rod inside the compressor engine, the rod slipped down. The employee's finger was then caught between the crankshaft and connecting rod, resulting in a left middle fingertip amputation and fracture.

An employee was walking to retrieve a forklift when they fell through a floor opening into a sump pit. The employee sustained chemical burns from their knees to their feet from the ammonium phosphate in the pit.

An employee was preparing a load on a semi-trailer for a delivery to a field location. After putting the straps over the totes, he descended the trailer. While descending, his pant leg was caught on the mud flap frame, which caused him to fall and strike his head on the ground. The employee lost consciousness and sustained a laceration and a fractured skull.

On 6/20/2023, at approximately 12:20 PM, the injured employee was working on a decompletion at a well. A rig crew had set a blow out preventer (BOP) on the wellhead, and the injured employee was torquing the nuts when a spark came out from the side of the torque unit and ignited a flash fire. The employee was engulfed by the fire and sustained first degree burns to their face and second degree burns to both hands.

Employees were cleaning a storage tank for petroleum. Employee 1 was inside the tank and employee 2 was outside the tank approximately 30 to 40 feet away when a flash fire occurred. The force of the fire/explosion threw employee 1 into a wall. Employee 1 sustained fractures to the left collar bone and left ribs, a dislocated right elbow, a lacerated left ear, and burns. Employee 2 sustained second-and-third- degree burns to the face, chest, hands, and fingers.
Employees were moving equipment onto a truck. The truck was backing up when an employee was caught between the trailer and the load, resulting in injuries to the shoulder, ribs, and back.

An employee was working on the floor of a workover rig removing tubulars from the wellbore when they were struck by the power swivel, which pushed them into a handrail. The employee suffered a fractured collarbone.

An employee was operating a hot oil truck and installing a fitting on a string of pipe. Slips were stuck on the wiper plate and the wiper plate sheared off. The pipe then slipped down and crushed the employee's middle and ring fingertips on their left hand.

An employee was spotting for a hydrovac truck that was backing up. They were struck by the hydrovac truck and became caught against another truck. The employee sustained a lacerated spleen and a fractured hip.
An employee sustained toe fractures after a floor plate that was being lifted detached from the chain and fell.
An employee was hooking up a hose when the hose fell and crushed their fingertip.
An employee was using a punch to get out a rolling pin when a piece of metal struck and entered the employee's right eye through a gap in his safety glasses.
An employee was driving a utility task vehicle onsite when the vehicle flipped over and pinned the employee's leg, resulting in a tibia fracture.

An employee was adjusting the operator console to raise it to a higher level. He removed the bracket that connects the console to the rail system so he could begin raising it. The console shifted, causing the employee to fall 10 feet, resulting in a shoulder fracture and head laceration.

An employee was assisting a crew with rigging down when his right index and middle fingers were crushed between the gripper and the top drive resulting in the amputation of the employee's right index finger.
An employee was cutting a casing pipe when a piece of the casing struck him in his left eye, resulting in an injury.
An employee was stepping from the back of a truck onto a 4-foot step ladder. The ladder fell over and the employee fell to the shop floor on his left side. He sustained a broken pelvis.

An employee climbed on a frac stack of valves when an unbalanced load began to shift. As the employee went to stabilize the connection, they lost balance and fell 7 feet to a lower level. The employee sustained a left wrist fracture that required surgery.

An employee was picking up a 5-foot, 950-pound pneumatic cylinder (mud bucket) by the handle to move it. The employee was positioning the bucket for use when their left arm became caught between it and an iron roughneck. The employee was hospitalized with compartment syndrome that required surgery.

An employee was moving a metal pipe with a hydraulic hoist when the winch came down faster than expected. This caused the pipe to fall and as the employee went to catch it, his finger was pinched. The employee's right index finger was partially amputated.
An employee was pressure washing a gas compression unit when they stepped off a 3-foot high skid and fell to the ground, sustaining an ankle fracture.

Employees were lifting the floor of a rig after tying off the floor with a winch line. The floor was lifted so the employees could remove the retaining/lifting chains. The knot came undone, causing the rig floor to fall a short distance and strike the injured employee. The employee was knocked down and rendered unconscious. He suffered a concussion and a compression to his upper spine.

An employee was welding an oil pipe and installing a gauge on the pipe of a drilling rig. As he cut into it with a torch, an explosion occurred. The shockwave of the explosion caused the employee to sustain a concussion and multiple broken bones.
On July 22, 2023, an employee was swinging a 5-ton hammer on a hammer union. The employee then noticed a piece of metal was lodged in his upper left thigh and required hospitalization.
An employee was changing the filter on a dehydration unit when the filter housing struck the employee's right leg, fracturing their tibia and fibula.
Employees were performing wireline operations when the slack on the wireline tightened, causing it to strike and lacerate the injured employee's neck.

During a routine inspection, a steam hose became unsecured and three individuals were burned by steam. The injured employee was hospitalized with burns to their face, torso, arms, and legs. Two other individuals were exposed to steam, but were not hospitalized.

An employee was on a catwalk helping to lay down tubing when he lost his balance. The employee jumped approximately 42 inches to the ground and the 30-foot section of tubing struck his left shin resulting in a fracture that required surgery.
An employee was loading a railcar when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained first- and second-degree burns to the left side of the body.

An employee was greasing a pumping unit. He was standing on the T-block when the weights swung. He moved back but was caught between the weights and the arm of the unit. He tried to catch himself, and his right hand was pulled into the pulley, resulting in amputation of his right little, ring, middle, and index fingers.

An employee was helping to download shaped charges. During the process, a charge exploded directly over the employee's left hand. The employee suffered lacerations and burns to his left hand. He was hospitalized, and his left little finger was surgically amputated.

A crew was tripping stand in a hole. As one stand was stabbed in the stump, the stand swung away. The injured employee's hand was caught between the stand and the cylinder, resulting in a right little fingertip amputation.
An employee was mixing mud when he began to feel dizzy due to dehydration from the heat.
An employee was removing a drill bit when their left index finger was caught between a moving and a stationary part. The part closed and the employee's finger was crushed.
An employee was removing equipment and placing it on the ground when they were bitten by a rattlesnake on the right little finger.

A crew was changing out a 3-by-3 studded block cross on a stand. They had used a forklift, forklift hooks, and straps to lift the stand and block using the jack handle arms as lifting points. While the U-bolt nuts were being tightened, the straps slipped, the stand tilted, and the block slid off the stand and landed on an employee's left leg and arm. The employee suffered a broken left femur, left ulna, and left radius.

An employee was working outdoors and performing various tasks at an oil well location. At the end of his work, the employee went to his hotel room and rested. He was later hospitalized with severe dehydration.
An employee was cleaning a pipe. He went to lift the pipe and his finger was caught and amputated by the pipe.

An employee was opening an oil and gas well. Nitrogen was put into the well to open it and start production. The employee went to the generator to shut it down and an explosion occurred when the cabinet door was opened. The employee sustained burns to over 15% of the body, including the face, neck, arms, and torso that required hospitalization.

Employees were performing well pad completion work. They pumped nitrogen into the well unit to open it up so that it would flow/produce. The employee went to the sand-removing unit/trailer to check if the well was flowing. He was standing on the steps and walkway of the trailer when an explosion occurred that knocked him over the walkway handrail resulting in a 3-4 foot fall. He was hospitalized with a fractured left foot and first-degree burns to his hands. A generator about 37 feet away had caused the ignition.

Employees were at a closed 3-inch loop pipe to test meters. The system had a leak and the injured employee went to fix it. The injured employee was removing a valve when he was struck in the head with approximately 50 psi of air pressure. He was knocked into a chain link fence, sustained a concussion and had a seizure due to the injury. He was hospitalized.

An employee was moving a vacuum pump with a pry bar when the pump slipped off the pry bar. The employee's left middle finger was caught between the vacuum pump foot and frame, resulting in amputation of the fingertip.

An employee was placing an 8-inch beam into a structure that was suspended by a forklift. The beam shifted and slide out of the sling, striking the employee. They sustained fractures to the right lower leg and ribs.

An employee had been waiting for tubing to be lowered. The swage came loose and dropped along with the tubing (approximately 31-feet long). It fell 60 feet to the ground, then tipped over and struck the employee's head. The employee was knocked out and sustained a concussion, a broken nose, and lacerations to the head.
An employee was working on a compressor panel when they lost consciousness due to heat stress, causing the employee to fall to the ground. They sustained five rib fractures and were hospitalized.
An employee was en route to take a break when a rattlesnake fell from an elevated pipe rack and bit the employee's right hand.

An employee was servicing company equipment. The employee was removing a valve cap cover off a first-stage discharge cylinder when trapped pressure released, causing the valve cap to strike the employee's hand and arm. The employee sustained a laceration and partial amputation of the right index finger. They required surgery for fractures to the arm and injury to tendons and ligaments.
An employee was operating a preform press when his hand was caught in the machine, resulting in a left index finger amputation.

An employee was working on a pump. As they hammered the hardline, the chiksan swivel connection blew apart, striking the injured employee. They sustained lacerations, a fracture, and head injury that caused loss of consciousness and required hospitalization.
An employee was working to move drilling equipment onto a truck for demobilization. The equipment began to tip and the employee jumped from the cab of the excavator, resulting in a tibia fracture.

An employee was working on a drilling rig as tongs were being hoisted. The lifting chain failed and the tongs fell on the employee and pinned him against the drilling rig floor. The employee sustained injuries to internal organs and their legs that required hospitalization.

An employee was fixing/cleaning up a pipe that had been welded using a handheld angle grinder. A piece of the grinding wheel broke and struck the employee's arm. The grinder then became caught and kicked back up toward the employee's face, resulting in a facial laceration and fractures to the teeth, nose, and face.

An employee was preparing a bushel corn bin for filling and was ensuring that residual product was removed from all gates. One gate had remaining product in it and as the employee lifted the modification tab, the slide gate began closing. The modification tab contacted the outer edge of the slide gate enclosure, amputating their right index fingertip.
An employee was loosening a bullhead when their wrench slipped. The employee fell from his position to the ground, sustaining a lower left leg fracture.
An employee was installing production tubing when it fell from the lifting sub. The employee sustained fractures to the clavicle and right cheek.

An employee was hand tightening bolts at the manway of a vertical tank at an oil and gas site. The employee hooked up the plumbing and hatch to the tank. They had begun to install a rubber seal around the hatch when a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained a burn to the face and third degree burns to the left arm requiring hospitalization.
An employee's hand was caught between two flanges, resulting in finger fractures.

An employee was removing a thread protector off the end of an alloy when the alloy shifted and pinched their finger between it and the catwalk. The employee sustained an open fracture of the left index finger and a fingertip amputation.

At a remote location, the injured employee was running a pig through the pipeline when the pig became stuck. As the employee was venting gas to the atmosphere to free the pig, a spark ignited the gas vapors, causing the employee to sustain second-degree burns to their face and left elbow.

An employee was checking fluid levels on a mast/power pack unit. The employee was on a ladder trying to access a catwalk when they slipped on a wet rung and fell 5 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured hip.

An employee was removing the bolts from a ram door during a ram changeover. The employee loosened the bolts and then utilized a speed wrench to unscrew them from the blowout preventer (BOP). The employee then instructed the operator to open the rams. The employee noticed one of the bolts was catching on a thread and went to unscrew it the rest of the way. Their gloved left index finger was caught between the head of the bolt and the ram door that was opening resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was pre-rigging a well pad and torquing down the monoline. His hands were placed on the head of the hydraulic torque wrench while moving it to a different bolt. At the same time, the employee's foot slipped and the torque wrench activated. His left little finger went between the nut and head, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was tying a hose. A truck backed up, pinching the employee's leg between the hose and hammer union, resulting in a right fibula fracture.

An employee was removing bolts from a pipe flange in order to remove an isolation blind. The employee was pulling the blind from the piping system when hydrogen gas released and flashed, resulting in burns to their face and left wrist.

An employee was running pipe into a hole on a rig floor. He was still running the other joint into the hole when the laydown machine shot the joint of pipe. The pipe hit the employee in the jaw and he fell backward, suffering a fractured cheekbone.
An employee was performing well maintenance activities when equipment failed and a rope socket struck the employee's face and chest. They suffered facial injuries.

Two employees were performing maintenance on a horse power unit. The plunger was pushed back in and an employee's left index and middle fingers were caught between the fluid-end plunger and power-end plunger, resulting in a laceration and amputation.
An employee was using a torque pump to tighten a frac valve when a spark ignited flammable gas and caused a flash fire. The employee sustained burns to their neck and arms.

An employee was working in an area where another company was also working. The other company's employees were using an electric hydraulic pump to remove the bolts of the frac valve. The wiring of the torque wrench and pump unit were then charred and a flash fire occurred. The employee sustained second-degree burns to their face and neck.
An employee was walking between a rig and generator when he stepped on the line backer (a device to protect cables and hose from damage) during wet conditions and was shocked.

An employee was climbing the derrick girt to perform work on a cover. As they went to tie off the top drive, the driller came down with the top drive pulling the employee off the girt and onto the top drive. The employee sustained fractures to the pelvis and tailbone.

An employee was moving an 8-9 inch service packer tool from a tool vise into a tool hoist for relocation. The tool shifted in the sling of the hoist and the employee's thumb was struck by the tool, amputating the tip. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was rolling up a power cord inside the tank of a vessel when they stepped backward into a manhole behind them. The employee fell through the hole inside the tank of the vessel and sustained fractures to the shoulder as well as swelling of the left side of the back.
An employee was removing a dock hose when their fingers were caught between the hose flange and the top rail of the dock, resulting in a partial finger amputation.
An employee slipped and fell on the ground while storing hoses that had been used in a tanker truck delivery. The employee sustained a fractured hip.

After running a survey and putting air back on the hole, two employees were standing in the doorway of the doghouse watching the flow line to see if there was a gas flare. The pilot light for the flow line was not ignited. The injured employee used a propane torch to igniting the pilot light. A flash fire resulted due to down-hole gas that had come out of the flow line. The injured employee sustained second degree burns to their face, forearms, and hands.

An employee was rigging and loading tools and equipment onto a trailer when they were shocked. The employee's sustained third-degree burns in the right hand and possible amputation of fingers. Electricity exited through the employee's left foot resulting in the amputation of the fourth toe and the partial amputation of the little toe. The employee then fell and suffered a skull fracture.
An employee was servicing a track tongue scissor assembly that was hoisted. The equipment fell from the hoisting mechanism and onto their left little finger, resulting in an amputation.
An employee was near a hybrid separator when it malfunctioned, resulting in a flash fire that burned the employee's upper body.

An employee was loading grain into a rail car when they fell from the top of a rail car. They landed 15 feet below, on concrete between two rail cars. The employee sustained fractures to their jaw, spine, and knee.

An employee was securing ladders on a gang truck. He lost his footing and fell from the back of the truck bed, striking his abdomen on the edge of the bed or the trailer hitch. The employee sustained five broken ribs and a punctured lung requiring hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was removing tubing caps and cleaning tubing ends with solvent. Their flame-resistant pants became soaked with the cleaning solvent and were ignited by a propane torch used for removing tubing caps. The employee was hospitalized with burns to their legs.

An employee removed the spark plugs and was rotating an engine to evacuate condensate from the cylinders. An unknown source ignited the condensate and natural gas. The employee sustained burns to the back of his hands and upper leg area.
An employee was moving a crosshead assembly. The joint on the assembly caught his left middle finger, amputating the tip.
An employee was assisting with moving a 12-inch PVC pipe. The pipe shifted, pinching the employee's left index finger against a support post. The employee's finger was fractured.

An employee was preparing a pump for maintenance. When the employee removed a cover, chemicals were released into the air. The employee was exposed to hydrogen sulfide and methyl mercaptan and was hospitalized.

An employee was moving a light tower so it could be hitched to a truck. He grabbed the tongue of the trailer hitch on the light tower to slide it to the left. The tongue jack fell off, causing the light tower tongue to drop on the employee's right hand. The employee's middle fingertip was amputated.

An employee was cleaning a sight glass on a gas separation machine that was located on top of a self contained/self evacuating tank. When the valve that connected the well bore to the gas separation machine was opened, gas/vapor ignited, causing a flash fire that burned the employee's face and hands.

An employee was performing oversight for the welding of a pipeline launcher door on a construction project. Two welders were performing arc welding, one on the interior diameter of the pipeline launcher door, and the other on the outside diameter of the launcher door when a flash fire occurred. The injured employee sustained first- and second-degree burns to the face, neck, back, and hands.

An employee was applying grease to the cables of a machine during maintenance. He was caught by the 1-inch cable and pulled into the cable spool. The employee sustained partial amputations to three fingers on his right hand.
An employee was on the ground level during pipe scanning operations assisting the rig crew to stand a 64-foot pipe. The pipe slid onto his left foot, resulting in the amputation of two toes.

The injured employee was spray painting lay flat shipping reels while another employee was picking up the reels with a telehandler after they were painted. The telehandler bumped a reel, causing other reels to fall. The injured employee was caught between the reels, resulting in broken left femur.
An employee was lowering a string with a valve attached onto a shaker table when their hand was caught between the guardrail and valve. The employee's right thumb was crushed and required surgery.
An employee was spinning rod tongs when his hand slipped and was caught in the tongs, resulting in a little finger amputation.
An employee was retrieving cable that had been laid on top of pipe racks. The employee's leg was pinned between two pipe racks. The employee suffered a contusion to the leg and was hospitalized.

An employee was standing by the front side of the mud mix pump guard. He squatted down and stretched out to reach the belt with his left hand and was able to grab it. When he began to rise, belt in hand, his hand got caught on the backside of the guard. The belt and pulley pulled the used belt that was in his hand into the pulley, causing amputations to the middle, ring, and little fingertips.
An employee was greasing tongs on a work-over rig. The tongs lacerated one of the employee's fingers.

An employee was diagnosing an alarm on a compressor skid. They were changing out a liquid level switch on the natural gas compressor system when there was a flash fire/explosion. The employee sustained burns to their face and ear, and severe burns to both hands. The employee was hospitalized.

The injured employee was standing near the end of a pipe rack installing a pin in the pipe stop. Another employee was utilizing a forklift nearby to move another set of pipe racks. As the forklift moved, it drove over a bump and bounced; the brakes were then applied and one side of the pipe rack fell off the forks and landed on the injured employee s right boot, pinning his boot against the ground and resulting in multiple fractures and lacerations to his right foot.
An employee was assisting with pipe on a drilling rig. The slips came down and landed on the employee's left foot fracturing four metatarsals.

An employee was retrieving a lost drill pipe with a lifting bail when their left thumb got pinched between the table and handle of the lifting bail while trying to re-thread the pipe to lift it out. The employee suffered an amputation to the left thumb.

An employee was installing a compressor piston. He tripped and fell backward while the piston was in his lap. As he landed, the little finger of his left hand became caught between the piston and compressor piping resulting in a partial amputation of the fingertip. The employee required stitches and the fingertip was reattached.

An employee was standing on the rig floor next to a polishing unit. His hand was placed on the polishing unit when the pump was lowered, resulting in amputation of their right thumb, ring, and middle fingertips.
An employee reached to push a control button to close an overhead door when their little finger was caught between the door and the track. The employee's right little fingertip was amputated.
An employee was moving a pump case around on jack stands when the load shifted and contacted the employee's right thumb causing a crush injury. The thumb tip was amputated.
An employee was closing an office door when their middle fingertip was caught between the door and the frame, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

Employees were flushing a chemical line at a job site. As an employee was unplugging a hose connection, residual pressure caused caustic liquids to spray under his face shield, resulting in chemical burns to the face and neck that required hospitalization.
An employee was standing on top of a pump truck when he slipped and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a skull fracture.
An employee was parking his company vehicle. As he stepped out of the truck, the employee stepped on a patch of ice, slipped, and fell to the ground. The employee suffered a lower right leg fracture.
An employee's left ring finger was caught between two pipes (one stationary and the other being rolled). The employee suffered a partial finger amputation.

An employee missed her chair while sitting down. She fell backward into a display case and landed on the floor. Items on top of the case then fell and struck the employee's head, causing injury to the left side of their head.

An employee was repairing an artificial lift. The employee opened a valve on the lift that caused a rapid release of energy, and the employee was struck by an object. The employee suffered fractures to the skull, right orbital socket, and right cheek. The employee was hospitalized.

On January 6, 2024, an employee was making a swivel connection involving a winch line. As the joint was being tightened, the threads became sticky. The employee was shaking the winch line to loosen it when the bridle caught on the line and wrapped around his finger. His middle finger was amputated past the fingernail and before the first knuckle.

An employee pulled a stand of drill pipe back and had just finished pushing it back into a "finger" before securing it with rope. The driller was coming down with top drives and blocks. A gust of wind blew the employee's secondary retention into the Kelly hose clamp. As a result, the top drive pulled the cable and the employee down into the steel frame of the derrick board. The employee's left hip and right femur were fractured.
An employee was attempting a lift with a crane and caught their left index finger between two shells (36-inch diameter cylinder vessels), resulting in amputation.

An employee took a CRT tube that was being rigged down. He got on the catwalk that takes him to the rig to put on the lift cap when the tube slipped and struck his foot. He was hospitalized and his right big toe was amputated.

An employee was using a hydraulic-pressured torque wrench to torque a bonnet connection on a valve when the elbow section of the torque head released pressure, resulting in a pressure cut/injection into the employee's left palm.

An employee was moving a mudboat to a new drilling location. He lost his footing and fell back into a pre-existing cellar that was approximately 8 feet deep. He was hospitalized with fractures to his hip and left arm.

An employee was inspecting trays inside an amine tower vessel to determine what needed to be replaced. The employee climbed down through the 20 percolator trays, going through 18" x 22" openings in the trays, until he reached the third or fourth tray from the bottom. The employee then slipped and fell approximately 20 feet to a metal surface below. The employee sustained injuries to their back, left elbow, and ankles and was hospitalized.

An employee was using a hydraulic bolt torquing machine on a ladder when the machine struck the employee's little finger and palm. The employee suffered a laceration and crush injury to the right hand that required hospitalization.
An employee was unwiring the secondary side of a de-energized transformer and draining oil for repairs when a wire came loose and shocked the employee. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was preparing to load a curtain-side trailer with pallets of carbon. While the support beam was being removed, it came loose from the trailer and closed on the employee's middle fingertip. He suffered a partial amputation to the finger.

An employee was working to set a drive pin on an S-hook so a forklift could pick up a part and bring it to the paint department. The employee's left middle finger was pinched between the pin and the S-hook resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee was preheating oil to place in the casing of an oil well flow line. A propane line shot under the truck and into the burner box, causing the burners to ignite and start a flash fire. The employee suffered burns to their face, neck, and wrist.
An employee was walking across a shop. His left foot caught on a pallet in the center of the shop, and he fell to the floor. He suffered a broken hip.
An employee was using a pressure washer when it lacerated his foot. He was hospitalized, requiring surgery.

A rig crew had installed the rotating rubber onto the last joint of pipe in a mouse hole. The crew picked up the joint out of the mouse hole to attach it to the stump to make up the last joint. As the joint was placed inside the stump, the rotating rubber (wet from the weather) slid down the casing and struck an employee's right index finger. The finger was amputated.

An employee was working from a scaffold over a blowout preventer, using a 5-foot bar to position an orbit valve. An air winch on the rig floor was being used to lift the valve and hold it in place. The air winch line went taut suddenly and struck the 5-foot bar, pushing it toward the substructure of the drilling rig. When the bar struck the substructure, the employee's left ring fingertip was caught between them. The fingertip was amputated.
An employee was holding a back-pressure regulator. A pipe came apart (under tension from a forklift) and injured the employee's left hand, lacerating and fracturing the index finger.
An employee was using a 7-inch grinder with a 6-inch cutting stone disc to put a bevel on a tube sheet. The cutting stone broke apart and contacted the employee, resulting in a fractured right tibia.

The injured employee was performing pre-job spotting and was staging equipment. The employee moved in to connect a bulldozer. The operator of the bulldozer saw that a bulk truck was moving backward, so he moved the bulldozer forward. The injured employee was crushed between the bulldozer's right ripper and the rear of the bulk trailer. He sustained a pelvic fracture on his left side and an open fracture to his upper right leg.
An employee was operating a winch when his left hand got caught under a cable, resulting in an amputation of the ring fingertip.

An employee was in a rod basket while moving rods from a well bore. He had his hand on a cable above the rotating rod when his glove or sleeve got caught in the rotating rod stand, resulting in a broken arm.
An employee was climbing up a fixed structural ladder when he lost his grip and fell approximately 6 feet to the ground, resulting in a fractured left hip.

An employee was trying to restart an engine on a compressor that went down. The engine flywheel and starter were not aligned. The employee attempted to use a bar to roll over the flywheel when built-up air pressure caused the entire engine to roll over. The bar then slammed into the employee's left arm, resulting in an injury.

An employee was rigging down a workover rig for relocation. The derrick had been retracted and the top section was down. The employee was on the rig floor ensuring the lines were not becoming tangled or caught on anything. While coiling up the slack of two guidelines, the swab line tightened unexpectedly while being winched in, and caught the employee's right leg. The leg was amputated below the base of the hip.

An employee was working in the rod basket on a well service rig when their left ring finger was caught in a pinch point between the rod basket swivel frame and a support on the rig. The finger was amputated.
An employee was lowering elevators while trying to couple a joint of tubing coming from a well. The employee's right hand was caught in a pinch point resulting in amputation of the ring fingertip.
An employee fell while exiting a tractor, landed on the ground, and suffered fractures to the pelvis and shoulder blade. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was running casing/putting pipe in the hole when their hand was caught in a rotating part, resulting in a left forearm fracture.

Employees were installing a manual start switch on a 480-volt variable speed drive motor controller on a saltwater disposal (SWD) well control panel when an arc flash occurred. Two employee sustained burns and were hospitalized.

An employee was conducting maintenance on a pipe and was using a T-bar tool to secure the retainer cap on a pump. The employee's left index finger was caught in the rotating pump, resulting in a partial amputation.

An employee was on a barge hooking up and unhooking loads on a boom crane. While under the boom crane, the employee was struck in the side of the head and the body by a free-falling headache ball and fast line. The employee suffered fractures and internal bleeding and was hospitalized.

An employee was trying to lift and hold a piece of 20" HDPE piping that was inserted into a fusion machine. The machine started and the employee's left index finger was caught between the roller and pipe causing a fingertip amputation.

An employee was trying to lower the level on a condensate boiler by opening a pump case drain line. The plugged condensate line shifted unexpectedly and pinched the employee's left hand against a stanchion. The employee suffered burns to the hand.

An employee was inserting drill pipe slips into the rotary table by kicking the slips while tripping drill pipe out of the hole when his foot was caught between the slips and the drill pipe, fracturing three toes and lacerating his right foot.

An employee was standing approximately 10 feet off to the side of a hydraulic power unit. When the hydraulic power unit was started, a metal valve inside a hose connector detached from the end of a hydraulic line and struck the employee, puncturing his abdomen.

An employee strapped an 8-inch mud motor on a pipe rack, then went to trace the high side of the mud motor from the adjustable kick off (AKO) to the upper connection of the motor. To better position the motor on the pipe rack, the employee went to roll the motor over. They inserted a rock between the motor and the pipe rack as a chock to prevent it from rolling. The motor rolled back crushing the employee's left thumb and resulting in amputation of the tip.

An employee was pulling drill line from the drill spool while the top drive was not set on the docking pins. The deadman was unexpectedly released which caused the top drive to fall to the drill floor from a height of 30 feet. This caused the drill line that was being pulled out and laid on the ground to retract and strike an employee. The employee suffered fractures to his legs and neck.

A crew of employees was using a hoist to lift a drillable sub on the rig floor. Single-joint elevators were placed on the sub before lifting. As the crew started to lift the sub, the sub struck the derrick leg, causing the single-joint elevators to open and the sub to drop approximately 1 1/2 feet, striking the injured employee in the right leg below the knee. The employee suffered two leg fractures.
An employee was removing a pipe from his truck when his middle finger got caught in the D ring on the pipe, resulting in a fingertip amputation up to the first knuckle.
Two employees were making repairs on a boat. A gust of wind shut the engine room door on one employee's head, opening a wound across the top of the scalp. He was hospitalized.
Two employees were raising the media/debris tank to dump it. The tank contacted an overhead power line and both employees were shocked.
An employee was taking measurements for electrical conduit while standing on an earthen berm when he lost his balance and fell, landing on his leg and fracturing his left leg and ankle.

An employee was working behind a piece of heavy machinery, lying on a cattleguard and putting bolts on the machinery. The machinery's tire backed up onto his right hip and dislocated it. He was hospitalized.
An employee was working on a mud pump when a hammer struck his mouth. He suffered a possible broken jaw and some broken teeth.
An employee was verifying belt tension while repairing a unit in the shop when their hand contacted the boost pump, resulting in a partial amputation to their left index and middle fingers.
An employee was sprayed with hot water when a nearby bleeder valve was under pressure that caused the valve to release. This resulted in burns to their legs and lower torso.
An employee was freeing a calf that had become entangled in a barbed wire fence when his finger became caught between the fence and the calf, resulting in an amputation to his left right fingertip.

A crew of two was attempting to blind/isolate the loop to the re-slurry control valve to the north rise. As the employees were loosening the bolts to open the pipe and placing the blind, a valve that was holding back the slurry opened. This released the hot slurry (640 degrees Fahrenheit) onto the employees performing the work. Both employees sustained thermal burns from the slurry and were hospitalized.

An employee was hoisting a piece of equipment and pushing a stabilizer pipe out a gate/door. The pipe was lowered. This caused the hoist to lose tension, and the pipe pinned the employee against other, stationary pipes. The employee sustained a broken jaw.
A culvert was being lifted when a pipe struck an employee in the face. The employee suffered a jaw laceration and was hospitalized.
An employee was using power tongs to trip a pipe while servicing a well when their left little finger got caught in the power tongs, resulting in an amputation between the nail and the first knuckle.

Employees were performing an integrity test of a section of pipe at an oil well. They were bleeding pressure off to a 2-inch line and the valve was already opened. As the inline pipe approached the line to open the valve further, the line parted and separated from the cross section. The cross section was threaded pipe that burst at the threads. The broken piping struck an employee, pushing him 33 feet away and causing fractures to his humerus and tibia.
An employee was breaking down a drill rig when the tower came down and struck them in the right thigh. They sustained a fractures to their L3 and L4 vertebrae and were hospitalized.

Employee 1 was operating the beveller and noticed that the machine was not working. They stopped the machine and entered the machine to address the issue. Employee 2, working on another machine, also noticed that the beveller was not working and went to assist. Employee 1 finished up, exited, and activated the machine. Employee 2, who remained in the machine, was pinned between a beveller and pipe at his upper legs/thighs, resulting in a severe laceration to the upper left thigh and internal bleeding to the left leg.
An employee was loading spare tires into the doghouse. There was a rattlesnake under one of the tires and it bit his left index finger. The employee was hospitalized.
An employee was setting an aluminum gangway on a ship when the gangway moved toward him, pinning him between the gangway and a bollard on the dock. He sustained a fractured pelvis.

An employee was removing a pin that was holding together a bucket and a hydraulic cylinder on a skid steer by using a hammer and a hole punch. When the pin was pushed out, the bucket shifted causing the hole punch to move and pinch their left ring finger. They sustained an amputation to the fingertip.

On May 2, 2024, an employee was holding a hose while pumping cement into a 25" pipe when a heavy steel plate that was attached to the pipe rolled onto his right foot. The employee sustained two broken bones on the top of his foot.
An employee was cleaning dead weeds and vegetation around pumping equipment so he could clean a screen/filter when he was bitten by a rattlesnake on his right hand.
An employee was walking down stairs when she tripped and fell, injuring her left leg and ankle.

An employee was performing abrasive blasting on two six-inch pipes. While rolling the pipe in the kneeling position, the blast nozzle engaged. They sustained an abrasion of the right inner thigh from the abrasive blasting media contacting them at 95 PSI.
An employee was unloading a fiberglass hut from a semi-truck and bracing it from the wind when a telehandler rolled over his leg, resulting in lower leg fractures requiring surgery.
An employee was exiting a pick-up truck bed when he fell backward off the rear bumper to the ground, resulting in a subdural hematoma.

An employee was burned on the hands, left elbow, face, neck, back, and knee during a flash fire in the gas processing unit (GPU) while it was being brought back online after equipment had been installed.
While unloading a debris container using a vacuum truck, a piece of solid debris tumbled out of the truck and struck the employee's left leg. He was hospitalized for surgery.

An employee was signaling a forklift operator as a 20-foot-long, 4-inch-thick section of steel pipe was lowered. The pipe came loose and fell striking the employee's head and shoulder. The employee sustained a head laceration and fractured ribs.

An employee was standing by while 110-inch oil and gas pipes were being loaded onto a gooseneck trailer. Some pipes fell from the trailer and one of them landed on the employee's left ankle, crushing it.

An employee was using a sledgehammer to loosen a hammer union. The employee's sledgehammer missed the hammer union causing him to lose his balance and fall on the ground. The employee sustained a fractured wrist.
An employee was power washing a tank when the high-pressure fluid from the pressure washer lacerated their abdomen.

An employee was connecting pipe when they missed stabbing the pipe into the stump and the drill kept moving downward. The pipe casing then bowed and struck him in the face. The employee sustained a fracture.

An employee was dewatering water base mud from inside the dewatering unit. They were standing at the transfer tank monitoring the discharged fluid from the centrifuge to make sure it was free of solids. The employee rotated the 6" pipe and 90-degree elbow so that the fluid would dump into the other side of the transfer tank and reached with his right hand to pull on the handle attached to the elbow. When the employee pulled on the handle to rotate the elbow, the elbow fell off and landed on his left hand which was resting on the divider wall below. The employee suffered blunt force trauma to the left hand that caused a laceration to the ring fingertip requiring stitches and an amputation to the middle fingertip.
An employee was moving a pipe when their right index finger was caught between a pipe and a well, resulting in a fingertip amputation.
An employee was standing next to a trailer when an iron stock pipe rolled off the trailer and landed on his right foot, fracturing toes.

A crew was pulling pipe out of the hole and laying pipe/joint one at a time. The injured employee was laying down a drill collar after removing it when the collar swung and pinched their left little finger against a stationary part. The finger was amputated at the first joint.
An employee was helping to prop up an engine head on a work table when it slipped out of his grip and landed on his left middle finger. The employee sustained a crush injury to the finger.

An employee was troubleshooting a valve that is involved with blending a dry chemical powder mix. The employee's left hand was caught in the valve when it was manually actuated. The employee sustained injury to their hand and fingers.

An employee had just finished unloading water from the vacuum truck into the tank and was preparing to leave. He was disconnecting a hose when pressure in the line caused the hose to fling him to the side. He fell and sustained a broken hip.
An employee was walking across the drilling pad and was struck and run over by a telehandler forklift. The employee's leg was crushed and broken.
An employee was attempting to screw a valve onto a pump when their hand slipped and was caught between the valve and the tool trap, resulting in amputation of their left ring finger.
The employee had been working that day on natural gas compression equipment in the field. As the employee was driving home, he experienced heat illness symptoms and was hospitalized.

An employee was working near the compressor when it over-pressurized and dislodged a case component that struck the employee's lower left leg. The employee sustained a laceration and fracture of the lower leg requiring hospitalization and surgery.

An employee was installing a safety cable on a flowline during a drilling operation. A forklift operator manipulated the boom to allow some slack in the strap to set the flowline box in the flowline trough. The employee had his hands on the strap to manipulate the box and set it down in the flowline trough. His left foot was forward while attempting to gain leverage when the flowline box shifted and struck his left foot and ankle area, resulting in a laceration to the top of his foot requiring hospitalization.

A rig was running in a hole with 2-3/8 drill string. The crew was utilizing the swivel to make up connections, and had modified the grabbing arm on the laydown machine utilizing dies on the grabbing arm. The drill string was not large enough for the grabbing arm to bite down on. The crew then used a third die so that the grabbing arm would bite down. The injured employee saw the third die slipping out of place and went to adjust it. His finger was caught between the pipe in the trough and the die on the grabbing arm resulting in amputation.

An employee was working from an aerial lift to remove test equipment from an elevated stack. The aerial lift basket got stuck on something and the basket flipped, causing the employee to fall 25 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a fractured sternum, a left ankle injury, and injuries to both knees. The employee was wearing a fall harness and was connected, but slipped out of the harness.
An employee was using a hydro-excavation truck on a cattle guard when the boom touched a 7,200-volt power line. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was lifting a spool of lay-flat pipe from the ground with a skid steer. The piston on the deployer that locks in place to keep the spool from sliding out of the deployer failed. The spool fell to the ground and fell over. The employee turned to get out of the way when he lost his balance and the spool fell on his hip and legs. The employee's tibia was fractured in two places.

An employee was working on a rig floor while connected to a hoist line that was leaning against a derrick held up by a tugger. The tugger fell and a 5-foot sub pipe struck the employee's head, knocking him over. He stood up quickly and his head struck a catwalk trough. The employee was hospitalized with a concussion and a laceration behind their ear with an indented fracture.
An employee was monitoring a shaker during an outdoor shift when they suffered dehydration due to heat exposure, resulting in kidney failure and hospitalization.
An employee was removing a pressurized choker valve at a wellsite when it separated and struck their head, resulting in a fractured jaw, fractured nose canal, and broken teeth.
An employee was positioning a single joint on a pipe rack and became caught between the corner of the pipe rack and the spooling trailer, resulting in fractures to the hip and pelvis.

An employee was transferring a fuel cell onto the back of a crew truck using a truck boom crane while standing in the truck bed. The employee lost his footing and fell backward from the rear of the truck bed, resulting in a fracture to his left wrist, contusions on the left side of his hip and head, and a laceration to his left eyebrow.

An employee was working to replace an air line. The line needed to be trimmed to fit and the employee was using a utility knife to cut the hose. The knife cut through the hose and the employee's glove, amputating their left index fingertip.
An employee was performing a voltage test on an electrical panel (4,160 volts) when an arc flash occurred and they sustained burns to their face and torso.
An employee was repairing a pipeline when the natural gas ignited. The employee was hospitalized for bilateral arm burns and a burn to the neck.

On June 27, 2024, two employees were doing a lineup of a vessel (metal drum) to be filled through a fixed pipe with heated water. The lid of the vessel became unseated and a burping action occurred, spraying hot water onto an employee. The employee was hospitalized with burns to their back, left arm, left leg, and right hip.
An employee was using a safety can to fuel a 4" trash pump with gasoline. The fuel ignited and the employee sustained burns to their arms and hands.
An employee was walking out of the mud lab when he slipped and landed on the ground. The employee's left shin was fractured.
An employee was using a hydraulic torque wrench to remove bolts when their right index finger was caught between the torque wrench and bolt. The employee's right index fingertip was amputated.
An employee was walking down the stairs of an oil and gas rig. They tripped and fell from the last step, landing on the ground. The employee's tibia and ankle were fractured.

An employee was troubleshooting a hydraulic hose he had just replaced on a railroad tugger to make sure it wasn't leaking when the base of his right index and middle fingers were exposed to high pressure hydraulic fluid from the leak. The pressurized fluid punctured his skin and he sustained inflammation from his hand up into his upper arm. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery.
An employee was removing a collar from a compressor when they fell approximately 5 feet and landed on an I-beam. The employee sustained fractured ribs and a collapsed lung.
On July 1, 2024, an employee was assisting in water well drilling operations when he began feeling ill. The employee was hospitalized with heat-related dehydration.

An employee was assisting with the rig down of tubing testing equipment when the end of one of the tool joints with a winch line broke. A small section swung back toward the rig floor and hit the employee in the upper back, causing a contusion on the spine. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was running casing when they pulled the hydraulic power tongs using the handle and the handle crushed their right middle finger against the drill pipe. The employee sustained an amputation to the fingertip and nail.

An employee was completing a well intervention. The system encountered a gas pocket while circulating the well. The gas pocket was pumped from the well bore to the open top tank that was being used to circulate the well. An ignition occurred, resulting in a flash fire that caused first-degree burns to the employee's arms.

An employee was using an electric torque wrench on the well when it sparked and ignited pressurized gas that was leaking from the well. This caused an explosion/flash fire that burned a nearby supervising employee's hands, arms, and face.
An employee walked behind a moving forklift. The forklift struck him and knocked him to the ground, resulting in a broken ankle.

An employee was removing tubulars from a mousehole but the slips did not release from the tubular until it was raised. When the slips released, they slid down the tubular and struck the employee in the head. The employee sustained a back injury, a head laceration, and a fractured rib.

A crew was dismantling a rig. They were closing the split spider after removing it from the casing when the injured employee's left hand was caught between the split spider and the rig's master bushing, which was also on the rig's floor. The employee suffered a laceration to the middle finger and fractures to the middle and ring fingers.

Two employees were carrying a drill bit and installation tool to the center of a drilling rig floor. One of them slipped and fell, and the drill bit and installation tool landed on his left hand. He suffered an open fracture and partial amputation of the last joint of the little finger, as well as a laceration to the ring finger.
An employee was rigging down a derrick. The board he was standing on shifted, causing him to lose his balance and fall to the ground about 8 feet below. He suffered a broken left ankle.
An employee was rigging pumps on an oil rig. After he had finished his task, he began to feel dizzy. The employee was hospitalized due to heat-related illness.
An employee was putting 75-foot long pipes in a rack. A joint pipe struck both of the employee's hands, breaking the right radius and ulna and lacerating the left middle finger.

The injured employee was working on the drill floor assisting to repair the oil well. The employee was using hydraulic-operated tongs when a piece inside the tongs came loose. The employee was fixing it when the lever that powers the tool was hit and the hydraulic tongs crushed his left ring finger, resulting in an amputation above the second joint.

An employee was working on a workover rig landing a joint for well servicing. The landing joint was resting on the trough when the weight of the joint made it's sleeve retract and it pinched the employee's left little fingertip resulting in amputation.

An employee was unlatching a sand container from a trailer so a forklift operator could then remove the container. While the employee was unlatching the container, the forklift operator pulled toward the container to remove it. The employee was struck in the abdominal area by a fork on the forklift, resulting in an abdominal injury.

An employee was trying to take out the cylinder of a power tong. Once the cylinder came out of its shackle, it fell and crushed the employee's right little finger below the nail. The employee suffered a fingertip amputation.
An employee was climbing a fixed ladder on a delivery truck when they missed a step and fell approximately 4 feet to the ground. The employee sustained a broken left hip.
An employee was cutting fabric with a knife when the knife stabbed the employee's leg.

An employee was releasing a counterweight from a pump jack. The counterweight rotated and struck the employee in the back, resulting in fractures to their left femur, left sacrum, and L1 and L2 vertebrae.

An employee was conducting torquing operations to connect the oil and gas well head to the blowout preventer (BOP) in the well cellar area. A flash fire occurred and engulfed the employee, resulting in burns to 30% of their body.
An employee had been performing work on a well that included pulling a pipe out of a hole in 106-degree weather. The employee was later hospitalized for heat-related illness.

An employee was opening a hatch on the top portion of a tanker truck. They tripped and fell approximately 8 feet to the ground, sustaining fractures to multiple ribs and their right wrist, as well as a punctured lung.

An employee was performing an audit and adjustment on the capping machine. They were removing cappers from the machine that had fallen out. The employee's right thumb was caught by the belt and pulley resulting in amputation of the thumb tip.

An employee had just finished blasting several parts in the blast booth. He began to use compressed air to blow the steel shot media off two drive rings (brake housings weighing 1,114 pounds) that were on separate pallets 45 inches apart. He heard a cracking sound and turned as the drive ring behind him fell over, hit the small of his back, and landed on his left leg and foot. The employee sustained fractures to their tibia, fibula, ankle, and foot.

An employee was closing transfer wheels and noticed that the rod was not transferring. He was troubleshooting the problem with the transfer wheels from the rear of the transfer trailer when his left hand was pinched. The employee sustained lacerations to four fingers.

An employee was plugging an air compressor into an outlet in a shed when it emitted a spark that ignited gas that had accumulated in the shed. The shed housed oil and gas equipment that may have leaked gas and a propane storage tank and fuel line that may have leaked. This resulted in a fire and explosion that caused burns to the employee's face, hands, and torso.

An employee was installing a gasket between flanges on a heat exchanger. The straight wedge that was used to separate the flanges became stuck between the flanges. The employee used a banana wedge to spread the flanges and remove the stuck straight wedge. When the employee struck the banana wedge with a hammer, the banana wedge dislodged from the flange and struck their face. The employee was hospitalized with a fractured jaw and required surgery.

An employee was unloading a manifold from an iron truck when the manifold shifted and their little finger became caught between the manifold and a storage bracket, resulting in an amputation to the fingertip.
An employee fell while getting onto a forklift. The front bucket of a backhoe that was passing by caught his right leg as he fell, breaking his femur.

An employee was loosening a valve on a frac tank when the wrench slipped, causing the employee to lose their balance and fall on the injured employee on the same level. The employee sustained a fractured left leg.

An employee was replacing the well house. After installing the new well house, the employee drilled a 2- to 3-inch hole in the side of the well house to run a 2-inch pipe. The employee inserted the pipe into the hole and secured it inside the well house. The employee then traveled outside the well house to apply tape onto the threaded section of the new pipe. The employee used his left index finger to hold the tape on the threads. The pipe section inside the well house fell from its support and the employee's finger was lacerated, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

An employee was setting time to the gear. The employee was manually rotating the upper gear when his left ring and little fingers were crushed between the upper and lower gears, resulting in distal amputations.
An employee climbed the staircase to check the levels inside an above ground storage tank (AST). A cigarette ignited flammable gasses and the employee suffered burns to the face and body.

An employee was pulling back a stand of heavy-weight drill pipe so it could be racked in the derrick. While the driller was slacking off with the top-drive, the injured employee unlatched the drill pipe elevators and pulled the pipe toward himself. The pipe came at him faster than expected and as he tried to get out of the way, the pipe hit his left ankle/leg and fractured the left tibia.

An employee connected a pipe elevator to a drill string. The pipe elevator unlatched while the string was being lifted. The elevator struck the employee causing a fracture and dislocation to their right elbow. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees had used an excavator to pull a hydrovac unit that had high-centered. The injured employee then went under the hydrovac to disconnect the tow line. The hydrovac lurched forward and ran over the employee's leg. The employee was hospitalized with a degloving injury to skin on their thigh.

An employee was changing out hoses on rig substructure scaffolding when he stepped back and fell through an edge of the scaffolding within the rig substructure. The employee fell 18 feet to the ground in an open cellar and sustained a fractured left tibia and a compression fracture to their T12 vertebra.
An employee was rigging up a well servicing rig when a steel cable broke and struck him in the head and hard hat. He was hospitalized due to head trauma.

An employee was waiting for another employee to remove a hose from a blend tank. There was still pressure in the line and the hose came loose, spraying thioglycolic acid onto his legs. He suffered chemical burns to both of his lower legs and his right knee.

On September 4, 2024, an employee was using a poke rod to clear a jam from a floor grate that dried distillers grain (DDG) is loaded into for a conveyor. He fell backward to the floor and sustained a brain bleed, two rib fractures, and fractures to their T1 and T2 vertebrae.

Two employees were lifting a schedule 40 pipe over a cattle fence to install a natural gas line when one employee lost his footing and his finger became caught between the pipe and the fence. The employee sustained an amputation of the top of his left middle finger.
An employee was on mud pumps cleaning out the bay with a pressure washer when the tip of the washer wand came off. Diesel fluid was injected into his finger as he was replacing the wand tip.

An employee was applying thread protector covers and moving the floor wrench into a stow position so they could lay pipe down. The wrench crushed the employee's hand between the wrench housing and a pipe.
An employee was shocked while checking a breaker with a meter. The employee sustained a burn to their left middle finger.

A crew was connecting a trailer to a pickup. The crew used a forklift to lift the trailer to put it on the receiver. The injured employee's left index finger was on the ball hitch when the forklift set the trailer down, resulting in amputation at the first joint.

An employee was refueling an air compressor that had recently run out of fuel. Gasoline spilled onto the hot air compressor causing it to ignite and the employee suffered second-degree burns to the left forearm.
An employee was performing hydro excavation under a pipe rack when he slipped and fell. The water nozzle contacted his neck, resulting in a laceration.
An employee was stowing a machine when his right arm was caught between the machine and the derrick leg, resulting in a displaced radial fracture and a hairline ulnar fracture.

An employee was removing a section of fencing around a yard using a backhoe. The fence section had three rails (pipes) on each side of a center post. The far end of the rails had been torch-cut from their respective posts. Due to the tension from the backhoe, the connected portion of the pipe broke at the weld, causing the rail section to flip upward toward the back of the backhoe. One end of the pipe hit the ground at an almost straight-up angle and fell toward the seat where the employee was sitting. The end of the pipe that was torch cut edge struck the employee on top of his head on the left side, causing a contusion, a fracture, and a laceration. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was loading a portable manlift onto a truck when the lifting jack's securing bolt sheared, causing the manlift to fall. It landed on the employee's right foot and they were hospitalized with a broken foot.

An employee was working in the MCC room of the natural gas-fired gas lift compressor when an explosion occurred. It is believed that the variable frequency drive ignited the hydrates in the instrument air compressor/piping causing an explosion. The employee sustained a concussion, four broken ribs, a punctured lung and burns.

An employee was verifying that water was circulating at a well. The mud pump was placed in gear with a valve closed resulting in pressure in the hose that caused the fitting to break apart. The hose struck the employee in the face, resulting in fractures to the left side of their face.

An employee was using a 24 aluminum pipe wrench to remove a 2 reducer assembly from a 2 casing valve that included a needle valve and a small gauge. The employee was struck in the forehead with the connections when he removed the assembly due to a pressure release. The employee was hospitalized with a fracture and laceration above the left eyebrow and they required surgery.

At about 10:10 a.m. on October 9, 2024, two maintenance employees were manually relighting a flare stack pilot. Built-up vapor and gas condensation in the blower ignited, causing a fire. Both employees sustained burns and one of the employees was hospitalized with burns to the face, neck, and hands.
An employee was inserting drilling slips in a wellbore. The drill pipe separated, moved within the wellbore, and struck the employee's head. The employee suffered head trauma.
An employee fell off a fixed ladder platform through an open gate, landing about 15-16 feet below. He struck his head, suffered a knee injury, and was hospitalized.
An employee's hand was caught in a pinch point in a breakout machine. The employee suffered amputations to the middle and ring fingers.
An employee was cleaning the head of a hot roller when their glove got caught in the roller, pulling their arm into it and resulting in burns to their forearm.
Employees were doing maintenance on a pump when the pump became energized and an employee sustained a right index finger amputation.

An employee was changing out the elements in the double-rotating head. The peg that was welded to the rig floor, where the double-rotating head was being stored, broke at the weld causing the metal rotating head to fall and strike the employee's left leg and fracture it.
An employee was positioning a trailer jack head when it slid downward and crushed the employee's right index fingertip. The fingertip was amputated.

A workover rig crew was tripping tubing out of the hole. The injured employee pushed back the elevators so the operator of the rig could latch up to another stand. When the operator came down, the injured employee's right index finger was caught between the elevators and the tubing that was sitting in the slips. The employee's finger was partially amputated.
An employee was working on the bucket of a case wheel loader when the metal plate that holds the bucket up fell on their left foot. The employee sustained broken bones in their foot and toes.

An employee was setting up a crane and reconfiguring the articulating boom head. The employee manually lifted the boom to pivot and pin it into a different position when their left index finger was pinched between the crane and the sheave. The employee suffered a fractured finger that required a surgical partial amputation.

An employee was changing out a bolt on the kicker (moveable object) on the driller side of the PDS (stationary object) control box on the rig floor. The kicker came down on his right hand, catching it between the kicker and the trough. The employee sustained fractures to his thumb and index finger, as well as lacerations to the top and bottom of his hand.

On October 24, 2024, at 1:06 AM, an employee shut the hydraulic fracturing pump's engine off and removed one of the pump's engine block coolant temperature sensors. Heated engine coolant then released from behind the sensor and burned the employee's hands and forearms.

An employee drove to the project site from his hotel. Upon exiting his vehicle, and during a turning/twisting motion to grab PPE from the backseat, he heard a pop in his back. The employee was hospitalized and required surgery for fragmented L4 and L5 discs in the lumbar spine.

An employee was performing routine surveillance operation rounds on a furnace and nearby equipment. The employee heard a rumbling sound coming from a low-pressure steam vent and when he looked up, he saw water falling from the vent. He quickly moved to avoid the falling water and ran into a pipe and then fell, resulting in a right tibia fracture.

The injured employee was holding tubing while another employee used a sledgehammer to straighten out a bent tube. The roof that was being lifted fell down with the piping and crushed the injured employee's left thumb, resulting in amputation.
An employee was working on a platform when pressurized water contacted their left thigh, lacerating it just above the knee. The employee was hospitalized.

Employees were tripping pipe out of a well. The injured employee was using the power tongs to loosen the pipe connection. After flipping the cover, the injured employee's fingers were caught in a pinch point on the tongs resulting in amputations to their left middle and ring fingers.
An employee was loosening piping prior to replacing a water pump on an engine when hot antifreeze sprayed onto his left hand and right forearm, resulting in burns.

An employee was standing on an injector head feeding chain with a rope, when the rope broke, causing him to lose his balance and fall to the ground. The employee sustained fractures to his left elbow and three ribs.
An employee was bitten by a spider on the job site. The employee was hospitalized.

An employee was finished with the job and began rigging down his equipment. The lifting sub was already on top of the testing tools and the lifting device (elevators) were latched on and ready to pick up tooling to lay the tools down on the ground. The employee grabbed the lift sub to make sure it was screwed in all the way when the lifting device came up and created a pinch point that caught their left thumb. The employee sustained an amputation of the thumb tip.

An employee was climbing into a reel to operate the inside reel valve when a shift of weight caused the reel to rotate. The employee got caught between a spoke of the wheel and the wall of the trailer, resulting in a crush injury to the chest, a lacerated spleen, multiple hemorrhages and internal bleeding, a fractured rib, an anterior chest wall abrasion, and back abrasions.

Two employees were performing routine maintenance on a mud pump. The injured employee was holding a plunger cap in place when the second employee dropped the plunger cap and the injured employee's right middle fingertip was caught between the plunger cap and the pump. The employee sustained a partial amputation to the right middle fingertip.
An employee was walking past an electric fan when their shirt was caught in the fan. The employee's right arm was pulled into the fan resulting in lacerations and a fractured forearm.

An employee was tearing down a hydraulic tool when he dropped it. He went to catch it with his left hand and his middle finger became caught between his steel-toe boot and the tool, resulting in a fingertip amputation.

Three employees were breaking a threaded tool string connection using two 36-inch pipe wrenches. One of the pipe wrenches slipped and struck an employee in the abdomen, resulting in a ruptured spleen.

An employee was opening the valve of a separator tank to drain the tank when a flash fire occurred and burned the employee's hands, face, and head. The employee was wearing fire-resistant clothing at the time of the incident.

An employee was responding to a gas leak on a second-stage piping that contained natural gas. After identifying the leak, he began to walk toward his truck when the pipe ruptured, causing a fire. The employee sustained second- and third-degree burns to his ears, neck, back, and arms.

A employee was anchoring a heavy pipe into a rack when the pipe slipped. The pipe pinched his left hand and middle finger when he went to catch it, resulting in an amputation of the middle finger above the middle knuckle.

An employee was climbing up into a tractor-trailer cab when he fell backward and his head struck the edge of an adjacent flatbed trailer. The employee was found lying on the ground by a co-worker and they were hospitalized with a skull fracture.

An employee was performing maintenance on a field light for a football field. The employee was descending the light pole when the lifeline broke and he fell approximately 22 feet to the grass below. The employee sustained a fractured left arm and a punctured lung.
An employee was descending a 3-foot step ladder when he fell from the last rung to the concrete floor. The employee sustained a fractured left femur.
An employee was draining steam from a tower to clear a blockage when steam came out and caused first- and second-degree burns to his legs.

An employee was tripping pipe out of a well. After one of the joints was unlatched, the block began coming down while there was an 18-inch pipe wrench stuck underneath the brake assembly. The block slowed down but did not stop. The block and bales impacted the rig floor. The bales fell on top of the injured employee's leg and head and the employee sustained an open fracture to the lower left leg/calf.

An employee was preparing to pour concrete. A barricade for the swing radius was set up behind and to the right of the drilling rig. The employee began drilling and swung the equipment to the left to begin the spoil pile. The back of the equipment swung to the right, struck the employee, and pinned him against the fall protection cage. The employee sustained fractures to their ribs and an injury to the transverse process of a vertebra.

An employee was descending a ladder on a rig during fueling when his hand slipped, causing him to spin and fall to the ground. The employee was hospitalized with compound ankle fractures to the right tibia and fibula that required surgery.
